\[m_\alpha\in(q-1)^{\lceil\sigma|\alpha|-\mathrm{C}\rceil}\M^+\]
for every multi-index $\alpha$ then $f\in\mathrm{C}_q(\Gamma,\M) = \mathrm{C}_q(\Gamma,\overline{\mathrm{A}}) \otimes_{\overline{\mathrm{A}},p_0}^{\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\blacksquare$}}}} \M$. This is easy to see, as taking the existing criterion for $\bar{\mathrm{A}}$ and choosing a finite free surjection $\overline{\mathrm{A}}^{+\oplus n} \twoheadrightarrow \M^+$ and inverting $q-1$ proves the criterion for finite coefficients. 

Now we consider our $\M$ with a continuous semilinear $\Gamma$-action, and view it as a module $\M$ with a coaction 
\[\M \longrightarrow \mathrm{C}(\Gamma,\mathrm{A}) \otimes_{p_0,\mathrm{A}} \M\]
satisfying counit and coassociativity axioms. Here we are using the perspective introduced at the start of this section that one may think of such a module as a comodule over the Hopf algebroid $(\overline{\mathrm{A}},\mathrm{C}(\Gamma,\overline{\mathrm{A}}))$.In Lemma \ref{lem:weak_top} we explained that we can also think of this as a continuous map $\M \to \mathrm{C}(\Gamma,\M)$ where we equip $\M$ with the weak topology.

What we wish to show is that upon taking a Frobenius pullback we have $\varphi^{*k} \M \to \mathrm{C}(\Gamma,\varphi^{*k}\M)$ factoring through $\mathrm{C}_q(\Gamma,\overline{\mathrm{A}}) \otimes_{\overline{\mathrm{A}},p_0}^{\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\blacksquare$}}}} \varphi^{*k}\M$. Conceptually the remaining argument is very simple using the observation in Remark \ref{rem:la_Cq}: one observes that such $\Gamma$ modules always have a (lower) $\lambda$-analytic $\Gamma$-action for some $\lambda$, and taking Frobenius pullbacks improves the $\lambda$ until the factorization holds. 

Making this precise of course requires some more work. The notion of $\lambda$-analytic vectors is defined in \cite[Definition 2.10]{Porat_locally_analytic} but we will use the slightly different convention in \cite[Definition 4.1]{HauckLA}. In this convention we put 
\[\mathrm{C}_{\lambda-\mathrm{an}}(\Gamma,\M) = \left\{\sum_\alpha m_\alpha \binom{x}{\alpha}: \nu_{q-1}(m_\alpha)-\frac{|\alpha|}{p^\lambda(p-1)} \to \infty\right\}.\]
Smaller $\lambda$ is a stronger condition. One also has upper $\lambda$-analytic vectors, replacing $\frac{|\alpha|}{p^\lambda(p-1)}$ with $\sum \nu_p\left(\lfloor \frac{\alpha_i}{p^\lambda} \rfloor!\right)$. One can check
\[\mathrm{C}_{\lambda-\mathrm{an}}(\Gamma,\M)\subseteq \mathrm{C}^{\lambda-\mathrm{an}}(\Gamma,\M) \subseteq \mathrm{C}_{(\lambda+\varepsilon)-\mathrm{an}}(\Gamma,\M)\]
for every $\varepsilon > 0$ (see the similar argument in \cite[Lemma 4.4(2)]{PoratSolidLocallyAnalytic}.)

In this specific case the results in \cite{PoratSolidLocallyAnalytic} do not literally apply, but \cite[Remark 5.10]{PoratSolidLocallyAnalytic} actually already contains everything needed for the argument. There Porat observes that for some small $\Gamma_0 \subset \Gamma$ that $(g-1) (q-1)^i \overline{\mathrm{A}}^+ \subset (q-1)^{i+1} \overline{\mathrm{A}}^+$. Picking $\Gamma_0$ small enough to be uniform and picking a coordinate $x: \Z_p^{n+1} \to \Gamma_0$ (we remark this is not a group homomorphism in our case) specified by generators $\gamma_i$ Porat computes for $g = \prod_i \gamma_i^{x_i}$ and $x=(x_0,\ldots,x_n)$ that
\[g(a) = \sum_{\alpha \in \N^{n+1}} \binom{x}{\alpha} (\gamma_0-1)^{\alpha_0} \cdots (\gamma_n-1)^{\alpha_n}(a),\]
concluding that any element of $\overline{\mathrm{A}}$ belongs to $\mathrm{C}^{\lambda-\mathrm{an}}(\Gamma_0,\overline{\mathrm{A}})^{\Gamma_0}$ for $\lambda \gg 0$, using the fact that $(g-1)$ is $q-1$-adic filtration raising. Of course, the same argument applies with finite coefficients $\M$ equipped with their weak topology, with the elements being generators. One must be slightly careful here to run the first step of the argument as we must pick a finite $\Gamma$-stable lattice $\M^+$ over $\overline{\mathrm{A}}^+$ of $\M$, but this follows by continuity of the $\Gamma$ action for the weak topology on $\M$. Given a finite set of generators $\mathrm{S}$ for any lattice $\M^+$, we observe that by continuity $\Gamma \mathrm{S} \subset (q-1)^{-N} \M^+$ (here we also use compactness of $\Gamma$). Now we simply replace $\M^+$ by $\overline{\mathrm{A}}^+ \cdot \Gamma \mathrm{S} \subset (q-1)^{-N} \M^+$. Since continuity on $\mathrm{S}$ gives the original lattice an open stabilizer in $\Gamma$, it follows that this module is finite, and by construction it is $\Gamma$-stable. The same argument gives $(g-1) (q-1)^i \M^+ \subset (q-1)^{i+1} \M^+$.

Thus we obtain that, before even taking a Frobenius pullback, the coaction factors as
\[\M \longrightarrow \mathrm{C}^{\lambda-\mathrm{an}}(\Gamma,\M).\]
Note however that in Remark \ref{rem:la_Cq} we used lower locally analytic vectors. However up to modifying $\lambda$ we can obtain the same claim for $\mathrm{C}_{\lambda-\mathrm{an}}(\Gamma,\M)$, by the earlier inclusions. The desired result then follows by observing that a Frobenius pullback improves $\lambda$ to $\lambda-k$ in the factorization of the coaction until Remark \ref{rem:la_Cq} applies.
<!-- end proof-16 -->
<!-- proposition-2: body_md -->
Let $\M$ be a finite $\overline{\mathrm{A}}$-module with continuous semilinear $\Gamma$-action. For $k\gg0$, the module $\varphi^{*k}\M$ arises from a coherent Laurent crystal killed by $p$.
\label{prop:Gamma_to_crys}
<!-- end proposition-2 -->
<!-- proof-17: body_md -->
Choose $k$ large enough for Lemma \ref{lem:Gamma_Frob_improvement} in degrees one and two, and put $\mathrm{N}=\varphi^{*k}\M$. Lemmas \ref{lem:Cech_function_calc} and \ref{lem:Cech_finite_coefficients} give injective vertical maps in the commutative diagram

\begin{display}
\mathrm{N} \ar[shift left]{r} \ar[shift right]{r} & \mathrm{C}(\Gamma,\mathrm{N}) \ar{r} \ar[shift left=2]{r} \ar[shift right=2]{r} & \mathrm{C}(\Gamma^2,\mathrm{N}) \\
\mathrm{N} \ar[equal]{u} \ar[shift left]{r} \ar[shift right]{r} & \overline{\mathrm{A}}^{(1)}\otimes_{\overline{\mathrm{A}},p_0}^{\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\blacksquare$}}}}\mathrm{N} \ar[hook]{u} \ar{r} \ar[shift left=2]{r} \ar[shift right=2]{r} & \overline{\mathrm{A}}^{(2)}\otimes_{\overline{\mathrm{A}},p_0}^{\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\blacksquare$}}}}\mathrm{N} \ar[hook]{u}
\end{display}

We are given a full descent datum for $\mathrm{N}$ on the upper row, and want to show that it actually comes from the lower row. The coaction $m \mapsto (g\mapsto g(m))$ factors uniquely through the lower degree one term $\overline{\mathrm{A}}^{(1)}\otimes_{\overline{\mathrm{A}},p_0}^{\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\blacksquare$}}}}\mathrm{N}$ by Lemma \ref{lem:Gamma_Frob_improvement}. Note also that the diagram commutes using the description of the vertical maps from Lemma \ref{lem:Cech_function_calc}. 

The counit and coassociativity identities hold in the upper row, hence in the lower row by injectivity in degrees one and two from Lemma \ref{lem:Cech_finite_coefficients}. Thus the lower row defines a descent datum on $\mathrm{N}$ as a coherent Laurent crystal and the claim follows.
<!-- end proof-17 -->
<!-- lemma-13: body_md -->
Let $\M\subset\mathrm{N}$ be finite $\overline{\mathrm{A}}$-modules with continuous semilinear $\Gamma$-action. If $\mathrm{N}$ is the evaluation of a coherent Laurent crystal killed by $p$ and $\M$ is $\Gamma$-stable, then $\M$ also arises from a coherent Laurent crystal.
\label{lem:Cech_submodule}
<!-- end lemma-13 -->
<!-- proof-18: body_md -->
One can identify the crystal's coaction with
\[\mathrm{N}\longrightarrow \overline{\mathrm{A}}^{(1)}\otimes_{\overline{\mathrm{A}},p_0}^{\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\blacksquare$}}}}\mathrm{N} \hookrightarrow \mathrm{C}(\Gamma,\mathrm{N}).\]
We are given $\M \subset \mathrm{N}$ equipped with a (coaction) map $\M \to \mathrm{C}(\Gamma,\M)$, such that
\begin{display}
\mathrm{N} \ar{r} & \mathrm{C}(\Gamma,\mathrm{N}) \\
\M \ar[hook]{u} \ar{r} & \mathrm{C}(\Gamma,\M) \ar[hook]{u}
\end{display}
commutes. By Lemma \ref{lem:Cech_finite_coefficients} we see the coaction restricts to $\M$ giving
\[\M\longrightarrow \overline{\mathrm{A}}^{(1)}\otimes_{\overline{\mathrm{A}},p_0}^{\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\blacksquare$}}}}\M.\]
The cocycle and counit conditions follow by a similar argument.
<!-- end proof-18 -->
<!-- proof-19: body_md -->
Let $\beta:\M \hookrightarrow \varphi^*\M$ be the given map. Iterating $\beta$ embeds both $\M$ and $\varphi^*\M$ as $\Gamma$-stable submodules of $\mathrm{N}=\varphi^{*k}\M$ for every $k\geq1$, as $\varphi$ is flat on $\overline{\mathrm{A}}$.

Now choose $k$ large enough for Proposition \ref{prop:Gamma_to_crys}, and let $\mathcal{F}$ be the resulting coherent crystal with evaluation $\mathrm{N}$. Lemma \ref{lem:Cech_submodule} gives coherent subcrystals $\mathcal{E},\varphi^* \mathcal{E} \subset \mathcal{F}$ with evaluations $\M$ and $\varphi^*\M$ (full faithfulness in Proposition \ref{prop:Gamma_mod_ff} shows the second crystal is really the Frobenius pullback; nuclearity is automatic for coherent crystals). Proposition \ref{prop:Gamma_mod_ff} also lifts $\beta$ uniquely to a morphism
\[\widetilde{\beta}:\mathcal{E} \longrightarrow \varphi^* \mathcal{E}.\]
Its kernel evaluates to zero on the log $q$-de Rham prism, so $t$-exactness and conservativity from Lemma \ref{lem:qdr_laur_cech} and Corollary \ref{cor:laur_t_struct} make $\widetilde{\beta}$ injective.
<!-- end proof-19 -->
<!-- corollary-1: body_md -->
Both Proposition \ref{prop:Gamma_mod_ff} and Theorem \ref{thm:laur_root_crys} hold over $\W(k)[\zeta_{p^\ell}]$ for $\ell > 0$, by changing to $\Gamma = (1+p^\ell \Z_p) \ltimes \Z_p(1)^n$ and keeping the same base $\mathrm{A}=\R_0^{\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\square$}}}}\mathopen{(\mkern-3mu(}q-1\mathclose{)\mkern-3mu)}^{\wedge}_p$.

For $\ell=0$, again keeping the same base $\mathrm{A}=\R_0^{\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\square$}}}}\mathopen{(\mkern-3mu(}q-1\mathclose{)\mkern-3mu)}^{\wedge}_p$ but using $\Gamma = \Z_p^\times \ltimes \Z_p(1)^n$ Proposition \ref{prop:Gamma_mod_ff} holds and Theorem \ref{thm:laur_root_crys} also holds.
\label{cor:coh_laur_other_bases}
<!-- end corollary-1 -->
<!-- proof-20: body_md -->
For $\ell > 0$ the modification is straightforward, and can be done by simply setting the prismatic ideal in the $q$-de Rham prism to be $\varphi^{\ell-1}([p]_q)$. The toric factor acts by $\T_i\mapsto q^{p^\ell b_i}\T_i$, so this action is trivial modulo $\varphi^{\ell-1}([p]_q)$.

For $\ell=0$ and $p$ odd, one can evade redoing the calculations in Proposition \ref{prop:Gamma_mod_ff} in favor of a simpler calculation. We will first show that the pullback along
\[f: [\W(k)[\zeta_p]^{\mathscr{L},\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\blacksquare$}}}}/\mu_{p-1}] \xlongrightarrow{} \W(k)^{\mathscr{L},\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\blacksquare$}}}}\]
is fully faithful on $\@undefined_{\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\blacksquare$}}}}(-)$. Here the $\mu_{p-1}$ action comes from functoriality and the Galois action on $\W(k)[\zeta_p]/\W(k)$. One can use the same argument as in Proposition \ref{prop:Gamma_mod_ff} to reduce to checking if the pushforward of the structure sheaf on the source is $\ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}_{\W(k)^{\mathscr{L},\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\blacksquare$}}}}}=\ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}[1/\I_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}]_p^{\wedge}$ via the projection formula after we verify $f$ is prim (for the six functor formalism on analytic stacks). If we know this, then it is formal to deduce the claim in the general case for $[(\R_0[\zeta_p],\mathcal{M})^{\mathscr{L},\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\blacksquare$}}}}/\mu_{p-1}] \to (\R_0,\mathcal{M})^{\mathscr{L},\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\blacksquare$}}}}$: one may use base change for prim maps to deduce the required isomorphism. Verifying $f$ is prim turns out to be formal from our results so far. One can use the diagram
\begin{display}
{[\AnSpf \B/\Z_p^\times]} \ar{dd} \ar{r} & {[\AnSpf \W(k)\mathopen{(\mkern-3mu(}q-1\mathclose{)\mkern-3mu)}^{\wedge}_p/\Z_p^\times]} \ar{d}{\rho^{\Gamma}_{\W(k)\mathopen{(\mkern-3mu(}q-1\mathclose{)\mkern-3mu)}^{\wedge}_p}} \\
 & {[\W(k)[\zeta_p]^{\mathscr{L},\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\blacksquare$}}}}/\mu_{p-1}]} \ar{d}{f} \\
{\AnSpf \W(k)\mathopen{(\mkern-3mu(}\tilde{p}\mathclose{)\mkern-3mu)}^{\wedge}_p} \ar{r} & {\W(k)^{\mathscr{L},\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\blacksquare$}}}}}
\end{display}
where the outer rectangle is Cartesian (with $\tilde{p}$ as in \cite[Notation 3.8.9]{APC}). We may compute $\B$ as a prismatic envelope using Lemma \ref{lem:mixed_BK_fiber_product}; the analytic realization $(-)^{\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\blacksquare$}}}}$ of Definition \ref{def:box_analytic_realization} and passage to Laurent stacks preserve finite limits.

The upper right arrow $\rho^{\Gamma}_{\W(k)\mathopen{(\mkern-3mu(}q-1\mathclose{)\mkern-3mu)}^{\wedge}_p}$ is proper, as in the argument of Proposition \ref{prop:Gamma_mod_ff}; moreover the argument also shows $\rho^{\Gamma}_{\W(k)\mathopen{(\mkern-3mu(}q-1\mathclose{)\mkern-3mu)}^{\wedge}_p,*}\ensuremath{\mathcal{O}} \simeq \ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}$. The left vertical map $[\AnSpf \B/\Z_p^\times] \longrightarrow \AnSpf \W(k)\mathopen{(\mkern-3mu(}\tilde{p}\mathclose{)\mkern-3mu)}^{\wedge}_p$ is proper by the same argument as in Proposition \ref{prop:Gamma_mod_ff}, using Lemma \ref{lem:prismatic_product_adic_descendable} and properness of $\B \Z_p^\times$. Hence the composite of the right vertical maps is proper, since the bottom map is an effective epimorphism of analytic stacks by Proposition \ref{prop:ordinary_BK_analytic_presentation}. Now \cite[Corollary 4.7.5(ii)]{HeyerMannSixFunctors} shows that $f$ is prim, which gives the required projection formula and base change properties for the argument by \cite[Corollary 4.5.11(ii) and Lemma 4.5.13(ii)]{HeyerMannSixFunctors}.

Thus we check $\ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}_{\W(k)^{\mathscr{L},\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\blacksquare$}}}}} \simeq \R f_* \ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}_{[\W(k)[\zeta_p]^{\mathscr{L},\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\blacksquare$}}}}/\mu_{p-1}]}$. One can use the same argument as in Proposition \ref{prop:Gamma_mod_ff} to reduce to checking if the pushforward of the structure sheaf on the source is $\ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}[1/\I_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}]_p^{\wedge}$. Using Proposition \ref{prop:stack_site_compare}, we may work site-theoretically, so one may reduce to checking the stronger claim
\[\W(k)\llbracket \tilde{p} \rrbracket \xlongrightarrow{\sim} {\mathbbl{\Delta}}_{\W(k)[\zeta_p]/\W(k)\llbracket \tilde{p} \rrbracket}^{h \mu_{p-1}}.\]
Here we use conservativity of evaluation on $\W(k)\llbracket \tilde{p} \rrbracket$ to make this reduction. This can be checked directly, using the Hodge-Tate comparison. Indeed, $\mathrm{L}_{\W(k)[\zeta_p]/\W(k)} \simeq \widehat{\Omega}^1_{\W(k)[\zeta_p]/\W(k)}$ compatibly with the Galois action on $\W(k)[\zeta_p]/\W(k)$, but the target has no ordinary $\mu_{p-1}$ invariants; higher exterior powers also follow, as in this case they are just shifts of $\widehat{\Omega}^1_{\W(k)[\zeta_p]/\W(k)}$ with Breuil-Kisin twists. The $\mu_{p-1}$ invariants are exact so the desired result follows from
\[\W(k)\llbracket \tilde{p} \rrbracket = \W(k)\llbracket q-1 \rrbracket^{\mu_{p-1}}.\]

We now explain the second assertion, the proof of Theorem \ref{thm:laur_root_crys}. The \v{C}ech calculation carries over for the log prism $(\R_0^{\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\square$}}}}\llbracket \tilde{p}\rrbracket, (\tilde{p}),\mathcal{M})$ -- this prism is constructed analogously to the log $q$-de Rham prism via a framing, but we note that one must be cautious as it does not possess a full $\Gamma$ action. Its first \v{C}ech term is
\[(\R_0^{\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\square$}}}}\llbracket \tilde{p}\rrbracket)^{(1)} \simeq \R_0^{\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\square$}}}}\llbracket \tilde{p}_0,\tilde{p}_1\rrbracket[u_1^{\pm1},\ldots,u_n^{\pm1}] \left\{ \frac{\tilde{p}_1}{\tilde{p}_0}, \frac{u_1-1}{\tilde{p}_0}, \ldots, \frac{u_n-1}{\tilde{p}_0} \right\}_{\delta,(p,\tilde{p}_0)}^{\wedge},\]
where $u_i=\T_{i,1}/\T_{i,0}$ and $\delta(u_i)=0$.
As we work modulo $p$ always, what is really needed is an analogue of Lemma \ref{lem:Cq_criterion}. This doesn't seem to quite work, but we can use the following trick. By a similar argument we may deduce
\[\left((\R_0^{\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\square$}}}}\llbracket \tilde{p}\rrbracket)^{(1)} \otimes_{\R_0^{\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\square$}}}}\llbracket \tilde{p}\rrbracket} \R_0^{\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\square$}}}}\llbracket q-1\rrbracket\right)/p \simeq \left(\bigoplus_{\alpha \in\N^{n+1}} (\R_0^{\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\square$}}}}/p)\llbracket q-1 \rrbracket \tilde{p}^{\alpha_0}(q-1)^{|(\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_n)|}\binom{x}{\alpha}\right)^{\wedge}_{(q-1)}.\]
Indeed for the toric directions we can repeat verbatim the same argument as already appearing in Lemma \ref{lem:Cech_function_calc} for $\eta_{i,m}$ when $i>0$, which then works identically through the method of Lemma \ref{lem:Cq_criterion}. For the remaining part one similarly observes that
\[\W(k)\llbracket \tilde{p}_0, \tilde{p}_1 \rrbracket\{\tilde{p}_1/\tilde{p}_0\}^{\wedge}_{\delta,(p,\tilde{p}_0)}/p \simeq \left(\bigoplus_{\alpha_0\in \N} k\llbracket \tilde{p}_0 \rrbracket \tilde{p}^{\alpha_0} \binom{x_0}{\alpha_0}\right)^{\wedge}_{\tilde{p}_0} \subset \mathrm{C}(1+p\Z_p, k\llbracket \tilde{p}_0\rrbracket).\]
Combining these gives the claimed identification, noting that we need base extension primarily to deal with the toric part (otherwise $q-1$ is not an element of the ring, so the identification makes no sense).

This identification shows that a single Frobenius pullback makes 
\[\mathcal{E}\in \Coh((\R_0 \otimes_{\W(k)} \W(k)[\zeta_p],\mathcal{M})_{\mathbbl{\Delta}},\ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}[1/\I_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}]_p^{\wedge})_{p=0}^{h\mu_{p-1}}\]  
descend to $\Coh((\R_0,\mathcal{M})_{\mathbbl{\Delta}},\ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}[1/\I_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}]_p^{\wedge})$. Indeed comparing the previous identification to $(\R_0^{\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\square$}}}}\llbracket q-1\rrbracket)^{(1)}/p$ shows a single Frobenius pullback lands the coaction of a Laurent crystal in the Laurentization of $\left((\R_0^{\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\square$}}}}\llbracket \tilde{p}\rrbracket)^{(1)} \otimes_{\R_0^{\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\square$}}}}\llbracket \tilde{p}\rrbracket} \R_0^{\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\square$}}}}\llbracket q-1\rrbracket\right)/p$. But then taking $\mu_{p-1}$ invariants further lands the coaction in $(\R_0^{\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\square$}}}}\llbracket \tilde{p}\rrbracket)^{(1)}/p [1/\tilde{p}]$ as desired, giving the crystal.

Thus it follows that given such a $\Z_p^\times \ltimes \Z_p(1)^n$-module over $\mathrm{A}$ some high Frobenius pullback comes from a crystal. To finish the argument, we note that the description of $\left((\R_0^{\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\square$}}}}\llbracket \tilde{p}\rrbracket)^{(1)} \otimes_{\R_0^{\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\square$}}}}\llbracket \tilde{p}\rrbracket} \R_0^{\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\square$}}}}\llbracket q-1\rrbracket\right)/p$ yields the corresponding claim in Lemma \ref{lem:Cech_finite_coefficients} as the required points (e.g. flatness of the maps in the \v{C}ech nerve) again hold. Note that we also get the description for the second term of the \v{C}ech nerve, since this is $(\R_0^{\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\square$}}}}\llbracket \tilde{p}\rrbracket)^{(1)} \widehat{\otimes}_{\R_0^{\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\square$}}}}\llbracket \tilde{p}\rrbracket} (\R_0^{\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\square$}}}}\llbracket \tilde{p}\rrbracket)^{(1)}$. Thus we obtain the analogue of Lemma \ref{lem:Cech_submodule}, and can conclude Theorem \ref{thm:laur_root_crys} in the same way.
<!-- end proof-20 -->
<!-- definition-4: body_md -->
Let $(\mathrm{A}^+,\I)$ be an orientable prism with $\I=(d)$. Equip $\mathrm{A}=\mathrm{A}^+[1/d]_p^{\wedge}$ with $\@undefined_{\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\blacksquare$}}}}(\mathrm{A})$ as defined in \ref{def:laur_category}. Note $\mathrm{A}$ has a natural Frobenius $\varphi$ induced by the Frobenius on $\mathrm{A}^+$ (since $\varphi(d)\equiv d^p \pmod{p}$).

Write $\mathrm{A}\langle \mathrm{F}\rangle$ for
\[\widehat{\bigoplus}_{i\ge 0} \mathrm{A} \mathrm{F}^i,\]
where $\mathrm{F} x = \varphi(x) \mathrm{F}$. We put $\@undefined_{\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\blacksquare$}}}}(\mathrm{A}\langle \mathrm{F}\rangle)$ for $p$-complete solid modules over this noncommutative analytic ring, with the analytic ring structure induced from $\mathrm{A}$.

For $\M\in\@undefined_{\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\blacksquare$}}}}(\mathrm{A}\langle \mathrm{F}\rangle)$, we say $\M$ is \textit{unit} if
\[\varphi_{\mathrm{A}}^*\M:=\mathrm{A}\otimes^{\mathrm{L},\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\blacksquare$}}}}_{\mathrm{A},\varphi_{\mathrm{A}}}\M\longrightarrow\M\]
given by $a\otimes m\mapsto a\mathrm{F}_\M(m)$ is an equivalence. A unit object is \textit{finitely generated unit} if it is perfect over $\mathrm{A}\langle \mathrm{F}\rangle$; these objects form the full subcategory $\@undefined_{\fgu}(\mathrm{A})$. Here, we mean perfect in the sense that it lies in the thick subcategory generated by $\mathrm{A}\langle \mathrm{F}\rangle$ as we work over a noncommutative base.
\label{def:module_fgu}
<!-- end definition-4 -->
<!-- lemma-14: body_md -->
Let $(\mathrm{A}^+,(d))$ be an orientable prism, and let $\mathrm{A}=\mathrm{A}^+[1/d]_p^{\wedge}$ with $\@undefined_{\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\blacksquare$}}}}(\mathrm{A})$ as in Definition \ref{def:laur_category}. Then 
\[\mathrm{Thick}_{\mathrm{A}\langle \mathrm{F} \rangle} \@undefined(\mathrm{A}\langle \mathrm{F} \rangle) \simeq \mathrm{Thick}_{\mathrm{A}\langle \mathrm{F} \rangle} \@undefined_{\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\blacksquare$}}}}(\mathrm{A}\langle \mathrm{F} \rangle)\] 
with inverse given by $\M \mapsto \M(*)$. 

The solid modules in the target thick subcategory are all $p$-completely nuclear.
\label{lem:solid_Frob_perf_comparison}
<!-- end lemma-14 -->
<!-- proof-21: body_md -->
The comparison is exact and carries $\mathrm{A}\langle \mathrm{F} \rangle$ to the corresponding solid module. To show the equivalence it therefore suffices to compute $\RHom_{\@undefined_{\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\blacksquare$}}}}(\mathrm{A}\langle \mathrm{F}\rangle)}\bigl(\mathrm{A}\langle \mathrm{F}\rangle,\mathrm{A}\langle \mathrm{F} \rangle\bigr)$ and similarly on the module side and check that they are identified. 

We can compute
\[\RHom_{\@undefined_{\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\blacksquare$}}}}(\mathrm{A}\langle \mathrm{F}\rangle)}\bigl(\mathrm{A}\langle \mathrm{F}\rangle,\mathrm{A}\langle \mathrm{F} \rangle\bigr)\simeq \RHom_{\@undefined_{\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\blacksquare$}}}}(\mathrm{A})}\bigl(\mathrm{A},\mathrm{A} \langle \mathrm{F} \rangle\bigr) \simeq \mathrm{A} \langle \mathrm{F} \rangle.\]
To justify this, by derived $p$-completeness it suffices to check equivalences modulo $p^n$, which makes the argument slightly easier as then $\mathrm{A}\langle \mathrm{F} \rangle \mathord{/\mkern-6mu/} p^n = (\mathrm{A} \mathord{/\mkern-6mu/} p^n)[\mathrm{F}]$. The first equivalence uses the free/forgetful adjunction, and the second equivalence is then clear. This then matches the corresponding calculation in ordinary modules, so it follows $\mathrm{Thick}_{\mathrm{A}\langle \mathrm{F} \rangle} \@undefined(\mathrm{A}\langle \mathrm{F} \rangle) \simeq \mathrm{Thick}_{\mathrm{A}\langle \mathrm{F} \rangle} \@undefined_{\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\blacksquare$}}}}(\mathrm{A}\langle \mathrm{F} \rangle)$. 

Now we address the nuclearity claim. The unit $\mathrm{A}^+$ of $\@undefined_{\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\blacksquare$}}}}(\Spa(\mathrm{A}^+,\mathrm{A}^+))$ is nuclear. Since $\mathrm{A}$ is the filtered colimit of multiplication by $d$ in derived $p$-complete solid modules, it is $p$-completely nuclear. The $p$-completely nuclear objects are closed under colimits, so $\mathrm{A}\langle \mathrm{F}\rangle=\widehat{\bigoplus}_{i\geq0}\mathrm{A} \mathrm{F}^i$ is $p$-completely nuclear. Nuclearity is preserved under the operators cutting out a thick subcategory, for example retracts or finite limits.
<!-- end proof-21 -->
<!-- definition-5: body_md -->
Let $(\X,\mathcal{M})$ be a bounded fs log $p$-adic formal scheme. A crystal
\[\mathcal{E}\in \@undefined_{\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\blacksquare$}}}}((\X,\mathcal{M})_{\mathbbl{\Delta}},\ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}[1/\I_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}]_p^{\wedge})^{\varphi=1}\]
is finitely generated unit if for every object $(\mathrm{A},\I,\M_{\Spf \mathrm{A}})^a$ of $(\X,\mathcal{M})_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}$, its evaluation belongs to $\@undefined_{\fgu}(\mathrm{A}[1/\I]^{\wedge}_p)$ in the sense of Definition \ref{def:module_fgu}.

\vskip1em

We write $\@undefined_{\fgu}((\X,\mathcal{M})_{\mathbbl{\Delta}},\ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}[1/\I_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}]_p^{\wedge})$ for the full subcategory of finitely generated unit crystals, and $\Mod_{\fgu}((\X,\mathcal{M})_{\mathbbl{\Delta}},\ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}[1/\I_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}]_p^{\wedge})$ for its intersection with the heart of $\@undefined_{\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\blacksquare$}}}}((\X,\mathcal{M})_{\mathbbl{\Delta}},\ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}[1/\I_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}]_p^{\wedge})$.
\label{def:fgu}
<!-- end definition-5 -->
<!-- remark-4: body_md -->
Let $\B$ be a $p$-adically complete associative ring (in which $p$ is central), and let $\M$ be a derived $p$-complete left $\B$-module. Then
\[\M\in\Perf(\B) \Longleftrightarrow (\B/p)\otimes^{\mathrm{L}}_{\B}\M\in\Perf(\B/p).\]
This can be seen by using \cite[Lemma 15.99.4, Tag \href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09AW}{09AW}]{StacksProject} for $\{(\B/p^n)\otimes^{\mathrm{L}}_{\B}\M\}_{n\geq1}$. Passing through Lemma \ref{lem:solid_Frob_perf_comparison} we can run the same argument in the solid setting for $\mathrm{A}\langle \mathrm{F} \rangle$, thus detecting the finitely generated unit condition modulo $p$.
\label{rem:fgu_mod_p}
<!-- end remark-4 -->
<!-- definition-6: body_md -->
Let $\mathrm{A}$ be as in \ref{def:module_fgu}, and assume that $\mathrm{A}$ is Noetherian regular. If $\M$ is a unit Frobenius module over $\mathrm{A}$, a \textit{root} of $\M$ is a coherent $\mathrm{A}$-submodule $\M_0\subset \M$ together with an injective map $\beta:\M_0\to\varphi_{\mathrm{A}}^*\M_0$ whose iterates identify
\[\M\simeq \colim_n \varphi_{\mathrm{A}}^{*n}\M_0.\]
It is \textit{minimal} if it has no proper subroot. A distinguished minimal root is a minimal root contained in every other root of $\M$ as a submodule of the same ambient unit module.

One can make the analogous definitions in $\QCoh_{\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\blacksquare$}}}}((\X,\mathcal{M})_{\mathbbl{\Delta}},\ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}[1/\I_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}]_p^{\wedge})^{\varphi=1}$. When referring to a root of a module we mean the former, and when referring to a root of a crystal we mean the latter.
\label{def:roots}
<!-- end definition-6 -->
<!-- lemma-15: body_md -->
For $\mathrm{A} = \R_0^{\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\square$}}}}\mathopen{(\mkern-3mu(}q-1\mathclose{)\mkern-3mu)}^{\wedge}_p$, a unit $\mathrm{A}\langle \mathrm{F} \rangle$-complex $\M$ is perfect over $\mathrm{A}\langle \mathrm{F} \rangle$ if and only if $\M$ is $t$-bounded and each $\mathrm{H}^i(\M)$ is finitely generated as a left $\mathrm{A}\langle \mathrm{F} \rangle$-module.
\label{lem:fgu_actually_fgu}
<!-- end lemma-15 -->
<!-- proof-22: body_md -->
Supposing $\M$ is perfect over $\mathrm{A}\langle \mathrm{F} \rangle$, then so is $\M \mathord{/\mkern-6mu/} p$. Then \cite[Proposition 11.3.9]{BhattLurieModpRH} shows all $\mathrm{H}^i(\M \mathord{/\mkern-6mu/} p)$ are finitely generated over $\bar{\mathrm{A}}[\mathrm{F}]$. Now
\[\mathrm{H}^i(\M)/p \hookrightarrow \mathrm{H}^i(\M \mathord{/\mkern-6mu/} p)\]
is a unit submodule, hence finitely generated. Then lifting generators to get a map $\mathrm{A}\langle \mathrm{F} \rangle^{\oplus n} \twoheadrightarrow \mathrm{H}^i(\M)$ and applying derived Nakayama to the derived $p$-complete cokernel for surjectivity shows $\mathrm{H}^i(\M)$ is finitely generated.

Conversely, suppose all $\mathrm{H}^i(\M)$ are finitely generated over $\mathrm{A}\langle \mathrm{F} \rangle$. Then $\mathrm{H}^i(\M)/p$ is as well, so to conclude we only need to show $\mathrm{H}^{i+1}(\M)[p]$ is as well, using the exact sequences
\begin{display}
0 \ar{r} & \mathrm{H}^i(\M)/p \ar{r} & \mathrm{H}^i(\M \mathord{/\mkern-6mu/} p) \ar{r} & \mathrm{H}^{i+1}(\M)[p] \ar{r} & 0.
\end{display}
Indeed \cite[Proposition 11.3.9]{BhattLurieModpRH} then shows $\M \mathord{/\mkern-6mu/} p$ is finitely generated unit, and we already know from Remark \ref{rem:fgu_mod_p} that it can be detected modulo $p$.

Thus we reduce to proving the assertion that if $\M$ is a finitely generated unit left module over $\mathrm{A}\langle \mathrm{F} \rangle$ that $\M[p]$ is too. For a finitely generated unit module, $\M[p^\infty]=\M[p^\ell]$ for some $\ell$. Indeed upon considering 
\[\mathrm{im}(\M[p^k] \longrightarrow (\M/p\M))\]
we must get a stabilizing ascending chain of finitely generated unit submodules (by root considerations and Noetherianity of $\overline{\mathrm{A}}$). Once the chain stabilizes at $\ell$ we obtain that $p^\ell \M[p^\infty]$ is $p$-divisible; if nonzero we would have a nonzero map $\Q_p \to \M$ so derived $p$-completeness forces $\M[p^\infty]=\M[p^\ell]$. We then consider the finite filtration $\M[p] \cap p^i \M$ for $i\le \ell$. The graded pieces are unit subquotients of $\M/p\M$, hence finitely generated unit. Since the filtration is finite the desired claim follows.
<!-- end proof-22 -->
<!-- theorem-5: body_md -->
Let $(\Spf \R,\mathcal{M})$ be a framed log affine in the sense of Definition \ref{def:fr_log_aff} and put $\mathrm{A}=\R_0^{\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\square$}}}}\mathopen{(\mkern-3mu(}q-1\mathclose{)\mkern-3mu)}^{\wedge}_p$. Evaluation on the log $q$-de Rham prism $(\R_0^{\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\square$}}}}\llbracket q-1\rrbracket,[p]_q,\mathcal{M})^a$ induces an equivalence
\[\rho_{\mathrm{A}}^{\Gamma,*}:\@undefined_{\fgu}((\Spf \R,\mathcal{M})_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}, \ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}[1/\I_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}]_p^{\wedge}) \xlongrightarrow{\sim} \@undefined_{\fgu}(\mathrm{A})^{h\Gamma}.\]
\label{thm:qdR_crys_Gamma_mod}
<!-- end theorem-5 -->
<!-- proof-23: body_md -->
First, we note that the functor is fully faithful. This follows from Proposition \ref{prop:Gamma_mod_ff}, but for the solid version of the target given by 
\[\@undefined_{\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\blacksquare$}}}}(\mathrm{A})^{h\Gamma, \varphi=1} = \lim_{[s]\in \Delta} \@undefined_{\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\blacksquare$}}}}(\mathrm{C}(\Gamma^s,\mathrm{A}))^{\varphi=1}.\]
The essential image, by definition of $\@undefined_{\fgu}((\Spf \R,\mathcal{M})_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}, \ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}[1/\I_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}]_p^{\wedge})$, satisfies the property that evaluation on the log prism $\mathrm{C}(\Gamma^s,\mathrm{A}^+)$ we get a unit Frobenius module in the category $\mathrm{Thick}_{\mathrm{C}(\Gamma^s,\mathrm{A}\langle \mathrm{F} \rangle)} \@undefined(\mathrm{C}(\Gamma^s,\mathrm{A}\langle \mathrm{F} \rangle))$. By Lemma \ref{lem:solid_Frob_perf_comparison}, it follows that equivalently the functor lands in $\@undefined_{\fgu}(\mathrm{A})^{h\Gamma}$, by which we mean unit objects in
\[\lim_{[s]\in \Delta} \mathrm{Thick}_{\mathrm{C}(\Gamma^s,\mathrm{A}\langle \mathrm{F} \rangle)} \@undefined(\mathrm{C}(\Gamma^s,\mathrm{A}\langle \mathrm{F} \rangle)).\]

Thus we obtain the desired fully faithful functor
\[\rho_{\mathrm{A}}^{\Gamma,*}:\@undefined_{\fgu}((\Spf \R,\mathcal{M})_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}, \ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}[1/\I_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}]_p^{\wedge}) \longrightarrow \@undefined_{\fgu}(\mathrm{A})^{h\Gamma}.\]
Now we turn to essential surjectivity. We first prove essential surjectivity onto the heart of the target modulo $p$. Put $\overline{\mathrm{A}}=\mathrm{A}/p$, and let $\mathrm{M}$ be a finitely generated unit $\overline{\mathrm{A}}$-module with continuous semilinear $\Gamma$-action.

Since $\overline{\mathrm{A}}$ is regular and $\mathrm{F}$-finite, \cite[Corollary 2.26]{BlickleGamma} gives a distinguished minimal root
\[\beta:\mathrm{M}_{\min}\hookrightarrow\varphi^*\mathrm{M}_{\min}.\]
Every $\Gamma$-translate is again a root. Since it is a distinguished minimal root, it becomes $\Gamma$-equivariant and Theorem \ref{thm:laur_root_crys} lifts it to a coherent Laurent crystal $\mathcal{E}_0$. Its unitalization $\mathcal{E}$ is necessarily finitely generated unit\footnote{\label{fn:root_unitalization_fgu}If $\B=\B^+[1/\I]_p^{\wedge}$ for a log prism $(\B^+,\I, \M_{\Spf \B^+})^a$, let $\M_0,\M$ be the evaluations of $\mathcal{E}_0,\mathcal{E}$. We have
\[\M\simeq\bigl[\B \langle \mathrm{F} \rangle \otimes_{\B}^{\mathrm{L},\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\blacksquare$}}}}\M_0\xlongrightarrow{1-\widetilde\beta}\B \langle \mathrm{F} \rangle \otimes_{\B}^{\mathrm{L},\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\blacksquare$}}}}\M_0\bigr]\]
where $\widetilde\beta$ is induced by $\beta:\M_0\to\varphi^*\M_0$, showing $\mathcal{E}$ is finitely generated unit.}, and satisfies $\rho_{\mathrm{A}}^*\mathcal{E}\simeq\mathrm{M}$, giving the desired preimage for objects in the heart of the target $\@undefined_{\fgu}(\mathrm{A})^{h\Gamma}$ modulo $p$. 

This suffices to prove essential surjectivity. Since evaluation on the log prism $\mathrm{A}^+$ is exact, in particular compatible with shifts and fibers, a Postnikov d\'{e}vissage (see \cite[Lemma 5.4.3]{HauckStacky}) on the target upgrades essential surjectivity on the heart modulo $p$ to essential surjectivity on the derived categories. Thus evaluation is an equivalence modulo $p$. Lemma \ref{lem:categorical_nakayama} now gives the claim.
<!-- end proof-23 -->
<!-- remark-5: body_md -->
On the heart one may again work classically, instead asking that the $\Gamma$ action is continuous for the weak topology when viewed as a finitely generated unit $\mathrm{A}\langle \mathrm{F} \rangle$-module. We will not need this, so we omit the argument (it can be done with a similar strategy to Lemma \ref{lem:weak_top}). In later arguments we will only need the easy direction, namely that from the cobar construction one obtains an action continuous for the weak topology or $\M \to \mathrm{C}(\Gamma,\mathrm{A}\langle \mathrm{F} \rangle) \otimes_{\mathrm{A}\langle \mathrm{F} \rangle, p_0} \M \to \mathrm{C}(\Gamma,\M)$ is continuous. The first map as expained in Lemma \ref{lem:weak_top} is automatically continuous, and for the second to deduce just continuity we do not need $\mathrm{K}$ to have the subspace topology (or to even use it at all).
\label{rem:weak_top_fgu}
<!-- end remark-5 -->
<!-- lemma-16: body_md -->
In Theorem \ref{thm:qdR_crys_Gamma_mod}, the $t$-structure on solid Laurent crystals restricts to the source $\@undefined_{\fgu}((\Spf \R,\mathcal{M})_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}, \ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}[1/\I_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}]_p^{\wedge})$ and $\rho_{\mathrm{A}}^{\Gamma,*}$ is $t$-exact.
\label{lem:fgu_local_tstruct}
<!-- end lemma-16 -->
<!-- proof-24: body_md -->
We note that in this proof of essential surjectivity in Theorem \ref{thm:qdR_crys_Gamma_mod} implicitly the preimages constructed are all in the heart of $\@undefined_{\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\blacksquare$}}}}((\Spf \R,\mathcal{M})_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}, \ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}[1/\I_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}]_p^{\wedge})$. Indeed mod $p$ the preimage is a unitalization of a coherent root, and coherent crystals are in the heart of the solid $t$-structure by Corollary \ref{cor:laur_t_struct}. The analogous procedure, instead run for exact sequences in the heart of $\@undefined_{\fgu}(\mathrm{A})^{h\Gamma}$ to iteratively write heart objects as extensions of $p^\ell$-torsion objects (and taking a limit), constructs preimages in the heart by full faithfulness.

The desired claim is completely formal using the inverse equivalence in Theorem \ref{thm:qdR_crys_Gamma_mod}. Indeed, we have seen the inverse gives a $t$-exact functor
\[\@undefined_{\fgu}(\mathrm{A})^{h\Gamma} \longrightarrow \@undefined_{\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\blacksquare$}}}}((\Spf \R,\mathcal{M})_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}, \ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}[1/\I_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}]_p^{\wedge})^{\varphi=1}\]
since the preimages constructed lie in the heart. But then for any finitely generated unit Laurent crystal $\mathcal{E}$ in the essential image of this functor this implies its cohomology sheaves $\mathrm{H}^i(\mathcal{E})$ are also finitely generated unit, so the $t$-structure restricts to the essental image of $\@undefined_{\fgu}((\Spf \R,\mathcal{M})_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}, \ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}[1/\I_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}]_p^{\wedge})$. This argument also shows $\rho_{\mathrm{A}}^{\Gamma,*}$ is $t$-exact.
<!-- end proof-24 -->
<!-- proposition-3: body_md -->
Let $(\Spf \R,\mathcal{M})$ be a framed log affine. A crystal 
\[\mathcal{E}\in \@undefined_{\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\blacksquare$}}}}((\Spf \R,\mathcal{M})_{\mathbbl{\Delta}},\ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}[1/\I_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}]_p^{\wedge})^{\varphi=1}\] 
is finitely generated unit if and only if it is $t$-bounded and each crystal $\mathrm{H}^i(\mathcal{E}\mathord{/\mkern-6mu/} p)$ admits a distinguished minimal root in $\Coh((\Spf \R,\mathcal{M})_{\mathbbl{\Delta}},\ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}[1/\I_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}]_p^{\wedge})_{p=0}$.
\label{prop:root_crys_minimal}
<!-- end proposition-3 -->
<!-- proof-25: body_md -->
Combining Theorem \ref{thm:qdR_crys_Gamma_mod}, Lemma \ref{lem:fgu_actually_fgu} and Remark \ref{rem:fgu_mod_p} to work modulo $p$, we see that each $\mathrm{H}^i(\mathcal{E}\mathord{/\mkern-6mu/} p)$ admitting a distinguished minimal root in $\Coh((\Spf \R,\mathcal{M})_{\mathbbl{\Delta}},\ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}[1/\I_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}]_p^{\wedge})_{p=0}$ is sufficient. Indeed we see the unitalization of a coherent crystal root is a finitely generated unit Laurent crystal, by the same argument as in the footnote \ref{fn:root_unitalization_fgu}.

Conversely, take a finitely generated unit Laurent crystal. Reducing modulo $p$ using Theorem \ref{thm:qdR_crys_Gamma_mod} and Lemma \ref{lem:fgu_actually_fgu} we reduce to the case where $\mathcal{E}$ corresponds to $\M \in \Mod_{\fgu}(\mathrm{A})_{p=0}^{h\Gamma}$. Here we also implicitly use Lemma \ref{lem:fgu_local_tstruct}. By the previous argument in Theorem \ref{thm:qdR_crys_Gamma_mod}, by \cite[Corollary 2.26]{BlickleGamma} there is a distinguished $\Gamma$-equivariant minimal root $\M_0$ of $\M$. Using Theorem \ref{thm:laur_root_crys} this root arises from a crystal $\mathcal{E}_0$. Together with Proposition \ref{prop:Gamma_mod_ff}, this theorem identifies roots as Laurent crystals with $\Gamma$-equivariant roots of $\M$. Since $\M_0$ has the stronger property of being a distinguished minimal root, the claim follows.
<!-- end proof-25 -->
<!-- lemma-17: body_md -->
\label{lem:completion-minimal}
Let $\mathrm{A}$ be a regular local $\mathrm{F}$-finite $\F_p$-algebra with completion $\widehat{\mathrm{A}}$, and let $\mathrm{N}_0\subset \mathrm{N}$ be a root of a finitely generated unit $\mathrm{A}[\mathrm{F}]$-module. Then $\mathrm{N}_0$ is minimal if and only if $\widehat{\mathrm{A}}\otimes_\mathrm{A} \mathrm{N}_0 \subset \widehat{\mathrm{A}}\otimes_\mathrm{A} \mathrm{N}$ is minimal.
<!-- end lemma-17 -->
<!-- proof-26: body_md -->
The forward implication is \cite[Corollary 2.11]{BlickleIH}. Conversely, assume the completed root is minimal and let $\mathrm{N}_1\subset \mathrm{N}_0$ be a subroot. Its completion is a subroot, hence $\widehat{\mathrm{A}}\otimes_\mathrm{A} \mathrm{N}_1=\widehat{\mathrm{A}}\otimes_\mathrm{A} \mathrm{N}_0$.

Since $\mathrm{A}\to\widehat{\mathrm{A}}$ is faithfully flat, it follows that $\mathrm{N}_1=\mathrm{N}_0$. Thus $\mathrm{N}_0$ has no proper subroot, hence is minimal.
<!-- end proof-26 -->
<!-- lemma-18: body_md -->
\label{lem:completed-localization-minimal}
Let $\Spa \B \to \Spa \mathrm{A}$ be an \'{e}tale morphism of regular affinoids over $k\mathopen{(\mkern-3mu(}q-1\mathclose{)\mkern-3mu)}$. Then pullback along this map sends minimal roots of finitely generated unit modules to minimal roots.
<!-- end lemma-18 -->
<!-- proof-27: body_md -->
We first note that $\mathrm{A}$ and $\B$ are both regular $\mathrm{F}$-finite, so all of the hypotheses of \cite{BlickleGamma} are satisfied. For testing minimality, the results in \cite{BlickleGamma} give us several useful tools. Let us suppose that $\M$ is a finitely generated unit module over say $\mathrm{A}$, with root $\beta: \M_0 \to \varphi^* \M_0$.

Following \cite[\S2.4]{BlickleGamma}, Blickle constructs $\sigma^{-1}_{\beta}(\M_0)\subset\M_0$ which can be characterized as the smallest submodule $\M_0'$ such that $\beta(\M_0)\subset \varphi_{\mathrm{A}}^* \M_0'$. By \cite[Lemma 2.16]{BlickleGamma} this construction commutes with localization, and a root is minimal in our sense precisely when $\sigma^{-1}_{\beta}(\M_0)=\M_0$.

This construction is given by an explicit formula, which we now explain. We let $\@undefined_{\mathrm{A}}^{(1)} = \End_{\mathrm{A}}(\mathrm{A}^{(1)})$ be the algebra of right $\mathrm{A}$-linear endomorphisms of the Frobenius twist $\mathrm{A}^{(1)}$. Blickle gives a Frobenius descent functor
\[\sigma^{-1}: \Mod_{\@undefined_{\mathrm{A}}^{(1)}} \longrightarrow \Mod_{\mathrm{A}}\]
as the inverse to $\mathrm{A}^{(1)} \otimes_{\mathrm{A}} -$ (which is an equivalence since $\mathrm{A}^{(1)}$ is finite locally free over $\mathrm{A}$). We may compute $\sigma^{-1}_\beta(\M_0)$ as $\sigma^{-1}(\@undefined_{\mathrm{A}}^{(1)}\cdot \beta(\M_0)) \subseteq \sigma^{-1} \sigma^\ast \M_0 = \M_0$.

Now we prove the claim. By localization compatibility, a root $\M_0$ over $\mathrm{A}$ is minimal if and only if its localization at every maximal ideal is again minimal. We use here that $\sigma_{\beta}^{-1}(\M_0)=\M_0$ is an open condition, see \cite[Proposition 2.17]{BlickleGamma}. The same then also holds for $\B$. Together with Lemma \ref{lem:completion-minimal}, this shows that minimality may be checked on the \textit{completed} local rings at the classical points of the rigid spaces.

Fix a maximal ideal $\mathfrak{m}\subset\B$, let $x\in\Spa(\B)$ be the corresponding rigid point, and put $\mathfrak{n}=\mathfrak{m}\cap\mathrm{A}$. The morphism $\Spa \B \to \Spa \mathrm{A}$ factors near $x$ into affinoid open immersions and a finite \'{e}tale morphism. Since affinoid open immersions induce isomorphisms on completed local rings by \cite[7.3.2/3]{BoschGuntzerRemmert}, the map
\[\widehat{\mathrm{A}}_{\mathfrak{n}} \longrightarrow \widehat{\B}_{\mathfrak{m}}\]
is finite \'{e}tale as an ordinary map of rings. Both rings are again regular and $\mathrm{F}$-finite. It therefore remains to show that finite \'{e}tale pullbacks preserve minimal roots.

Now we reduce to this situation, and can just assume the ring map $\mathrm{A} \to \B$ is finite \'{e}tale. We would be done if we just showed the identity
\[\sigma^{-1}_{\beta_{\B}} (\B \otimes_{\mathrm{A}} \M_0) = \B \otimes_{\mathrm{A}} \sigma^{-1}_{\beta}(\M_0),\]
as using minimality the right side simplifies to $\B \otimes_{\mathrm{A}} \M_0$, meaning $\B \otimes_{\mathrm{A}} \M_0$ is minimal. Using the explicit formula, 
\[\sigma^{-1}_{\beta_{\B}} (\B \otimes_{\mathrm{A}} \M_0) =  \sigma^{-1}(\@undefined_{\B}^{(1)} \beta(\B\otimes_{\mathrm{A}}\M_0)).\]
Now substitute $\B\otimes_{\mathrm{A}}\@undefined_{\mathrm{A}}^{(1)}\simeq\@undefined_{\B}^{(1)}$. This follows here since the relative Frobenius is an isomorphism, so $\B \otimes_{\mathrm{A}} \mathrm{A}^{(1)} \simeq \B^{(1)}$, and taking $\End$ gives the claim.

Applying this substitution yields 
\[\sigma^{-1}_{\beta_{\B}} (\B \otimes_{\mathrm{A}} \M_0) = \sigma^{-1}(\B\otimes_{\mathrm{A}}\@undefined_{\mathrm{A}}^{(1)} \cdot \beta(\B\otimes_{\mathrm{A}}\M_0)) = \sigma^{-1}(\@undefined_{\mathrm{A}}^{(1)} \cdot \beta(\M_0)) \otimes_{\mathrm{A}} \B.\]  
In the last step we have used that $\sigma^{-1}$ commutes with \'{e}tale base change, which again can be seen from $\B\otimes_{\mathrm{A}}\@undefined_{\mathrm{A}}^{(1)}\simeq\@undefined_{\B}^{(1)}$. Recalling the definition of $\sigma^{-1}_{\beta}(\M_0)$ we have proved $\sigma^{-1}_{\beta_{\B}} (\B \otimes_{\mathrm{A}} \M_0) = \B \otimes_{\mathrm{A}} \sigma^{-1}_{\beta}(\M_0)$ as desired.
<!-- end proof-27 -->
<!-- corollary-2: body_md -->
Let $f:(\Spf \mathrm{S},\mathcal{M}_{\Spf \mathrm{S}})\to(\Spf \R,\mathcal{M}_{\Spf \R})$ be a strict \'{e}tale map where the target is a framed log affine. If $\mathcal{E}\in \@undefined_{\fgu}((\Spf \R,\mathcal{M}_{\Spf \R})_{\mathbbl{\Delta}},\ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}[1/\I_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}]_p^{\wedge})_{p=0}$ with distinguished minimal root $\mathcal{E}_{0}$, then $f^*\mathcal{E}$ is finitely generated unit and $f^*\mathcal{E}_{0}$ is its distinguished minimal root.
\label{cor:minimal_root_framed_pullback}
<!-- end corollary-2 -->
<!-- proof-28: body_md -->
If $(\Spf \R,\mathcal{M}_{\Spf \R})$ has framing $\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\square$}}}$, give $(\Spf \mathrm{S},\mathcal{M}_{\Spf \mathrm{S}})$ the framing $\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\square$}}} \circ f$. The claim follows by combining Lemma \ref{lem:completed-localization-minimal} and Proposition \ref{prop:root_crys_minimal}, using the description in Theorem \ref{thm:qdR_crys_Gamma_mod} to apply the first lemma.
<!-- end proof-28 -->
<!-- theorem-6: body_md -->
Let $(\X,\mathcal{M})$ satisfy Assumption \ref{ass:snc_log_structure} over $\W(k)[\zeta_p]$. Then the assignment
\[(\X,\mathcal{M}) \mapsto \@undefined_{\fgu}((\X,\mathcal{M})_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}, \ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}[1/\I_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}]_p^{\wedge})\]
is a stack for the strict \'{e}tale topology on such $(\X,\mathcal{M})$.
\label{thm:fgu_etale_desc}
<!-- end theorem-6 -->
<!-- proof-29: body_md -->
By Corollary \ref{cor:laur_strict_etale}, $\@undefined_{\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\blacksquare$}}}}((\X,\mathcal{M})_{\mathbbl{\Delta}},\ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}[1/\I_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}]_p^{\wedge})^{\varphi=1}$ satisfies strict \'{e}tale descent. The pullback is $t$-exact, and the cover may be taken finite, so boundedness is local. Let $\{\rho_i:\U_i\to(\X,\mathcal{M})\}_{i\in\I}$ be a strict \'{e}tale cover such that every $\rho_i^*\mathcal{E}$ is finitely generated unit.

Using Remark \ref{rem:fgu_mod_p} and Proposition \ref{prop:root_crys_minimal} we may reduce the claim to showing
\[\left\{\rho_i^*\mathcal{E} \in \Mod_{\fgu}((\U_i)_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}, \ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}[1/\I_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}]_p^{\wedge})_{p=0}\right\} \implies \left\{ \mathcal{E}\in \Mod_{\fgu}((\X,\mathcal{M})_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}, \ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}[1/\I_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}]_p^{\wedge})_{p=0}\right\}\]
for $\mathcal{E}\in \QCoh_{\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\blacksquare$}}}}((\X,\mathcal{M})_{\mathbbl{\Delta}},\ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}[1/\I_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}]_p^{\wedge})^{\varphi=1}$ killed by $p$, or that the condition can be detected locally on a strict \'{e}tale cover. Note that the converse is obvious, because any test log prism for the $\U_i$ is also one for $(\X,\mathcal{M})$, so the finitely generated unit condition on the right side already includes the conditions imposed on the left hand side.

By Lemma \ref{lem:strict_etale_local_framing}, after a finite strict \'{e}tale refinement we may assume without loss of generality that every $\U_i=\Spf\R_i$ is a framed log affine. Put $\U_{ij}=\U_i\times_{(\X,\mathcal{M})}\U_j$ with projections $p_i,p_j$; each affine open of $\U_{ij}$ inherits a framing through either projection. Proposition \ref{prop:root_crys_minimal} gives distinguished minimal roots $\mathcal{R}_i\subset\rho_i^*\mathcal{E}$. Corollary \ref{cor:minimal_root_framed_pullback}, applied with each framing, makes $p_i^*\mathcal{R}_i$ and $p_j^*\mathcal{R}_j$ distinguished minimal roots on any affine open of $\U_{ij}$. We may further cover $\U_{ij}$ by framed log affines.

Their uniqueness in Proposition \ref{prop:root_crys_minimal}, or what we called `distinguished', gives
\[p_i^*\mathcal{R}_i=p_j^*\mathcal{R}_j\subset\mathcal{E}|_{\U_{ij}}.\]
Indeed by the remark after Corollary \ref{cor:laur_t_struct} one has descent for coherent Laurent crystals $\Coh^{\varphi}((\X,\mathcal{M})_{\mathbbl{\Delta}},\ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}[1/\I_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}]_p^{\wedge})$ with a lax Frobenius. Thus we can check agreement locally on the chosen open cover of $\U_{ij}$ by framed log affines, which also shows agreement of the root maps. These equalities also satisfy the cocycle condition on triple overlaps, which is all we need to check as we work with coherent Laurent crystals.

Strict \'{e}tale descent for $\Coh^{\varphi}((\X,\mathcal{M})_{\mathbbl{\Delta}},\ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}[1/\I_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}]_p^{\wedge})_{p=0}$ and $\@undefined^{\varphi}_{\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\blacksquare$}}}}((\X,\mathcal{M})_{\mathbbl{\Delta}},\ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}[1/\I_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}]_p^{\wedge})^\ensuremath\heartsuit_{p=0}$ produces a global coherent root $\mathcal{E}_0$. Restricting any subroot or any other root to the cover shows that this root is again distinguished minimal. It is clear the unitalization remains $\mathcal{E}$ (as the claim is local and pullbacks commute with colimits). By the argument in Footnote \ref{fn:root_unitalization_fgu} we deduce $\mathcal{E}$ is finitely generated unit from the existence of a root.
<!-- end proof-29 -->
<!-- remark-6: body_md -->
Combined with Theorem \ref{thm:qdR_crys_Gamma_mod}, this shows that the finitely generated unit condition can equivalently be tested upon evaluation by a covering family of log $q$-de Rham prisms as claimed in the introduction.
\label{rem:qdR_test_sufficient}
<!-- end remark-6 -->
<!-- corollary-3: body_md -->
Let $(\X,\mathcal{M})$ satisfy Assumption \ref{ass:snc_log_structure} over $\W(k)[\zeta_p]$. A crystal 
\[\mathcal{E}\in \@undefined_{\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\blacksquare$}}}}((\X,\mathcal{M})_{\mathbbl{\Delta}},\ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}[1/\I_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}]_p^{\wedge})^{\varphi=1}\]
is finitely generated unit if and only if it is $t$-bounded and, for every $\ell$, the unit Laurent crystal $\mathrm{H}^\ell(\mathcal{E}\mathord{/\mkern-6mu/} p)$ admits a unique global minimal coherent root.
\label{cor:global_root_fgu_condition}
<!-- end corollary-3 -->
<!-- proof-30: body_md -->
The forward implication is the construction in the proof of Theorem \ref{thm:fgu_etale_desc}, applied to the cohomology sheaves of $\mathcal{E}\mathord{/\mkern-6mu/} p$ using Proposition \ref{prop:root_crys_minimal} locally. The converse follows from the first paragraph of the proof of Proposition \ref{prop:root_crys_minimal} which argues on a framed log affine why it suffices to know $\mathrm{H}^\ell(\mathcal{E}\mathord{/\mkern-6mu/} p)$ admit roots. Then as we know the property of being finitely generated unit is strict \'{e}tale local by Theorem \ref{thm:fgu_etale_desc} the general claim follows.
<!-- end proof-30 -->
<!-- remark-7: body_md -->
This is an analogue of the root criterion for finitely generated unit modules on a $k$-scheme $\X$. By \cite[Theorem 6.1.3]{EmertonKisin2}, a finitely generated unit $\ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}_{\mathrm{F},\X}$-module admits a coherent root on every quasicompact open; as $\X$ is quasicompact, the root is global. 

Such a root need not carry a crystal structure like in the previous corollary, but it turns out there always exists a root carrying such a structure. This seems to not be in the literature but follows from a short argument. Cartier descent (see \cite[Theorem 5.1]{KatzNilpMon}) gives a fully faithful functor
\[\QCoh(\X^{(1)}) \longrightarrow \QCoh((\X/k)_\cris)\]
with essential image the crystals with vanishing $p$-curvature. If $\mathrm{Fr}:\X\to\X^{(1)}$ is relative Frobenius, it sends $\mathscr{F}$ to $(\mathrm{Fr}^*\mathscr{F},\nabla_{\mathrm{can}})$, where $(\mathrm{Fr}^*\mathscr{F})^{\nabla_{\mathrm{can}}=0}\simeq\mathscr{F}$.

Write the absolute Frobenius as $\mathrm{F}_\X=\pi\circ\mathrm{Fr}$, with $\pi:\X^{(1)}\to\X$. Given a coherent root $\beta:\M_0\to \mathrm{F}_\X^*\M_0$, replace it by
\[\mathrm{F}_\X^*\beta:\mathrm{F}_\X^*\M_0 \longrightarrow \mathrm{F}_\X^{*2}\M_0.\]
Since $\mathrm{F}_\X$ is finite flat, this map is injective and has the same unitalization. Moreover, $\mathrm{F}_\X^*\M_0=\mathrm{Fr}^*\pi^*\M_0$ and $\mathrm{F}_\X^*\beta=\mathrm{Fr}^*(\pi^*\beta)$, so the map is horizontal for the canonical Cartier connections. It is therefore a coherent crystalline root. Uniqueness in Cartier descent identifies its unitalization with the crystal structure on $\M$ (similarly) induced by being an $\ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}_{\X}$-module with unit Frobenius.
<!-- end remark-7 -->
<!-- corollary-4: body_md -->
Let $f:(\Y,\mathcal{N})\to(\X,\mathcal{M})$ be a morphism between pairs satisfying Assumption \ref{ass:snc_log_structure} over $\W(k)[\zeta_p]$. Then $\mathrm{L} f^*$ preserves finitely generated unit crystals.
\label{cor:pullback}
<!-- end corollary-4 -->
<!-- proof-31: body_md -->
Let $\mathcal{E}$ be a finitely generated unit crystal on $(\X,\mathcal{M})_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}$, and let $(\B,\I,\M_{\Spf\B})^a$ be a log prism over $(\Y,\mathcal{N})$. Upon composing with $f$, we can give it the structure of a log prism over $(\X,\mathcal{M})$, and pullback of crystals gives a Frobenius equivariant equivalence
\[(\mathrm{L} f^*\mathcal{E})(\B,\I,\M_{\Spf\B})\simeq\mathcal{E}(\B,\I,\M_{\Spf\B}).\]
Thus every evaluation of $\mathrm{L} f^*\mathcal{E}$ is perfect over $\B[1/\I]^{\wedge}_p\langle\mathrm{F}\rangle$ by Definition \ref{def:fgu}.
<!-- end proof-31 -->
<!-- lemma-19: body_md -->
\label{lem:perfectoid_basis}
Let $(\X,\mathcal{M})$ be a locally Noetherian fs log $p$-adic formal scheme. Then the log affinoid perfectoid objects form a basis $\B$ of $(\X,\mathcal{M})_{\eta,\ensuremath{\mathrm{prok\acute{e}t}}}$ stable under fiber products.
<!-- end lemma-19 -->
<!-- proof-32: body_md -->
This is \cite[Propositions 5.3.11 and 5.3.12]{DiaoLanLiuZhuLogAdic}.
<!-- end proof-32 -->
<!-- definition-7: body_md -->
Let $(\X,\mathcal{M})$ be a locally Noetherian fs log $p$-adic formal scheme, and let $\mathcal{E}$ be a finitely generated unit Laurent crystal. Let $\U\in \B$ as in Lemma \ref{lem:perfectoid_basis}, with associated log perfectoid space
\[\widehat{\U} = (\Spa(\mathrm{S},\mathrm{S}^+),\mathcal{M}_{\mathrm{S}}).\]
We let ${\mathbbl{\Delta}}_{\mathrm{S}^+}$ be the log prism with underlying prism $(\W(\mathrm{S}^{+,\flat}),\ker \theta)$ and log structure induced by the tilted log structure on $\mathrm{S}^\flat$. We define
\[\T_\ensuremath{\mathrm{\acute{e}t}}(\mathcal{E})(\U) := \R\Hom_{\@undefined^{\varphi}_{\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\blacksquare$}}}}(\W(\mathrm{S}^\flat))}(\mathcal{E}({\mathbbl{\Delta}}_{\mathrm{S}^+}), \W(\mathrm{S}^\flat)) \in \widehat{\@undefined}(\Z_p).\]
These assignments define a presheaf on $\B$, which by ``unfolding" (or right Kan extension) yields a presheaf on $(\X,\mathcal{M})_{\eta,\ensuremath{\mathrm{prok\acute{e}t}}}$ we denote by $\T_\ensuremath{\mathrm{\acute{e}t}}(\mathcal{E})$.
\label{def:Tet}
<!-- end definition-7 -->
<!-- remark-8: body_md -->
Our convention so far has been to use the strict site, and unfortunately these perfect prisms do not live in the strict site. However this is not an issue because Remark \ref{rem:crystal_indep} allows us to use the saturated log prismatic site and obtain the same category of crystals.
<!-- end remark-8 -->
<!-- lemma-20: body_md -->
Let $(\X,\mathcal{M})$ be a locally Noetherian fs log $p$-adic formal scheme. Definition \ref{def:Tet} yields a well-defined functor
\[\T_\ensuremath{\mathrm{\acute{e}t}}: \@undefined_{\fgu}((\X,\mathcal{M})_{\mathbbl{\Delta}},\ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}[1/\I_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}]_p^{\wedge})^\op \longrightarrow \@undefined((\X,\mathcal{M})_{\eta,\ensuremath{\mathrm{prok\acute{e}t}}},\Z_p).\]
\label{lem:T_et_proket_sheaf}
<!-- end lemma-20 -->
<!-- proof-33: body_md -->
We will actually check hyperdescent, which is made easier as hypersheaves on the basis $\B$ from Lemma \ref{lem:perfectoid_basis} are the same as hypersheaves on $(\X,\mathcal{M})_{\eta,\ensuremath{\mathrm{prok\acute{e}t}}}$.

For $\U \in \B$ let $\U_\bullet\to\U$ be a hypercover by basis objects in $\B$, with associated perfectoid spaces $\widehat{\U}=\Spa(\mathrm{S},\mathrm{S}^+)$ and $\widehat{\U}_m=\Spa(\mathrm{S}_m,\mathrm{S}_m^+)$. On the associated perfectoid spaces one gets a $v$-hypercover
\[\widehat{\U}_\bullet \longrightarrow \widehat{\U}.\]
Here we use that the assignment $\U \mapsto \widehat{\U}$ commutes with fiber products, and the easier fact that pro-Kummer-\'{e}tale covers induce $v$-covers.

Put $\M=\mathcal{E}({\mathbbl{\Delta}}_{\mathrm{S}^+})$ and $\M_m=\mathcal{E}({\mathbbl{\Delta}}_{\mathrm{S}_m^+})$. The desired descent claim is that 
\[\lim_{[m]\in\Delta} \RHom_{\@undefined_{\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\blacksquare$}}}}^\varphi(\mathbb{A}_{\inf}(\mathrm{S}_m))}(\M_m,\mathbb{A}_{\inf}(\mathrm{S}_m)) \simeq \RHom_{\@undefined_{\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\blacksquare$}}}}^\varphi(\mathbb{A}_{\inf}(\mathrm{S}))}(\M,\mathbb{A}_{\inf}(\mathrm{S})).\] 
We can use the extension and restriction adjunction to make all $\RHom$s in $\@undefined_{\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\blacksquare$}}}}^\varphi(\mathbb{A}_{\inf}(\mathrm{S}))$, simplifying the left side to 
\[\lim_{[m]\in\Delta} \RHom_{\@undefined_{\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\blacksquare$}}}}^\varphi(\mathbb{A}_{\inf}(\mathrm{S}))}(\M,\mathbb{A}_{\inf}(\mathrm{S}_m)).\]
Thus the needed claim is actually that $\mathbb{A}_{\inf}(\mathrm{S}) \simeq\R\lim_{[m]\in\Delta}\mathbb{A}_{\inf}(\mathrm{S}_m)$. The claim can be checked modulo $p$, where it reduces to the $v$-acyclicity of the structure sheaves on $\Spa(\mathrm{S}_m^\flat, \mathrm{S}_m^{+,\flat})$ shown in \cite[Theorem 1.2]{etCohDiamonds}. Here we must also keep track of Frobenius and solid structures, but this much is clear.
<!-- end proof-33 -->
<!-- definition-8: body_md -->
Let $(\X,\mathcal{M})$ be as in Assumption \ref{ass:snc_log_structure}. We call $\mathscr{F}\in\@undefined^{(b)}_{\cons,\@undefined}((\X,\mathcal{M})_\eta,\Z_p)$ \emph{$p$-Kummer} if prime-to-$p$ logarithmic inertia $\I_{\bar{x}}^{\log, (p)'}$ acts trivially on every cohomology stalk of $\mathscr{F}\mathord{/\mkern-6mu/} p^n$ at every log geometric point, for every $n\geq1$. 
\label{def:p-Kum}
<!-- end definition-8 -->
<!-- lemma-21: body_md -->
On pairs satisfying Assumption \ref{ass:snc_log_structure} over $\ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}_K$, the full subcategories of $p$-Kummer sheaves in
\[\@undefined^{(b)}_{\cons,\@undefined}((\X,\mathcal{M})_\eta,\Z_p)\]
form a stack for the strict \'{e}tale topology.
\label{lem:constructible_strict_etale_descent}
<!-- end lemma-21 -->
<!-- proof-34: body_md -->
We first check the claim without the $p$-Kummer condition imposed. This can be checked fairly directly. Let $f:(\U,\mathcal{N})\to(\X,\mathcal{M})$ be a strict \'{e}tale cover on the log formal schemes, and let $\U^{(\bullet)}$ be its \v{C}ech nerve. 

Passing to adic generic fibers, this is compatible with fiber products so we can simply take log adic generic fibers of $\U^{(\bullet)}$ to obtain the corresponding \v{C}ech nerve on the log adic generic fiber. On the larger category of pro-Kummer-\'{e}tale sheaves, trivially we have
\[\@undefined^{(b)}((\X,\mathcal{M})_{\eta,\ensuremath{\mathrm{prok\acute{e}t}}},\Z_p) \simeq \varprojlim_{[n]\in\Delta} \@undefined^{(b)}((\U^{(n)},\mathcal{N}^{(n)})_{\eta,\ensuremath{\mathrm{prok\acute{e}t}}},\Z_p).\]
We also have such descent for $\@undefined^{(b)}_{\mathrm{lisse}}$. By strictness, if $\X_\eta^{(a)}$ and $\U_\eta^{(a)}$ denote the loci where $\mathrm{rk}_{\Z} \overline{\mathcal{M}}_{\bar x}^{\mathrm{gp}} = a$ (respectively for $\mathcal{N}$), then
\[\U_\eta^{(a)}=\U_\eta\times_{\X_\eta}\X_\eta^{(a)}.\]
The logarithmic strata in the \v{C}ech are therefore compatible, and we also have descent for lisse sheaves on each stratum (the strata are obtained by base change, so the corresponding \v{C}ech nerve again consists of strict \'{e}tale maps). As we are interested in constructible sheaves for this stratification the claim follows.

For the categories $\@undefined^{(b),\mathrm{pKum}}_{\cons,\@undefined}((\X,\mathcal{M})_\eta,\Z_p)$ with the $p$-Kummer condition imposed, note that strictness identifies the logarithmic inertia groups so the claim follows.
<!-- end proof-34 -->
<!-- lemma-22: body_md -->
Let $(\X,\mathcal{M})$ be a framed log affine with $\X=\Spf \R$ and let $\mathscr{F}$ be derived $p$-complete in $\@undefined^{(b)}((\Spf \R,\mathcal{M})_{\eta,\ensuremath{\mathrm{prok\acute{e}t}}},\Z_p)$. For $\Lambda\subseteq\{1,\ldots,r\}$, put
\[(\X,\mathcal{M})_{\infty,\eta,\Lambda}=(\X,\mathcal{M})_{\infty,\eta}\times_{(\X,\mathcal{M})_\eta}(\X,\mathcal{M})_{\eta,\Lambda},\]
and let $\epsilon_\infty:((\X,\mathcal{M})_{\infty,\eta},\mathcal{M}_\infty)_{\ensuremath{\mathrm{prok\acute{e}t}}}\to((\X,\mathcal{M})_{\infty,\eta})_{\ensuremath{\mathrm{pro\acute{e}t}}}$ be the natural morphism of sites. The following are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\mathscr{F}$ is constructible for the stratification induced by $\@undefined$ and is $p$-Kummer;
\item Its pullback to $(\X,\mathcal{M})_{\infty,\eta}$ is $\epsilon_\infty^*\mathcal{L}_\infty$ for some $\mathcal{L}_\infty\in\@undefined^{(b)}(((\X,\mathcal{M})_{\infty,\eta})_{\ensuremath{\mathrm{pro\acute{e}t}}},\Z_p)$ which is constructible for the finite stratification $(\X,\mathcal{M})_{\infty,\eta}=\bigsqcup_\Lambda (\X,\mathcal{M})_{\infty,\eta,\Lambda}$.
\end{enumerate}
\label{lem:pKum_framed_criterion}
<!-- end lemma-22 -->
<!-- proof-35: body_md -->
Constructibility is clear, because the pro-Kummer-\'{e}tale Galois cover $(\X,\mathcal{M})_{\infty,\eta}\to (\X,\mathcal{M})_\eta$ has the Galois group $\Gamma$ respect the strata $(\X,\mathcal{M})_{\infty,\eta}=\bigsqcup_\Lambda(\X,\mathcal{M})_{\infty,\eta,\Lambda}$. In particular we may test lissity on the strata induced by $\@undefined$ after pullback to $(\X,\mathcal{M})_{\infty,\eta,\Lambda}$, and then constructibility along $\@undefined$ after pullback to $(\X,\mathcal{M})_{\infty,\eta}=\bigsqcup_\Lambda(\X,\mathcal{M})_{\infty,\eta,\Lambda}$ by testing lissity on each stratum.

For the $p$-Kummer condition, we check stalkwise. The point is that the logarithmic inertia on the perfectoid cover $(\X,\mathcal{M})_{\infty,\eta}$ extracts precisely the prime-to-$p$ part on the base $(\X,\mathcal{M})_{\eta}$: for $\bar{y}\in (\X,\mathcal{M})_{\infty,\eta}$ a log geometric point above $\bar{x}\in (\X,\mathcal{M})_{\eta}$,
\[\I_{\infty,\bar{y}}^{\log} \simeq \Hom(\Z[1/p]^{|\Lambda|}, \widehat{\Z}(1)) = \I_{\bar{x}}^{\log, (p)'}\]
since $\I_{\bar{x}}^{\log, (p)'}$ is the prime-to-$p$ part of $\Hom(\overline{\mathcal{M}}_{\bar{x}}^{\mathrm{gp}},\widehat{\Z}(1))$. The condition we ask, that the pullback is of the form $\epsilon_\infty^*\mathcal{L}_\infty$, is equivalent to saying this acts trivially.
<!-- end proof-35 -->
<!-- lemma-23: body_md -->
Let $(\Spf \R,\mathcal{M})$ be a framed log affine, and put $\overline{\R}=\R_0/p$. If $\mathfrak{a}\subset \overline{\R}^{\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\square$}}}}\mathopen{(\mkern-3mu(}q-1\mathclose{)\mkern-3mu)}$ is an ideal stable under $\Z_p(1)^n\subset\Gamma$, then, on each connected component of
\[\Spa \overline{\R}^{\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\square$}}}}\mathopen{(\mkern-3mu(}q-1\mathclose{)\mkern-3mu)}\setminus \V(\T_1\cdots \T_r)\]
the image of $\mathfrak{a}[1/\T_1,\ldots,1/\T_r]$ is either zero or the unit ideal.

Moreover, the same conclusion holds for the scheme $\Spec \overline{\R}^{\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\square$}}}}\mathopen{(\mkern-3mu(}q-1\mathclose{)\mkern-3mu)}[1/\T_1,\ldots,1/\T_r]$.
\label{lem:toric_stable_ideal}
<!-- end lemma-23 -->
<!-- proof-36: body_md -->
Put $\X=\Spa \overline{\R}^{\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\square$}}}}\mathopen{(\mkern-3mu(}q-1\mathclose{)\mkern-3mu)}$ and $\X^\circ=\X\setminus \V(\T_1\cdots \T_r)$. Due to the framing $\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\square$}}}$, as rigid analytic spaces over $k\mathopen{(\mkern-3mu(}q-1\mathclose{)\mkern-3mu)}$ we have an \'{e}tale map 
\[\X\longrightarrow \Spa k\mathopen{(\mkern-3mu(}q-1\mathclose{)\mkern-3mu)} \langle \T_1, \ldots, \T_r, \T_{r+1}^{\pm 1}, \ldots, \T_n^{\pm 1} \rangle.\]
The target is reduced, hence so is $\X$. Through this \'{e}tale map, we also get an action of $\Z_p(1)^n$ on $\X$ which preserves $\X^{\circ}$. On the base, elements $x\in \Z_p(1)_i$ of the $i$th copy of $\Z_p(1)$ act by $\T_i\mapsto q^{px}\T_i$ and fixes the other coordinates.

Put $\mathcal{I}=\mathfrak{a}\ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}_{\X^\circ}$, and let $x$ be a classical point for which $\mathcal{I}_x$ is a proper ideal. Since $\ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}_{\X^\circ,x}$ is a local ring, this means $\mathcal{I}_x$ is contained in $\mathfrak{m}_x \ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}_{\X^\circ,x}$ and so all $f\in \mathfrak{a}$ vanish at $x$. Up to replacing $k\mathopen{(\mkern-3mu(}q-1\mathclose{)\mkern-3mu)}$ by the residue field $\kappa(x)/k\mathopen{(\mkern-3mu(}q-1\mathclose{)\mkern-3mu)}$, the rigid analytic inverse function theorem will identify some neighborhood of $x$ with a polydisk. Whether or not $\mathcal{I}_x$ vanishes can be checked after this extension, so without loss of generality we can assume $x$ is a rational point with a polydisk neighborhood.

Now we use $\Z_p(1)^n$ stability of $\mathfrak{a}$. Considering the elements $\gamma_\alpha = (p^{\alpha_1}, \ldots, p^{\alpha_n})\in \Z_p(1)^n$, stability means for $f\in \mathfrak{a}$ that $\gamma_\alpha \cdot f \in \mathfrak{a}$. They all vanish at $x$, so we will also get vanishing at $q^{p^{\alpha_i+1}}\T_i(x)$. For $\min_i \alpha_i \gg 0$ these live in the polydisk around $x$, by continuity of the action of $\Z_p(1)^n$. Since we work in positive characteristic we get
\[q^{p^{\alpha+1}}-1=(q-1)^{p^{\alpha+1}} \longrightarrow 0,\]
so we have produced an accumulating grid of zeroes in a polydisk around $x$. Applying the single variable rigid analytic identity theorem repeatedly, as in \cite[Lemma 3.9]{syncrisloc}, shows that a finite set of generators of $\mathfrak{a}$ vanishes on a neighborhood of $x$. Thus $\mathcal{I}_x=0$ if $\mathcal{I}_x$ is a proper ideal. In particular either $\mathcal{I}_x=\ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}_{\X^\circ,x}$ or it is zero, and we have seen the locus where it is zero is open (i.e. it propagates to a polydisk around $x$). Thus on connected components it is either zero or the unit ideal.

This proves the first assertion. To deduce the claim for the scheme, the same claims hold for $\mathfrak{a}_\mathfrak{m}$ for maximal ideals $\mathfrak{m}$ of $\Spec \overline{\R}^{\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\square$}}}}\mathopen{(\mkern-3mu(}q-1\mathclose{)\mkern-3mu)}[1/\T_1,\ldots,1/\T_r]$.
