Indeed the claim that $\mathcal{I}_x$ is zero or the unit ideal is simply about the base change to the completed local ring, which is faithfully flat over $\overline{\R}^{\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\square$}}}}\mathopen{(\mkern-3mu(}q-1\mathclose{)\mkern-3mu)}[1/\T_1,\ldots,\T_r]_\mathfrak{m}$ in our situation. Thus by faithfully flat descent, we deduce $\mathfrak{a}_\mathfrak{m}$ is zero or the unit ideal for maximal ideals in $\Spec \overline{\R}^{\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\square$}}}}\mathopen{(\mkern-3mu(}q-1\mathclose{)\mkern-3mu)}[1/\T_1,\ldots,1/\T_r]$. 

This is enough to deduce the desired claim that $\mathfrak{a}$ is $0$ or $1$ on connected components for the scheme. To see this, note that connected components are integral, and so reducing to the affine case we can use the fact that for a domain $\@undefined$ that
\[\@undefined = \bigcap_{\mathfrak{m} \in \mathrm{mSpec} \@undefined} \@undefined_\mathfrak{m}.\]
The ideal $\mathfrak{a}$ is zero or one in each $\@undefined_{\mathfrak{m}}$, hence on $\@undefined$. The claim then follows.
<!-- end proof-36 -->
<!-- lemma-24: body_md -->
Let $\overline{\mathrm{A}}=\overline{\R}^{\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\square$}}}}\mathopen{(\mkern-3mu(}q-1\mathclose{)\mkern-3mu)}$ for a framed log affine, and let $\mathrm{J}_{\Lambda}=(\T_i)_{i\in \Lambda}$ for some $\Lambda\subset\{1,\ldots,r\}$. If $\M \in \@undefined_{\fgu}(\overline{\mathrm{A}})^{h\Gamma}$, then
\[(\overline{\mathrm{A}}/\mathrm{J}_{\Lambda})\otimes^\mathrm{L}_{\overline{\mathrm{A}}}\M\]
is in $\@undefined_{\fgu}(\overline{\mathrm{A}}/\mathrm{J}_{\Lambda})^{h\Gamma}$.
\label{lem:derived_stratum_fgu}
<!-- end lemma-24 -->
<!-- proof-37: body_md -->
There is an induced $\Gamma$ action because the ideal $\mathrm{J}_{\Lambda}$ is stable under $\Gamma$. The finitely generated unit claim is clear because
\[(\overline{\mathrm{A}}/\mathrm{J}_{\Lambda})[\mathrm{F}]\otimes^{\mathrm{L}}_{\overline{\mathrm{A}}[\mathrm{F}]}\M\simeq(\overline{\mathrm{A}}/\mathrm{J}_{\Lambda})\otimes^{\mathrm{L}}_{\overline{\mathrm{A}}} \M,\]
showing the result is in $\mathrm{Thick}((\overline{\mathrm{A}}/\mathrm{J}_{\Lambda})[\mathrm{F}])$. It is unit because $\mathrm{J}_{\Lambda}$ is Frobenius stable (as is any ideal in positive characteristic).
<!-- end proof-37 -->
<!-- proposition-4: body_md -->
Let $(\Spf \R,\mathcal{M}_{\Spf \R})$ be a framed log affine with framing $\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\square$}}}$, and let $\mathcal{E}$ be an object of $\@undefined_{\fgu}((\Spf \R,\mathcal{M}_{\Spf \R})_{\mathbbl{\Delta}},\ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}[1/\I_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}]_p^{\wedge})$. Then $\T_{\ensuremath{\mathrm{\acute{e}t}}}^{\perf}(\mathcal{E}(\R_0^{\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\square$}}}}\mathopen{(\mkern-3mu(}q-1\mathclose{)\mkern-3mu)}^{\wedge}_p))$ is constructible for the stratification of $\Spec (\R_0^{\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\square$}}}})_{\infty,\eta}^{\flat}$ cut out by the divisor $\@undefined_\infty=\bigcup_i \V(\T_i^\flat)$.
\label{prop:perfectoid_constructibility}
<!-- end proposition-4 -->
<!-- proof-38: body_md -->
Because constructibility can be detected after reduction modulo $p$, from the start we can assume $\mathcal{E}\in \@undefined_{\fgu}((\Spf \R,\mathcal{M}_{\Spf \R})_{\mathbbl{\Delta}},\ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}[1/\I_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}]_p^{\wedge})_{p=0}$. As usual we put $\overline{\mathrm{A}} = \overline{\R}_0^{\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\square$}}}}\mathopen{(\mkern-3mu(}q-1\mathclose{)\mkern-3mu)}$ for the mod $p$ reduction of $\R_0^{\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\square$}}}}\mathopen{(\mkern-3mu(}q-1\mathclose{)\mkern-3mu)}^{\wedge}_p$.

Let $\M=\mathcal{E}(\R_0^{\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\square$}}}}\mathopen{(\mkern-3mu(}q-1\mathclose{)\mkern-3mu)}^{\wedge}_p)$, which we may regard as an object $\@undefined_{\fgu}(\overline{\mathrm{A}})^{h\Gamma}$ using Theorem \ref{thm:qdR_crys_Gamma_mod}. We defined $\T_{\ensuremath{\mathrm{\acute{e}t}}}^{\perf}(\M)$ to be 
\[\T_{\ensuremath{\mathrm{\acute{e}t}}}^{\perf}\left(\M\otimes_{\R_0^{\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\square$}}}}\mathopen{(\mkern-3mu(}q-1\mathclose{)\mkern-3mu)}^{\wedge}_p}^{\mathrm{L}} \W((\R_0^{\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\square$}}}})_{\infty,\eta}^{\flat})\right).\]
The input is in $\@undefined_{\fgu}(\W((\R_0^{\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\square$}}}})_{\infty,\eta}^{\flat}))$. For testing the claim, we may reduce to the case where $\M$ is a module (note the base change is flat, by flatness of Frobenius). To simply show that the output of $\T_\ensuremath{\mathrm{\acute{e}t}}^{\perf}$ in this case is lisse on the open stratum, or complement of $\@undefined_\infty$, it would suffice to show that $\M[1/\T_1,\ldots,1/\T_r]$ is a vector bundle over $\overline{\mathrm{A}}[1/\T_1,\ldots,1/\T_r]$ -- then the contravariant version of Katz's theorem from Remark \ref{rem:katz_contra} shows the output is lisse.

Let us dispense with this case first. We regard everything in what follows as a module over $\overline{\mathrm{A}}[1/\T_1,\ldots,1/\T_r]$ (i.e. we replace $\M$ with its base change to this ring). As we work modulo $p$, we can pick a $\Gamma$-equivariant minimal root $\beta: \M_0 \to \varphi^* \M_0$ for $\M$ (just as in the proof of Theorem \ref{thm:qdR_crys_Gamma_mod} using \cite{BlickleGamma}). Now Lemma \ref{lem:toric_stable_ideal} provides some serious constraints: each $\Fitt_i(\M_0)$ is $\Z_p(1)^n$-stable as are Fitting ideals of $\varphi^* \M_0$ and $\coker \beta$. Pick the minimal $i$ so that $\Fitt_i(\M_0)\neq 0$. One may test the desired constructibility claim locally, so we may reduce to the connected case and apply Lemma \ref{lem:toric_stable_ideal} to deduce this is the unit ideal. Finally applying \cite[Lemma 15.8.8, Tag \href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/07ZD}{07ZD}]{StacksProject} makes $\M_0$ locally free of rank $i$. We note $\varphi^*\M_0$ has the same rank and is necessarily a vector bundle.

By the same argument, we also find $\coker \beta$ is a vector bundle of some possibly different rank. But then we have the situation where we have an exact sequence
\begin{display}
0 \ar{r} & \M_0 \ar[hook]{r}{\beta} & \varphi^* \M_0 \ar{r} & \coker \beta \ar{r} & 0
\end{display}
consisting entirely of vector bundles, but the first two have the same rank. Thus $\coker \beta$ has rank zero, and $\beta$ is an isomorphism. Thus $\M=\M_0$, and the contravariant version of Katz's theorem tells us that $\T_{\ensuremath{\mathrm{\acute{e}t}}}^{\perf}(\M)$ is lisse away from $\@undefined_\infty$.

One can run exactly the same argument for any other stratum in the stratification induced by $\@undefined_\infty$ to see the result is lisse on this stratum. What we must do is consider $\overline{\R}_0^{\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\square$}}}}\mathopen{(\mkern-3mu(}q-1\mathclose{)\mkern-3mu)}/\mathrm{J}_{\Lambda}$ as in Lemma \ref{lem:derived_stratum_fgu} and use this lemma to deduce the derived base change of $\M$ is finitely generated unit, and then we can invert any surviving $\T_i$ if desired. Running the same reduction to the heart and repeating the argument the result follows.
<!-- end proof-38 -->
<!-- remark-9: body_md -->
For the trivial log structure there is only the open stratum, so the same argument shows we obtain a derived lisse complex. In particular without log structures, the theory degenerates to the ordinary theory of $(\varphi,\Gamma)$-modules.
<!-- end remark-9 -->
<!-- lemma-25: body_md -->
Let $(\Spf \R,\mathcal{M})$ be a framed log affine with framing $\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\square$}}}:(\Spf \R,\mathcal{M})\to\mathbb{T}_r^n$. Evaluation on ${\mathbbl{\Delta}}_{(\R_0^{\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\square$}}}})_\infty}$ gives a commutative diagram
\begin{display}[column sep=small,row sep=large]
\@undefined_{\fgu}((\Spf \R,\mathcal{M})_{\mathbbl{\Delta}},\ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}[1/\I_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}]_p^{\wedge})^\op \ar{rrr}{\T_\ensuremath{\mathrm{\acute{e}t}}} \ar[swap]{d}{\mathcal{E}\mapsto\mathcal{E}({\mathbbl{\Delta}}_{(\R_0^{\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\square$}}}})_\infty})} & & & \@undefined((\Spf \R,\mathcal{M})_{\eta,\ensuremath{\mathrm{prok\acute{e}t}}},\Z_p) \\
\left(\@undefined_{\fgu}(\W((\R_0^{\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\square$}}}})_{\infty,\eta}^{\flat}))^{h\Gamma}\right)^\op \ar{rrr}{\T_\ensuremath{\mathrm{\acute{e}t}}^{\perf}} & & & \@undefined^{(b)}_{\mathrm{cons}}(\Spec (\R_0^{\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\square$}}}})_{\infty,\eta}^{\flat},\Z_p)^{h\Gamma} \ar[swap]{u}{\mathrm{an}_\Gamma^*}
\end{display}
\label{lem:factorization}
<!-- end lemma-25 -->
<!-- proof-39: body_md -->
We showed already that the formula for $\T_\ensuremath{\mathrm{\acute{e}t}}$ outputs a sheaf in $\@undefined((\Spf \R,\mathcal{M})_{\eta,\ensuremath{\mathrm{prok\acute{e}t}}},\Z_p)$ in Lemma \ref{lem:T_et_proket_sheaf}, we may compute its output using the \v{C}ech nerve of $(\X,\mathcal{M})_{\infty,\eta}$ which is a pro-Kummer-\'{e}tale $\Gamma$-torsor over $(\Spf \R,\mathcal{M})_\eta$. In particular, once we use this specific cover to compute $\T_\ensuremath{\mathrm{\acute{e}t}}(\mathcal{E})$ we get a factorization
\[\T_\ensuremath{\mathrm{\acute{e}t}}: \@undefined_{\fgu}((\Spf \R,\mathcal{M})_{\mathbbl{\Delta}},\ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}[1/\I_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}]_p^{\wedge})^\op \longrightarrow \@undefined((\X,\mathcal{M})_{\infty,\eta,\ensuremath{\mathrm{prok\acute{e}t}}},\Z_p)^{h\Gamma}.\]
Setting $\M_{\infty}=\mathcal{E}({\mathbbl{\Delta}}_{(\R_0^{\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\square$}}}})_\infty})$, the goal is therefore a $\Gamma$-equivariant identification
\[\T_\ensuremath{\mathrm{\acute{e}t}}(\mathcal{E})(\U) \xlongrightarrow{\sim} \epsilon_\infty^*((\mathrm{an}^*\T_\ensuremath{\mathrm{\acute{e}t}}^{\perf}(\mathrm{M}_\infty))^{\#})(\U)\]
for log perfectoids $\U=(\Spa(\mathrm{S},\mathrm{S}^+),\mathcal{M}_{\mathrm{S}}) \to (\X,\mathcal{M})_{\infty,\eta}$. The equivariance is automatic once we do this functorially in $\U$, as the \v{C}ech nerve of $(\X,\mathcal{M})_{\infty,\eta}$ over $(\X,\mathcal{M})_\eta$ is a bar construction in $\Gamma$.

To construct the map is straightforward. Let $\mathscr{F}=\T_\ensuremath{\mathrm{\acute{e}t}}^{\perf}(\M_{\infty})$, and write $\mathscr{F}_{\mathrm{S}}$ for its pullback to $\Spec \mathrm{S}^\flat$. The formula for $\T_\ensuremath{\mathrm{\acute{e}t}}(\mathcal{E})(\U)$ identifies it directly with $\R\Gamma(\Spec \mathrm{S}^{\flat}_{\ensuremath{\mathrm{pro\acute{e}t}}}, \mathscr{F}_{\mathrm{S}})$. The right hand side $\epsilon_\infty^*((\mathrm{an}^*\T_\ensuremath{\mathrm{\acute{e}t}}^{\perf}(\mathrm{M}_\infty))^{\#})(\U)$ identifies with $\R\Gamma(\Spa(\mathrm{S}^{\flat},\mathrm{S}^{+,\flat})_{\ensuremath{\mathrm{pro\acute{e}t}}}, \mathrm{an}^* \mathscr{F}_{\mathrm{S}})$. Thus analytification, by functoriality, induces a comparison morphism.

By derived Nakayama, derived $p$-completeness reduces us to working with mod $p$ coefficients. The comparison map between $\R\Gamma(\Spa(\mathrm{S}^{\flat},\mathrm{S}^{+,\flat})_{\ensuremath{\mathrm{pro\acute{e}t}}}, \mathrm{an}^* \mathscr{F}_{\mathrm{S}})$ and $\R\Gamma(\Spec \mathrm{S}^{\flat}_{\ensuremath{\mathrm{pro\acute{e}t}}}, \mathscr{F}_{\mathrm{S}})$ is then an equivalence by \cite[Proposition 5.1]{AnschutzExtendingTorsors}\footnote{We note this comparison can be reproved using $\mathrm{arc}_{\varpi}$ descent results (which appeared later) for torsion \'{e}tale cohomology from \cite[Theorem 5.4 and Corollary 6.17]{BhattMathewArc}, where $\varpi$ is the tilted pseudouniformizer.}, applied to $(\mathrm{S}^\flat,\mathrm{S}^{+,\flat})$, together with the \'{e}tale versus pro\'{e}tale comparisons in \cite[Corollary 5.1.6]{proet} and \cite[Proposition 8.5(i)]{etCohDiamonds}.
<!-- end proof-39 -->
<!-- remark-10: body_md -->
\label{rem:Tet_sym_mon}
The factorization in Lemma \ref{lem:factorization} shows that $\T_\ensuremath{\mathrm{\acute{e}t}}$ from Definition \ref{def:Tet} is symmetric monoidal: for $\T_{\ensuremath{\mathrm{\acute{e}t}}}^{\perf}$, we showed it is symmetric monoidal in Theorem \ref{thm:EK_perfect}, and the remaining functors are symmetric monoidal. Note that one must also check that finitely generated unit modules are closed under $\otimes$, which can be done modulo $p$ by Remark \ref{rem:fgu_mod_p} and then using the roots provided by Corollary \ref{cor:global_root_fgu_condition} and that fact that $\otimes$ commutes with colimits.
<!-- end remark-10 -->
<!-- proposition-5: body_md -->
Every object in the essential image of $\T_\ensuremath{\mathrm{\acute{e}t}}$ on $\@undefined_{\fgu}((\X,\mathcal{M})_{\mathbbl{\Delta}},\ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}[1/\I_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}]_p^{\wedge})^\op$ is a $p$-Kummer sheaf in $\@undefined^{(b)}_{\cons,\@undefined}((\X,\mathcal{M})_\eta,\Z_p)$.
\label{prop:T_et_cons}
<!-- end proposition-5 -->
<!-- proof-40: body_md -->
The result is automatically $p$-Kummer by Lemma \ref{lem:factorization} and Lemma \ref{lem:pKum_framed_criterion}. 

For constructibility, we again use Lemma \ref{lem:factorization}. Inspecting the diagram, it suffices to know that the result in $\@undefined^{(b)}_{\mathrm{cons}}(\Spec (\R_0^{\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\square$}}}})_{\infty,\eta}^{\flat},\Z_p)^{h\Gamma}$ is constructible for the stratification induced by $\V(\T_i^\flat)$. Indeed, analytification and untilting respect these strata, as does the $\Gamma$-action as the strata on $(\X,\mathcal{M})_{\infty,\eta}$ are stable under the $\Gamma$ action, and descend to the strata $(\X,\mathcal{M})_{\Lambda,\eta}$ induced by $\@undefined_\eta$ on $(\X,\mathcal{M})_\eta$. 

Proposition \ref{prop:perfectoid_constructibility} shows exactly this result, so the desired claim follows.
<!-- end proof-40 -->
<!-- definition-9: body_md -->
Let $\mathcal{M}(-\@undefined)$ be the $\ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}_\X^\times$-torsor of local sections $m\in\mathcal{M}$ such that $\alpha_\X(m)\ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}_\X=\ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}_\X(-\@undefined)$. Let $(\mathrm{A},\I,\M_{\Spf \mathrm{A}})^a$ be a bounded log prism in $(\X,\mathcal{M})_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}^\op$, with structure map
\[f:(\Spf \mathrm{A}/\I,\M_{\Spf \mathrm{A}/\I})\to (\X,\mathcal{M}).\]
Let $i:\Spf \mathrm{A}/\I\to\Spf \mathrm{A}$ be the closed immersion. On $(\Spf \mathrm{A}/\I)_\ensuremath{\mathrm{\acute{e}t}}$, set $f^*\mathcal{M}(-\@undefined)$ to be obtained from $f^{-1}\mathcal{M}(-\@undefined)$ as the $\ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}^\times_{\Spf \mathrm{A}/\I}$-torsor given by change of structure group along $f^{-1} \ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}_\X^\times \to \ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}^\times_{\Spf \mathrm{A}/\I}$. The map $f^\flat: f^{-1}\mathcal{M} \to \M_{\Spf \mathrm{A}/\I}$ obtained from the structure map $f$ induces a morphism of \'{e}tale sheaves $f^*\mathcal{M}(-\@undefined)\to\M_{\Spf \mathrm{A}/\I}$. On $(\Spf \mathrm{A})_\ensuremath{\mathrm{\acute{e}t}}$, set $\widetilde{\mathcal{M}}_{\mathrm{A}}(-\@undefined):=\M_{\Spf \mathrm{A}}\times_{i_*\M_{\Spf \mathrm{A}/\I}}i_*f^*\mathcal{M}(-\@undefined)$. We then finally take
\[\ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}_{{\mathbbl{\Delta}}}(-\@undefined)(\mathrm{A},\I,\M_{\Spf \mathrm{A}}):=\Gamma\left(\Spf \mathrm{A},\mathcal{L}_{\ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}_{\Spf \mathrm{A}}^\times}(\widetilde{\mathcal{M}}_{\mathrm{A}}(-\@undefined))\right),\]
which one can think as of taking an $\ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}_{\Spf \mathrm{A}}$-span of the generators in $\widetilde{\mathcal{M}}_{\mathrm{A}}(-\@undefined)$ we have extracted.
<!-- end definition-9 -->
<!-- definition-10: body_md -->
For $n\geq 0$, set
\[\ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}(n\@undefined):=\underline{\Hom}_{\ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}}\left(\ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}(-\@undefined)^{\otimes^{\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\blacksquare$}}}} n},\ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}\right).\]
The map $\ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}(-\@undefined)\to \ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}$ gives transition maps $\ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}(n\@undefined)\to \ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}((n+1)\@undefined)$. We define
\[\ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}[1/\I_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}]_p^{\wedge}(\ast\@undefined):=\left(\left(\colim_{n\geq0}\ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}(n\@undefined)\right)^{\wedge}_p[1/\I_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}]\right)^{\wedge}_p.\]
\label{def:open_crystal}
<!-- end definition-10 -->
<!-- lemma-26: body_md -->
We have $\ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}[1/\I_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}]_p^{\wedge}(\ast \@undefined)\in \@undefined_{\fgu}((\X,\mathcal{M})_{\mathbbl{\Delta}},\ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}[1/\I_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}]_p^{\wedge})$.

Moreover, any crystal in $\Perf((\X,\mathcal{M})_{\mathbbl{\Delta}},\ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}[1/\I_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}]_p^{\wedge}(\ast \@undefined))^{\varphi=1}$ is also in $\@undefined_{\fgu}((\X,\mathcal{M})_{\mathbbl{\Delta}},\ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}[1/\I_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}]_p^{\wedge})$.
\label{lem:open_localized_fgu}
<!-- end lemma-26 -->
<!-- proof-41: body_md -->
For the first claim, the finitely generated unit condition can be checked modulo $p$ by Remark \ref{rem:fgu_mod_p}, and upon doing so the colimit presentation in Definition \ref{def:open_crystal} can be rewritten as $\left(\colim_{n\geq0}\varphi^{*n}\ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}(\@undefined)/p \right)[1/\I_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}]$. But then this root presentation makes it clear that after evaluation on any log prism $(\mathrm{A}^+,\I,\mathcal{M}_{\mathrm{A}^+})^a$ the result is in $\mathrm{Thick}(\bar{\mathrm{A}}[1/\I][\mathrm{F}])$ and unit, by the same argument as the footnote in Theorem \ref{thm:qdR_crys_Gamma_mod}.

For the second claim, we use Theorem \ref{thm:qdR_crys_Gamma_mod} as a shortcut. By Remark \ref{rem:qdR_test_sufficient} we can test membership in $\@undefined_{\fgu}((\X,\mathcal{M})_{\mathbbl{\Delta}},\ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}[1/\I_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}]_p^{\wedge})$ using log $q$-de Rham prisms, so we pick a log $q$-de Rham prism $(\R_0^{\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\square$}}}}\llbracket q-1 \rrbracket, [p]_q,\M)^a$ and wish to show for $\mathrm{A}=\R_0^{\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\square$}}}}\mathopen{(\mkern-3mu(}q-1\mathclose{)\mkern-3mu)}^{\wedge}_p$ that
\[\Perf(\mathrm{A}[1/\T_1,\ldots,1/\T_r]_p^{\wedge})^{\varphi=1} \hookrightarrow \@undefined_{\fgu}(\mathrm{A}).\]
Again using Remark \ref{rem:fgu_mod_p}, this can be tested modulo $p$; then it is clear from the root criterion to test the finitely generated unit condition for a Noetherian regular ring such as $\bar{\mathrm{A}}=\mathrm{A}/p$.

Indeed, using a Postnikov d\'{e}vissage (see \cite[Lemma 5.4.3]{HauckStacky}) we reduce to checking the claim on the heart for $\M \in \Coh(\bar{\mathrm{A}}[1/\T_1,\ldots,1/\T_r])^{\varphi=1}$. But there it is clear, as we can choose a coherent $\bar{\mathrm{A}}$-submodule $\M_0\subset \M$ with $\M_0[1/\T]=\M$, and let $\beta:\M \to\varphi^*\M$ be inverse to the unit Frobenius on $\M$. But then for some $\mathrm{N} \ge 0$ we have
\[\beta(\M_0)\subseteq\T^{-\mathrm{N}}\varphi^*\M_0.\]
It follows that $\T^{-k} \M_0$ is the desired root once $k$ is large; the claim follows.
<!-- end proof-41 -->
<!-- theorem-7: body_md -->
Let $(\X,\mathcal{M})$ be as in Assumption \ref{ass:snc_log_structure} over $\W(k)[\zeta_p]$. Then $\T_\ensuremath{\mathrm{\acute{e}t}}$ fits in a commutative diagram
\begin{display}
\Perf((\X,\mathcal{M})_{\mathbbl{\Delta}},\ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}[1/\I_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}]_p^{\wedge}(\ast \@undefined))^{\varphi=1,\op} \ar[hook]{d} \ar{r}{\sim} & \@undefined^{(b)}_{\mathrm{lisse}}((\X_\eta \setminus \@undefined_\eta)_{\ensuremath{\mathrm{pro\acute{e}t}}}, \Z_p) \ar[hook]{d}{j_!} \\
\@undefined_{\fgu}((\X,\mathcal{M})_{\mathbbl{\Delta}},\ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}[1/\I_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}]_p^{\wedge})^\op \ar{r}{\T_\ensuremath{\mathrm{\acute{e}t}}} & \@undefined^{(b)}_{\cons,\@undefined}((\X,\mathcal{M})_\eta,\Z_p).
\end{display}
The top horizontal arrow is an equivalence.
\label{thm:open_stratum}
<!-- end theorem-7 -->
<!-- remark-11: body_md -->
\label{rem:strata}
Although \cite[Corollary 3.7]{BhattScholzePrismaticFCrystals} describes the target using ordinary Laurent $\mathrm{F}$-crystals, it is not directly suited to the functor $j_!$. Among several issues is that the complement $\X_\eta\setminus\@undefined_\eta$ need not be quasicompact; for example, consider $\mathbf{P}^1_{\Q_p}\setminus\{\infty\}=\A^1_{\Q_p}$. Moreover, a formal model of this complement need not map to the fixed smooth proper model $\X$ with generic fiber $\X_\eta$, and even worse Raynaud models require noncanonical admissible blowups to acquire such a map and need not remain smooth. We fix these problems by using log formal schemes to encode the stratification.
<!-- end remark-11 -->
<!-- remark-12: body_md -->
Let $\pi=\zeta_p-1$ be a uniformizer of $\W(k)[\zeta_p]$. If one does not invert $\I_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}$ and instead takes the unitalization of $\ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}(\@undefined) \to \varphi^* \ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}(\@undefined)$, one can calculate that the crystalline realization (i.e. the unitalization $\mathcal{E}$ of $\ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}_\cris(\@undefined) \to \varphi^* \ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}_\cris(\@undefined)$) satisfies
\[\R\Hom_{\@undefined^{\varphi}(((\X,\mathcal{M})_{\pi=0}/\W(k))_\cris,\ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}_\cris)} (\mathcal{E},\ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}_\cris) \simeq \left(\R\Gamma_{\cris,c}((\X,\mathcal{M})_{\pi=0}/\W(k))\right)^{\varphi=1}.\]
Here compactly supported log crystalline cohomology is as defined in \cite{TsujiLogCrystallinePD}. This shows the crystalline realization of the natural non-Laurentized variant of $\ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}[1/\I_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}]_p^{\wedge}(\ast \@undefined)$ is compatible with the expectation one would have from the open $\mathrm{C}_{\mathrm{st}}$ conjecture.
\label{rem:comparison}
<!-- end remark-12 -->
<!-- lemma-27: body_md -->
Let $(\X,\mathcal{M})$ be as in Assumption \ref{ass:snc_log_structure} over $\W(k)[\zeta_p]$. The category 
\[\Perf((\X,\mathcal{M})_{\mathbbl{\Delta}},\ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}[1/\I_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}]_p^{\wedge}(\ast \@undefined))^{\varphi=1,\op}\]
is a stack for the strict \'{e}tale topology on such $(\X,\mathcal{M})$.
\label{lem:open_stratum_desc}
<!-- end lemma-27 -->
<!-- proof-42: body_md -->
This follows from Theorem \ref{thm:fgu_etale_desc}, because we can extract the desired category 
\[\Perf((\X,\mathcal{M})_{\mathbbl{\Delta}},\ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}[1/\I_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}]_p^{\wedge}(\ast \@undefined))^{\varphi=1}\]
as dualizable modules over the idempotent algebra $\ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}[1/\I_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}]_p^{\wedge}(\ast \@undefined)$ in $\@undefined_{\fgu}((\X,\mathcal{M})_{\mathbbl{\Delta}},\ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}[1/\I_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}]_p^{\wedge})$. Formally, both of these operations preserve the limit diagram we use to test descent along a strict \'{e}tale cover $(\U,\mathcal{M}_\U) \to (\X,\mathcal{M})$, namely that we have a limit diagram
\[\@undefined_{\fgu}((\X,\mathcal{M})_{\mathbbl{\Delta}},\ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}[1/\I_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}]_p^{\wedge}) \simeq \lim_{[n]\in \Delta} \@undefined_{\fgu}((\U^{(n)},\mathcal{M}_{\U^{(n)}})_{\mathbbl{\Delta}},\ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}[1/\I_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}]_p^{\wedge})\]
for the \v{C}ech nerve. This is because $\ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}[1/\I_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}]_p^{\wedge}(\ast \@undefined)$ is an idempotent algebra in $\@undefined_{\fgu}((\X,\mathcal{M})_{\mathbbl{\Delta}},\ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}[1/\I_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}]_p^{\wedge})$ taking modules over it gives a limit diagram, and then the same holds for taking dualizable objects. This last step is actually not necessary, since the Fitting ideal argument in Proposition \ref{prop:perfectoid_constructibility} shows it is redundant.
<!-- end proof-42 -->
<!-- lemma-28: body_md -->
Let $(\Spf \R,\mathcal{M})$ be a framed log affine. Then
\[\Perf((\Spf \R,\mathcal{M})_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}, \ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}[1/\I_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}]_p^{\wedge}(\ast \@undefined))^{\varphi=1} \simeq \Perf(\R_0^{\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\square$}}}}\mathopen{(\mkern-3mu(}q-1\mathclose{)\mkern-3mu)}^{\wedge}_p[1/\T_1, \ldots, 1/\T_r]^{\wedge}_p)^{\varphi=1, h\Gamma}.\]
\label{lem:open_crys_gamma_mod}
<!-- end lemma-28 -->
<!-- proof-43: body_md -->
Put $\mathrm{A}=\R_0^{\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\square$}}}}\mathopen{(\mkern-3mu(}q-1\mathclose{)\mkern-3mu)}^{\wedge}_p$ and $\mathrm{A}^{\circ}=\mathrm{A}[1/\T_1,\ldots,1/\T_r]^{\wedge}_p$, so that evaluation on the logarithmic $q$-de Rham prism carries $\ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}[1/\I_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}]_p^{\wedge}(\ast\@undefined)$ to $\mathrm{A}^\circ$ with its $\Gamma$-action. Using Lemma \ref{lem:open_localized_fgu} we can embed the source category into finitely generated unit Laurent crystals, and due to Theorem \ref{thm:qdR_crys_Gamma_mod} we see $\Perf((\Spf \R,\mathcal{M})_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}, \ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}[1/\I_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}]_p^{\wedge}(\ast \@undefined))^{\varphi=1} \xrightarrow{} \Perf(\mathrm{A}^{\circ})^{\varphi=1, h\Gamma}$ is fully faithful.

Conversely, let $\M\in \Perf(\mathrm{A}^{\circ})^{\varphi=1,h\Gamma}$. This category clearly sits inside $\@undefined_{\fgu}(\mathrm{A})^{h\Gamma}$, thus \ref{thm:qdR_crys_Gamma_mod} gives an fgu crystal $\mathcal{E}$ with evaluation $\M$. The localization map
\[\mathcal{E}\longrightarrow\mathcal{E}\otimes\ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}[1/\I_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}]_p^{\wedge}(\ast\@undefined)\]
is an equivalence after evaluation on the log $q$-de Rham prism, hence is an equivalence by conservativity. Thus $\mathcal{E}$ is an $\ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}[1/\I_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}]_p^{\wedge}(\ast\@undefined)$-module. Using the description 
\[\Perf((\Spf \R,\mathcal{M})_{\mathbbl{\Delta}},\ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}[1/\I_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}]_p^{\wedge}(\ast\@undefined))\simeq\varprojlim_{[m]\in\Delta}\Perf(\mathrm{A}^{\circ,(m)})\]
and that the crystal property identifies evaluation of $\mathcal{E}$ on the $m$th term of the \v{C}ech nerve of the log $q$-de Rham prism with
\[\mathrm{A}^{\circ,(m)}\widehat\otimes_{\mathrm{A}^\circ}^{\mathrm{L}}\M,\]
which is perfect over $\mathrm{A}^{\circ,(m)}$, since dualizability is detected termwise in a limit of symmetric monoidal categories $\mathcal{E}$ is perfect over $\ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}[1/\I_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}]_p^{\wedge}(\ast\@undefined)$. The claim follows.
<!-- end proof-43 -->
<!-- proposition-6: body_md -->
\label{prop:open_decompletion_hom}
Let $(\Spf \R,\mathcal{M})$ be a framed log affine. The base change functor
\[\Perf((\Spf \R,\mathcal{M})_{\mathbbl{\Delta}},\ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}[1/\I_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}]_p^{\wedge}(\ast \@undefined))^{\varphi=1} \longrightarrow \Perf(\mathbb{A}_{\inf}((\R_0^{\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\square$}}}})_\infty)[1/\xi,1/[\T_1^\flat],\ldots,1/[\T_r^\flat]]^{\wedge}_p)^{\varphi=1,h\Gamma}\]
is fully faithful.
<!-- end proposition-6 -->
<!-- proof-44: body_md -->
As usual, associated to the framed log affine we have a logarithmic $q$-de Rham prism, so we let $\mathrm{A}=\R_0^{\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\square$}}}} \mathopen{(\mkern-3mu(}q-1\mathclose{)\mkern-3mu)}_p^{\wedge}$. For this particular proof we only care about a localization, so put $\mathrm{A}^{\circ} := \mathrm{A}[1/\T_1,\ldots,1/\T_r]_p^{\wedge}$ and $\mathrm{A}_{\perf}^{\circ} = \mathbb{A}_{\inf}((\R_0^{\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\square$}}}})_\infty)[1/\xi,1/[\T_1^\flat],\ldots,1/[\T_r^\flat]]^{\wedge}_p$. We can express the source as $\Perf(\mathrm{A}^{\circ})^{\varphi=1,h\Gamma}$ using Lemma \ref{lem:open_crys_gamma_mod}; the target is already $\Perf(\mathrm{A}_\perf^{\circ})^{\varphi=1,h\Gamma}$.

By the tensor/Hom adjunction, it suffices to show that
\begin{equation}
\mathrm{R}\Gamma_{\mathrm{cont}}(\Gamma,\M)^{\varphi=1}\longrightarrow\mathrm{R}\Gamma_{\mathrm{cont}}(\Gamma,\M\otimes_{\mathrm{A}^{\circ}} \mathrm{A}^{\circ}_{\perf})^{\varphi=1}
\label{eq:cohom_comp}
\end{equation}
is an isomorphism for $\M \in \Perf(\mathrm{A}^{\circ})^{\varphi=1,h\Gamma}$. We can also use the ordinary tensor product $\M\otimes_{\mathrm{A}^{\circ}} \mathrm{A}^{\circ}_{\perf}$ in the target because the relevant map $\mathrm{A}^{\circ} \to \mathrm{A}^{\circ}_{\perf}$ is faithfully flat. Indeed, Kunz's theorem makes $\mathrm{A}^+/p\to\mathrm{A}^+_{\perf}/p$ faithfully flat, so $\mathrm{A}^+\to\mathrm{A}^+_{\perf}$ is $p$-completely faithfully flat. The map $\mathrm{A}^{\circ}\to\mathrm{A}^{\circ}_{\perf}$ is its $p$-completed base change after inverting $[p]_q,\T_1,\ldots,\T_r$, so it is $p$-completely faithfully flat; since $\mathrm{A}^{\circ}$ is Noetherian, it is faithfully flat.

By derived Nakayama we can work with mod $p$ coefficients, which we now do. The source and target both have standard $t$-structures modulo $p$ obtained by restricting the $t$-structures on $\@undefined(\mathrm{A}^{\circ}/p)$ and $\@undefined(\mathrm{A}^{\circ}_{\perf}/p)$. To check these are well-defined one must check truncations remain perfect -- this is clear for the source because $\mathrm{A}^{\circ}/p$ is Noetherian regular. For the target the $t$-structure exists before applying $(-)^{h\Gamma}$, which is implicit in the proof \cite[Proposition 3.4]{BhattScholzePrismaticFCrystals}: in particular they show that the top cohomology of a perfect unit Frobenius module over an $\F_p$-algebra is a vector bundle. Using a Postnikov d\'{e}vissage (\cite[Lemma 5.4.3]{HauckStacky}) we reduce to testing the claim for $p$-torsion $\M$ in the heart (which must lie in $\Vect(\mathrm{A}^{\circ}/p)^{\varphi=1,h\Gamma}$).

We now prove (\ref{eq:cohom_comp}) for $\M$ in $\Vect(\mathrm{A}^{\circ}/p)^{\varphi=1,h\Gamma}$. The faithfully flat map $\mathrm{A}^\circ/p\to\mathrm{A}^\circ_{\perf}/p$ is injective, with cokernel $(\mathrm{A}^\circ_{\perf}/\mathrm{A}^\circ)/p$. Since $\M$ is finite projective over $\mathrm{A}^\circ/p$, tensoring this sequence with $\M$ is exact. It is therefore enough to prove $\mathrm{R}\Gamma_{\mathrm{cont}}(\Gamma,\M\otimes_{\mathrm{A}^{\circ}}(\mathrm{A}^\circ_{\perf}/\mathrm{A}^{\circ}))^{\varphi=1}=0$.

Choose $m\gg0$ and let $(\R_0^{\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\square$}}}})_m$ be obtained from the framing by adjoining $p^m$th roots of the coordinates $\T_i$. Define $\varphi^{-m}\mathrm{A}^{\circ}=(\R_0^{\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\square$}}}})_m\mathopen{(\mkern-3mu(}q^{1/p^m}-1\mathclose{)\mkern-3mu)}[1/\T_1,\ldots,1/\T_r]_p^{\wedge}$ and $\varphi^{-m}\mathrm{A}^{\circ,\mathrm{cyc}}=(\R_0^{\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\square$}}}})_m\mathopen{(\mkern-3mu(}q^{1/p^\infty}-1\mathclose{)\mkern-3mu)}^{\wedge}[1/\T_1,\ldots,1/\T_r]^{\wedge}_p$, viewed as intermediate subrings
\[\mathrm{A}^{\circ} \subset \varphi^{-m}\mathrm{A}^{\circ}\subset \varphi^{-m}\mathrm{A}^{\circ,\mathrm{cyc}}\subset \mathrm{A}^{\circ}_{\perf}.\]
Since $\varphi$ and $\Gamma$ commute, the unit Frobenius of $\M$ gives a $\Gamma$-equivariant equivalence
\[\mathrm{R}\Gamma_{\mathrm{cont}}(\Gamma,\M)^{\varphi=1}\simeq\mathrm{R}\Gamma_{\mathrm{cont}}\bigl(\Gamma,\M\otimes_{\mathrm{A}^\circ}\varphi^{-m}\mathrm{A}^\circ\bigr)^{\varphi=1}.\]

For $m \gg 0$, the exact triangles associated to 
\[\varphi^{-m}\mathrm{A}^{\circ}/\mathrm{A}^{\circ} \longrightarrow \mathrm{A}^{\circ}_{\perf}/\mathrm{A}^{\circ} \longrightarrow \mathrm{A}^{\circ}_{\perf}/\varphi^{-m}\mathrm{A}^{\circ}\]  
and to $\varphi^{-m}\mathrm{A}^{\circ,\mathrm{cyc}}/\varphi^{-m}\mathrm{A}^{\circ} \longrightarrow \mathrm{A}^{\circ}_{\perf}/\varphi^{-m}\mathrm{A}^{\circ} \longrightarrow \mathrm{A}^{\circ}_{\perf}/\varphi^{-m}\mathrm{A}^{\circ,\mathrm{cyc}}$ show
\[\mathrm{R}\Gamma_{\mathrm{cont}}(\Gamma,\M\otimes_{\mathrm{A}^{\circ}}(\mathrm{A}^{\circ}_{\perf}/\mathrm{A}^{\circ}))^{\varphi=1}=0\]
by applying Lemmas \ref{lem:open_decompletion_toric_acyclic} and \ref{lem:open_decompletion_q_acyclic}. The claim then follows.
<!-- end proof-44 -->
<!-- lemma-29: body_md -->
\label{lem:kedlaya-liu}
Let $\Gamma_0 \le \Gamma$ be a closed subgroup and let $\B$ be an LB ring with a continuous action of $\Gamma_0$, and let $\V$ be an LB $\B$-module with a continuous $\Gamma_0$-action.

Suppose that we have a $\Gamma_0$-equivariant decomposition of LB modules
\[\widehat{\bigoplus}^{\mathrm{LB}}_{j\geq0} \V_j \xrightarrow{\sim} \V,\]
such that the cochain complexes $\R\Gamma(\Gamma_0,\V_j)$ admit uniformly bounded contracting homotopies. Then $\R\Gamma(\Gamma_0,\V)=0$.
<!-- end lemma-29 -->
<!-- proof-45: body_md -->
This is immediate from the definitions: uniform boundedness extends the contracting homotopy to $\R\Gamma(\Gamma_0,\V)$.
<!-- end proof-45 -->
<!-- lemma-30: body_md -->
\label{lem:open_decompletion_q_acyclic}
Let $\M\in \Vect(\mathrm{A}^{\circ}/p)^{\varphi=1,h\Gamma}$. For $m\gg0$,
\[\mathrm{R}\Gamma_{\mathrm{cont}}\bigl(\Gamma,\M \widehat{\otimes}_{\mathrm{A}^{\circ}}(\varphi^{-m}\mathrm{A}^{\circ,\mathrm{cyc}}/\varphi^{-m}\mathrm{A}^{\circ})\bigr)=0.\]
<!-- end lemma-30 -->
<!-- proof-46: body_md -->
It suffices to show the cohomology for $\Gamma_0=(1+p^m\Z_p)\ltimes (p^{m-1}\Z_p(1))^n$ vanishes, where $m$ is chosen as before so that $\gamma_i-1$ raise the $(q-1)$-adic filtration. We call the normal subgroup $\mathrm{H}=(p^{m-1}\Z_p(1))^n$.

To apply Lemma \ref{lem:kedlaya-liu}, we will decompose $\M\otimes_{\overline{\mathrm{A}}^{\circ}}(\varphi^{-m}\overline{\mathrm{A}}^{\circ,\mathrm{cyc}}/\varphi^{-m}\overline{\mathrm{A}}^{\circ})$. To do this, we set $\B_0 = \varphi^{-m} \overline{\mathrm{A}}^{\circ} = (\overline{\R}_0^{\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\square$}}}})_m\mathopen{(\mkern-3mu(}q^{1/p^{m}}-1\mathclose{)\mkern-3mu)}[1/\T_1,\ldots,1/\T_r]$. Recall we used the notation $(\overline{\R}_0^{\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\square$}}}})_m$ to denote that we have adjoined $1/p^m$th powers of the $\T_i$. We then set $\B_j = (\overline{\R}_0^{\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\square$}}}})_m \mathopen{(\mkern-3mu(}q^{1/p^{m+j}}-1\mathclose{)\mkern-3mu)}[1/\T_1,\ldots,1/\T_r]$, so $\B_\infty$ is $\varphi^{-m}\overline{\mathrm{A}}^{\circ,\mathrm{cyc}}$. We write $\M_{\B_j}$ for the base change of $\M$ to one of these LB rings. 

Then
\[\B_{j+1}=\bigoplus_{a=0}^{p-1}\B_jq^{a/p^{m+j+1}}\]
allows us to define $\Gamma$-equivariant $\B_j$-linear retractions $\psi_j$ by projection onto $a=0$. With the prescribed LB structures, 
\[\widehat{\bigoplus}^{\mathrm{LB}}_j\ker(\psi_j) \simeq \B_\infty/\B_0.\]
Tensoring up with the vector bundle $\M$, we get a decomposition by $\M_{\B_j} \widehat{\otimes} \ker \psi_j$ of $\M\otimes_{\overline{\mathrm{A}}^{\circ}}(\varphi^{-m}\overline{\mathrm{A}}^{\circ,\mathrm{cyc}}/\varphi^{-m}\overline{\mathrm{A}}^{\circ}) = \M_{\B_{\infty}}/\M_{\B_0}$.

Thus it only remains to produce the contracting homotopies. This is tricky, because our $\Gamma_0$ is not commutative. However Lemma \ref{lem:kedlaya-liu} still applies here, as we still have produced an explicit cochain model for $\Gamma_0$-cohomology in this case. For this model, we recall we had to fix generators. We fix $\gamma_0 = 1 + p^{m}$ generating $1+p^m \Z_p$, and $\gamma_i$ generators of $\mathrm{H}=(p^{m-1}\Z_p(1))^n$.

It suffices actually to produce a contracting homotopy for the fiber of $\gamma_0-1$, but for the entire Koszul complex $\mathrm{Kos}_{\mathrm{H}}^\bullet(\M_{\B_j} \otimes_{\B_j} \ker \psi_j)$. Using the aforementioned decompositions $\B_{j+1}=\bigoplus_{a=0}^{p-1}\B_jq^{a/p^{m+j+1}}$, since the decomposition is $\mathrm{H}$-equivariant we can decompose further into
\[\mathrm{Kos}_{\mathrm{H}}^\bullet(\M_{\B_j} \otimes_{\B_j} \ker \psi_j) \simeq \bigoplus_{1\le a \le p-1} \mathrm{Kos}_{\mathrm{H}}^\bullet(\M_{\B_j} q^{a/p^{m+j+1}}).\]
To apply Lemma \ref{lem:kedlaya-liu} it will suffice to produce a contracting homotopy for the action of $\gamma_0-1$ on these summands. 

For each $a$, the summands $\mathrm{Kos}_{\mathrm{H}}^\bullet(\M_{\B_j} q^{a/p^{m+j+1}})$ in question can be written as
\[\M_{\B_j} q^{a/p^{m+j+1}} \xlongrightarrow{} \M_{\B_j} q^{a/p^{m+j+1}} \otimes_{\Z_p} \Lambda^1(\mathrm{H}) \xlongrightarrow{} \cdots \xlongrightarrow{} \M_{\B_j} q^{a/p^{m+j+1}} \otimes_{\Z_p} \Lambda^n(\mathrm{H}).\]
For $\I\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}$, write $e_\I=\bigwedge_{i\in \I}e_i$ for the corresponding basis element of the term for $\Lambda^{|\I|}(\mathrm{H})$. Using $\gamma_0\gamma_i=\gamma_i^{1+p^m} \gamma_0$ we see
\[\gamma_0(- \cdot e_\I)=\left(\prod_{i\in \I}\frac{\gamma_i^{1+p^m}-1}{\gamma_i-1}\right)^{-1}\gamma_0(-)e_\I.\]
On the summand $\M_{\B_j} q^{a/p^{m+j+1}}$ we have $\gamma_0 - 1 = (q^{a/p^{j+1}}-1) \left[1+ (q^{a/p^{j+1}}-1)^{-1}(\gamma_0-q^{a/p^{j+1}})\right]$. Thus to give a contracting homotopy on the mapping fiber, it suffices to show the bound $\|(q^{a/p^{j+1}}-1)^{-1}(\gamma_0-q^{a/p^{j+1}})\|_{\mathrm{N}} < 1$. We actually do not care if the bound depends on $j$, since in computing $\|(\gamma_0 - 1)^{-1}\|_{\mathrm{N}}$ the inverse of $\left[1+ (q^{a/p^{j+1}}-1)^{-1}(\gamma_0-q^{a/p^{j+1}})\right]$ has norm $\le 1$ -- thus the bound is entirely dependent on $|(q^{a/p^{j+1}}-1)|^{-1} < |q-1|^{-1}$, making it uniform.

By using the action on $\B_j$ and using that $\gamma_0-1$ raises the $q-1$-adic filtration for coefficients this action eventually satisfies for $m \gg 0$
\[\left\|(q^{a/p^{j+1}}-1)^{-1}(\gamma_0-q^{a/p^{j+1}})\right\|_\mathrm{N} \leq |q-1|^{p^{-j}(1-p^{-m}-p^{-1})}<1.\]
This handles the fiber of $\gamma_0-1$ on $\M_{\B_j} q^{a/p^{m+j+1}}$. For the full Koszul complex, note that there are finitely many $\I\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}$ to deal with and $\left\|\left(\prod_{i\in \I}\frac{\gamma_i^{1+p^m}-1}{\gamma_i-1}\right)^{-1} - 1\right\|_\mathrm{N} \le |q-1|^{p^m-1}$ (again crucially using that $\gamma_i-1$ raise the $q-1$-adic filtration).

Thus we have produced the required homotopies and Lemma \ref{lem:kedlaya-liu} finishes the claim. Note that we only showed vanishing $\Gamma_0$ cohomology, but by Hochschild-Serre this proves there is no $\Gamma$-cohomology as well.
<!-- end proof-46 -->
<!-- lemma-31: body_md -->
\label{lem:open_decompletion_toric_acyclic}
Let $\M\in \Vect(\mathrm{A}^{\circ}/p)^{\varphi=1,h\Gamma}$. For $m\gg0$,
\[\mathrm{R}\Gamma_{\mathrm{cont}}\bigl(\Gamma,\M \widehat{\otimes}_{\mathrm{A}^{\circ}}(\mathrm{A}^{\circ}_{\perf}/\varphi^{-m}\mathrm{A}^{\circ,\mathrm{cyc}})\bigr)=0.\]
<!-- end lemma-31 -->
<!-- proof-47: body_md -->
The argument is very similar, so we simply indicate the decomposition we use and contracting homotopies to apply the same strategy as the previous lemma.

In this case we put $\B_j = \varphi^{-(m+j)}\mathrm{A}^{\circ,\mathrm{cyc}}/p$ and write $\M_{\B_j}$ for the base changes to these rings, and $\Gamma_0=(p^{m-1}\Z_p(1))^n$. We must produce a $\Gamma_0$-equivariant decomposition of
\[\M\otimes_{\mathrm{A}^{\circ}}(\mathrm{A}^{\circ}_{\perf}/\varphi^{-m}\mathrm{A}^{\circ,\mathrm{cyc}}) = \M_{\B_{\infty}}/\M_{\B_0}.\]
Now for $\alpha=(a_1,\ldots,a_n)$, there is a decomposition
\[\B_{j+1}=\bigoplus_{\alpha\in\{0,\ldots,p-1\}^n}\B_j\prod_{\nu=1}^n\T_\nu^{a_\nu/p^{m+j+1}}\]
This defines $\psi_j$ as the projection onto the $\alpha = \vec{0}$ component. With the obvious LB structures, these give
\[\widehat{\bigoplus}^{\mathrm{LB}}_{j\geq0}\ker(\psi_j)\simeq\B_\infty/\B_0,\]
which we can similarly tensor with $\M$ to get a decomposition of $\M_{\B_{\infty}}/\M_{\B_0}$. We must then produce contracting homotopies for the individual summands $\M_{\B_j} \widehat{\otimes} \ker \psi_j$.

Using the generators $\gamma_1,\ldots,\gamma_n$ of $\Gamma_0$, the preceding $\Gamma_0$-equivariant decomposition reduces us to contracting the complexes
\[\mathrm{Kos}_{\Gamma_0}^\bullet\left(\M_{\B_j}\prod_\nu\T_\nu^{a_\nu/p^{m+j+1}}\right)\]
for $\alpha\neq0$. Choose the least $i$ with $a_i\neq0$. We have 
\[\gamma_i-1 = (q^{a_i/p^{j+1}}-1)\left[1+(q^{a_i/p^{j+1}}-1)^{-1}(\gamma_i-q^{a_i/p^{j+1}})\right].\] 
To contract the fiber of $\gamma_i-1$ uniformly, as before it suffices to show 
\[\left\| (q^{a_i/p^{j+1}}-1)^{-1}(\gamma_i-q^{a_i/p^{j+1}}) \right\|_{\mathrm{N}}<1.\]
By using the action on $\B_j$ and that $\gamma_i-1$ is $q-1$-adic filtration raising for coefficients (by our choice of $m\gg 0$) we obtain
\[\left\| (q^{a_i/p^{j+1}}-1)^{-1}(\gamma_i-q^{a_i/p^{j+1}}) \right\|_{\mathrm{N}} \leq |q-1|^{(p-1)p^{-j-1}}<1.\]
This gives $(\gamma_i-1)^{-1}$ of norm at most $|q-1|^{-1}$ on each of the summands for $\M_{\B_j}$ where $\alpha \neq 0$. For the full Koszul complex, we can use a similar argument to the previous lemma for $\gamma_i-1$. These homotopies are compatible and have the same bound, so lemma \ref{lem:kedlaya-liu} then gives the vanishing for continuous $\Gamma_0$ cohomology, and Hochschild-Serre gives it for $\Gamma$.
<!-- end proof-47 -->
<!-- remark-13: body_md -->
\label{rem:perf_invar_counter}
It is tempting to try to argue that Lemma \ref{lem:open_decompletion_q_acyclic} would only need to use $\varphi$, as this is the case for ordinary $(\varphi,\Gamma)$ modules using invariance of \'{e}tale $\varphi$-modules under completed perfections. Consider the map
\[\mathrm{A}=k\mathopen{(\mkern-3mu(}q-1\mathclose{)\mkern-3mu)}\langle \T\rangle[1/\T]\to \B=k \mathopen{(\mkern-3mu(}q^{1/p^\infty}-1\mathclose{)\mkern-3mu)}^{\wedge}\langle (\T^\flat)^{1/p^\infty}\rangle[1/\T^\flat],\]
with $\T\mapsto \T^\flat$. If full faithfulness followed just from invariance under this completed perfection, then $\Perf(\mathrm{A})^{\varphi=1}\to \Perf(\B)^{\varphi=1}$ would be fully faithful. By Katz's theorem this would force $\mathrm{H}^1_\ensuremath{\mathrm{\acute{e}t}}(\mathrm{A},\F_p)\to \mathrm{H}^1_\ensuremath{\mathrm{\acute{e}t}}(\B,\F_p)$ to be an isomorphism. One can check that the Artin-Schreier class on $\B$ defined by
\[f=\sum_{n\geq 1}(q-1)^n(\T^\flat)^{-1+1/p^n}\]
is not pulled back from $\mathrm{A}$, so the \'{e}tale cohomology groups are not isomorphic via the natural base change map. The issue here is roughly that passage to $\B$ mixes completed and decompleted perfections.
<!-- end remark-13 -->
<!-- proposition-7: body_md -->
The top horizontal functor in Theorem \ref{thm:open_stratum} is fully faithful.
\label{prop:open_fullfaithful}
<!-- end proposition-7 -->
<!-- proof-48: body_md -->
Lemma \ref{lem:open_stratum_desc} and strict \'{e}tale descent for $\@undefined^{(b)}_{\mathrm{lisse}}((\X_\eta\setminus\@undefined_\eta)_{\ensuremath{\mathrm{pro\acute{e}t}}},\Z_p)$, together with Lemma \ref{lem:strict_etale_local_framing}, reduce the claim to a framed log affine. Lemma \ref{lem:open_crys_gamma_mod} identifies the source with $\Perf(\R_0^{\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\square$}}}}\mathopen{(\mkern-3mu(}q-1\mathclose{)\mkern-3mu)}^{\wedge}_p[1/\T_1,\ldots,1/\T_r]^{\wedge}_p)^{\varphi=1,h\Gamma}$, and Proposition \ref{prop:open_decompletion_hom} makes base change to 
\[\mathbb{A}_{\inf}((\R_0^{\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\square$}}}})_\infty)[1/\xi,1/[\T_1^\flat],\ldots,1/[\T_r^\flat]]^{\wedge}_p\]
fully faithful. Lemma \ref{lem:factorization} supplies a formula for $\T_\ensuremath{\mathrm{\acute{e}t}}$ where this is the first step, and the remaining steps are obviously fully faithful (for example tilting or $\Gamma$-descent) with the exception of analytification.

Thus we must investigate full faithfulness of analytification. Put
\[\U=\Spec (\R_0^{\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\square$}}}})_{\infty,\eta}^{\flat}[1/\T_1^\flat,\ldots,1/\T_r^\flat].\]
For $\mathbb{L},\mathbb{L}'\in \@undefined^{(b)}_{\mathrm{lisse}}(\U_{\ensuremath{\mathrm{\acute{e}t}}},\F_p)$, the monodromy of each $\mathrm{H}^i\underline{\mathrm{RHom}}(\mathbb{L},\mathbb{L}')$ is contained in a finite group $\GL_{m_i}(\F_p)$. Boundedness gives one finite \'{e}tale cover $\U'\to\U$ on which $\mathrm{H}^i\underline{\mathrm{RHom}}(\mathbb{L},\mathbb{L}')\simeq \F_p^{m_i}$ for every $i$. On $\U'$, \cite[Remark 6.2.7]{BhattPadicHodgeNotes} further gives
\[\R\Gamma(\U',\F_p)\xrightarrow{\sim}\R\Gamma(\U'^{\an},\F_p).\]
Finally, a Postnikov d\'{e}vissage combined with finite \'{e}tale descent to trivialize coefficients to $\F_p$ gives full faithfulness modulo $p$; derived Nakayama then gives full faithfulness of analytification.
<!-- end proof-48 -->
<!-- proposition-8: body_md -->
Let $(\Spf \R,\mathcal{M})$ be a framed log affine with coordinates $\T_1,\ldots,\T_r$, and let $\mathrm{N}$ be prime to $p$. Put
\[\R_\mathrm{N}=\R\langle \mathrm{S}_1,\ldots,\mathrm{S}_r\rangle/(\mathrm{S}_1^\mathrm{N}-\T_1,\ldots,\mathrm{S}_r^\mathrm{N}-\T_r),\]
and equip $\Spf \R_\mathrm{N}$ with the log structure $\mathcal{M}_{\mathrm{N}}$ induced by $\V(\mathrm{S}_1\cdots \mathrm{S}_{r})$. Then
\[\left(\Perf((\Spf \R_{\mathrm{N}},\mathcal{M}_{\mathrm{N}})_{\mathbbl{\Delta}},\ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}[1/\I_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}]_p^{\wedge}(\ast \@undefined_{\mathrm{N}}))^{\varphi=1,\op}\right)^{h\mu_{\mathrm{N}}^r} \simeq \Perf((\Spf \R,\mathcal{M})_{\mathbbl{\Delta}},\ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}[1/\I_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}]_p^{\wedge}(\ast \@undefined))^{\varphi=1,\op}.\]
\label{prop:open_strat_Kum_desc}
<!-- end proposition-8 -->
<!-- proof-49: body_md -->
Let $f_{\mathrm{N}}:(\Spf \R_{\mathrm{N}},\mathcal{M}_{\mathrm{N}})\to(\Spf\R,\mathcal{M})$ be natural map of log formal schemes, where as above $\R_\mathrm{N}=\R\langle \mathrm{S}_1,\ldots,\mathrm{S}_r\rangle/(\mathrm{S}_1^\mathrm{N}-\T_1,\ldots,\mathrm{S}_r^\mathrm{N}-\T_r)$. Since $f_{\mathrm{N}}^*\@undefined=\mathrm{N}\@undefined_{\mathrm{N}}$, there is a canonical equivalence
\[f_{\mathrm{N}}^*\ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}[1/\I_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}]_p^{\wedge}(\ast\@undefined) \simeq \ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}[1/\I_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}]_p^{\wedge}(\ast(\mathrm{N}\@undefined_{\mathrm{N}})) \simeq \ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}[1/\I_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}]_p^{\wedge}(\ast\@undefined_{\mathrm{N}}).\]
Thus pullback induces a functor on the corresponding module categories
\[\Perf((\Spf \R,\mathcal{M})_{\mathbbl{\Delta}},\ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}[1/\I_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}]_p^{\wedge}(\ast \@undefined))^{\varphi=1,\op} \longrightarrow \Perf((\Spf \R_{\mathrm{N}},\mathcal{M}_{\mathrm{N}})_{\mathbbl{\Delta}},\ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}[1/\I_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}]_p^{\wedge}(\ast \@undefined_{\mathrm{N}}))^{\varphi=1,\op}.\]
we will use to induce the desired equivalence.

The claim becomes more transparent when we write out the \v{C}ech nerves for the source and target. Base changing  the framing for $(\Spf \R,\mathcal{M})$ along $\T_i\mapsto\mathrm{S}_i^{\mathrm{N}}$ gives $(\Spf \R_{\mathrm{N}},\mathcal{M}_{\mathrm{N}})$ a framing $\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\square$}}}_{\mathrm{N}}$, so it also has an associated $q$-de Rham prism. Let $\mathrm{A} = \R_0^{\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\square$}}}}\mathopen{(\mkern-3mu(}q-1\mathclose{)\mkern-3mu)}_p^{\wedge}$, and $\mathrm{A}_{\mathrm{N}} = \R_{0,\mathrm{N}}^{\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\square$}}}_{\mathrm{N}}}\mathopen{(\mkern-3mu(}q-1\mathclose{)\mkern-3mu)}_p^{\wedge}$ be their corresponding (Laurentized) log $q$-de Rham prisms. As usual we write $\mathrm{A}^{(s)}$ and $\mathrm{A}_{\mathrm{N}}^{(s)}$ for the Laurentized \v{C}ech nerves. We write for $\mathrm{A}^{(s)}(\ast \@undefined)$ and $\mathrm{A}_{\mathrm{N}}^{(s)}(\ast \@undefined)$ for the evaluations of $\ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}[1/\I_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}]_p^{\wedge}(\ast \@undefined)$ on these prisms. 

We then obtain the following diagram:
\begin{display}
\Perf(\mathrm{A}_{\mathrm{N}}(\ast \@undefined_{\mathrm{N}}))^{\varphi=1} \ar[shift left]{r} \ar[shift right]{r} & \Perf(\mathrm{A}_{\mathrm{N}}^{(1)}(\ast \@undefined_{\mathrm{N}}))^{\varphi=1} \ar[shift left=2]{r} \ar{r} \ar[shift right=2]{r} & \Perf(\mathrm{A}_{\mathrm{N}}^{(2)}(\ast \@undefined_{\mathrm{N}}))^{\varphi=1} \ar[shift left]{r} \ar[shift right]{r} \ar[shift left=3]{r} \ar[shift right=3]{r} & \cdots \\

\Perf(\mathrm{A}(\ast \@undefined))^{\varphi=1} \ar{u} \ar[shift left]{r} \ar[shift right]{r} & \Perf(\mathrm{A}^{(1)}(\ast \@undefined))^{\varphi=1} \ar{u} \ar[shift left=2]{r} \ar{r} \ar[shift right=2]{r} & \Perf(\mathrm{A}^{(2)}(\ast \@undefined))^{\varphi=1} \ar{u} \ar[shift left]{r} \ar[shift right]{r} \ar[shift left=3]{r} \ar[shift right=3]{r} & \cdots 
\end{display}
The rings on top all have a grading by $\alpha \in (\Z/\mathrm{N} \Z)^r$, making $\Perf$ acquire an action of $\mu_{\mathrm{N}}^r$ \footnote{We also need the condition $\R_{\alpha} \cdot \R_\beta \subseteq \R_{\alpha + \beta}$ for $\alpha,\beta \in (\Z/\mathrm{N}\Z)^r$ for a general ring $\R$, which is satisfied here.}. For example, $\R_{0,\mathrm{N}}^{\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\square$}}}_{\mathrm{N}}}=\R_0^{\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\square$}}}}\langle \mathrm{S}_1,\ldots,\mathrm{S}_r\rangle/(\mathrm{S}_1^\mathrm{N}-\T_1,\ldots,\mathrm{S}_r^\mathrm{N}-\T_r)$, so 
\[\mathrm{A}_{\mathrm{N}}(\ast \@undefined) = \bigoplus_{\alpha \in (\Z/\mathrm{N} \Z)^r} \mathrm{A}(\ast \@undefined) \cdot \mathrm{S}^{\alpha},\]
with the $\alpha=0$ component being the natural inclusion of $\mathrm{A}(\ast \@undefined)$. For the first \v{C}ech term, the analogous grading induced from the one on $\R_{0,\mathrm{N}}^{\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\square$}}}_{\mathrm{N}}}$ again holds, even at the level of $\mathrm{A}_{\mathrm{N}}^{+,(1)}$ and $\mathrm{A}^{+,(1)}$. We see this by noting that the elements $v_i = \mathrm{S}_{i,1}/\mathrm{S}_{i,0}$ we adjoin (in the notation of Lemma \ref{lem:qdr_actual_cech_envelope}; for $\mathrm{A}_{\mathrm{N}}^{+,(1)}$ we use $v_i$ rather than $u_i$ to distinguish them) satisfies $v_i=(\mathrm{S}_{i,1}/\mathrm{S}_{i,0})=(\T_{i,1}/\T_{i,0})^{1/\mathrm{N}} = u_i^{1/\mathrm{N}} \in \mathrm{A}^{+,(1)}$ since $\mathrm{N}$ is prime to $p$. Indeed
\[u_i^{1/\mathrm{N}} = \sum_{k\ge 0} \binom{1/\mathrm{N}}{k} (u_i-1)^k,\]
which converges $(p,[p]_q)$-adically since we force $u_i-1\in [p]_q \mathrm{A}^{+,(1)}$. For higher \v{C}ech terms, the claim is clear because they are obtained from iterated tensor products of $\mathrm{A}^{+,(1)}$ over $\mathrm{A}^+$ (and similarly for $\mathrm{A}_{\mathrm{N}}$).

Even better, here
\[\mathrm{A}^{(s)}(\ast \@undefined) \longrightarrow \mathrm{A}_{\mathrm{N}}^{(s)}(\ast \@undefined_{\mathrm{N}})\]
is a finite \'{e}tale $\mu_{\mathrm{N}}^r$ torsor. Indeed, since we have $p$-completely inverted $\T_1,\ldots, \T_r$ and $\mathrm{S}_1,\ldots,\mathrm{S}_r$ the map becomes finite \'{e}tale.

It therefore follows that $\Perf(\mathrm{A}^{(s)}(\ast \@undefined))^{\varphi=1} \simeq \Perf(\mathrm{A}_{\mathrm{N}}^{(s)}(\ast \@undefined_{\mathrm{N}}))^{\varphi=1,h\mu_{\mathrm{N}}^r}$ by finite \'{e}tale descent, noting that the $\mu_{\mathrm{N}}^r$ action commutes with $\varphi$. The claim then follows as these equivalences are compatible with the maps in the \v{C}ech nerve.
<!-- end proof-49 -->
<!-- corollary-5: body_md -->
The top horizontal functor in Theorem \ref{thm:open_stratum} is an equivalence.
<!-- end corollary-5 -->
<!-- proof-50: body_md -->
By Proposition \ref{prop:open_fullfaithful}, it only remains to prove essential surjectivity. Since $\X_\eta$ is quasicompact and smooth, any $\mathbb{L}\in \@undefined^{(b)}_{\mathrm{lisse}}((\X_\eta\setminus\@undefined_\eta)_{\ensuremath{\mathrm{pro\acute{e}t}}},\Z_p)$ is actually globally bounded rather than simply locally bounded. Thus for the purpose of showing essential surjectivity, since $\mathbb{L}\in\@undefined^{(b)}_{\mathrm{lisse}}((\X_\eta\setminus\@undefined_\eta)_{\ensuremath{\mathrm{pro\acute{e}t}}},\Z_p)^\ensuremath\heartsuit$ generate bounded objects under shifts and fibers and the functor is exact we only need essential surjectivity on the heart. Moreover, by strict \'{e}tale descent we may also reduce to testing the equivalence when $(\X,\mathcal{M})$ is a framed log affine.

By the previous discussion it will then suffice to directly construct a preimage 
\[\mathcal{E} \in \Perf((\X,\mathcal{M})_{\mathbbl{\Delta}},\ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}[1/\I_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}]_p^{\wedge}(\ast \@undefined))^{\varphi=1,\op}\] 
so for such an $\mathbb{L}$ we get $\T_\ensuremath{\mathrm{\acute{e}t}}(\mathcal{E})=j_! \mathbb{L}$. By \cite[Corollary 6.3.4]{DiaoLanLiuZhuLogAdic}, $\mathbb{L}^{\mathrm{ext}}:=j_{\mathrm{k\acute{e}t},*}\mathbb{L}$ is a Kummer-\'{e}tale $\Z_p$-local system on the log generic fiber. We want to argue there is a single prime-to-$p$ Kummer cover $f_{\mathrm{N}}:(\X_{\mathrm{N}},\mathcal{M}_{\mathrm{N}})\to(\X,\mathcal{M})$ as in Proposition \ref{prop:open_strat_Kum_desc} such that $f_{\mathrm{N}}^*\mathbb{L}^{\mathrm{ext}}$ is $p$-Kummer. Without loss of generality we assume $(\Spf \R,\mathcal{M})_{\eta}$ is connected, as we can take the least common multiple of such $\mathrm{N}$ on each component. By \cite[Definition 4]{KoshikawaYaoCorrigendum} we want to show that if $\bar{x}$ is a log geometric point of $(\Spf \R,\mathcal{M})_\eta$ and $(\Spf \R,\mathcal{M})_{\eta,\bar{x}}$ denotes strict localization (at the underlying geometric point) with the induced log structure then
\[\pi_1^{\mathrm{k}\ensuremath{\mathrm{\acute{e}t}}}((\Spf \R,\mathcal{M})_{\eta,\bar{x}}, \bar{x}) \xlongrightarrow{\rho} \mathrm{Aut}_{\Z_p}(\mathbb{L}^{\mathrm{ext}}_{\bar{x}})\]
has pro-$p$ image after pullback along $f_{\mathrm{N}}$ for some $\mathrm{N}$. Here $\rho$ is the associated representation to $\mathbb{L}^{\mathrm{ext}}$. The key observation is that $\mathrm{Aut}_{\Z_p}(\mathbb{L}^{\mathrm{ext}}_{\bar{x}}) \to \GL_n(\F_p)$ has pro-$p$ kernel, where $n$ is the rank of the mod $p$ reduction of $\mathbb{L}$ (which makes sense by connectedness). Thus to obtain a pro-$p$ image we can take $\mathrm{N}$ to be the prime-to-$p$ part of $|\GL_n(\F_p)|$, as the effect of pullback along $f_{\mathrm{N}}$ takes $\mathrm{N}$th powers in the image (see the proof of Proposition 5 in \cite{KoshikawaYaoCorrigendum}).

Thus we may assume $f_{\mathrm{N}}^*\mathbb{L}^{\mathrm{ext}}$ is $p$-Kummer. By the contravariant version of \cite[Theorem 7]{KoshikawaYaoCorrigendum} we have an equivalence
\[\Perf((\X_{\mathrm{N}},\mathcal{M}_{\mathrm{N}})_{\mathbbl{\Delta}},\ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}[1/\I_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}]_p^{\wedge})^{\varphi=1,\op} \simeq \@undefined^{(b),\mathrm{pKum}}_{\mathrm{lisse}}((\X_{\mathrm{N}},\mathcal{M}_{\mathrm{N}})_\eta,\Z_p),\] 
therefore $f_{\mathrm{N}}^*\mathbb{L}^{\mathrm{ext}}$ has a corresponding perfect Laurent $\mathrm{F}$-crystal $\mathcal{E}$ on $(\X_{\mathrm{N}},\mathcal{M}_{\mathrm{N}})_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}$, or that $\T_\ensuremath{\mathrm{\acute{e}t}}(\mathcal{E})\simeq f_{\mathrm{N}}^*\mathbb{L}^{\mathrm{ext}}$.

Let $j_{\mathrm{N}}:\X_{\mathrm{N},\eta}\setminus\@undefined_{\mathrm{N},\eta}\hookrightarrow(\X_{\mathrm{N}},\mathcal{M}_{\mathrm{N}})_\eta$ denote the inclusion. Since $\T_\ensuremath{\mathrm{\acute{e}t}}(\ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}[1/\I_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}]_p^{\wedge}(\ast \@undefined_{\mathrm{N}}))\simeq j_{\mathrm{N},!}\Z_p$ using Lemma \ref{lem:factorization} and $\T_\ensuremath{\mathrm{\acute{e}t}}$ is symmetric monoidal (from Remark \ref{rem:Tet_sym_mon}) we deduce
\[\T_\ensuremath{\mathrm{\acute{e}t}}(\mathcal{E}\otimes\ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}[1/\I_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}]_p^{\wedge}(\ast \@undefined_{\mathrm{N}}))\simeq j_{\mathrm{N},!}f_{\mathrm{N}}^*\mathbb{L}.\]
On the $p$-Kummer-\'{e}tale side of the Koshikawa-Yao correspondence, $f_{\mathrm{N}}^*\mathbb{L}^{\mathrm{ext}}$ by descent comes equipped with an action of $\mu_{\mathrm{N}}^r$, which then extends to $\mathcal{E}\otimes\ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}[1/\I_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}]_p^{\wedge}(\ast \@undefined_{\mathrm{N}})$ (noting $\ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}[1/\I_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}]_p^{\wedge}(\ast \@undefined_{\mathrm{N}})$ has its own $\mu_{\mathrm{N}}^r$-action). Using Proposition \ref{prop:open_strat_Kum_desc} gives a descended crystal that realizes $j_!\mathbb{L}$, which we know by virtue of having a $\mu_{\mathrm{N}}^r$-equivariant map upstairs and pullback compatibility.
<!-- end proof-50 -->
<!-- lemma-32: body_md -->
\label{lem:thick_equiv_criterion}
Let $\mathrm{F}: \mathcal{C} \longrightarrow \mathcal{D}$ be an exact functor between idempotent complete stable $\infty$-categories which are thickly generated by objects $\{\mathrm{C}_{i}\}_{i\in \I}$ and $\{\@undefined_i\}_{i\in \I}$, such that $\mathrm{F}(\mathrm{C}_i)=\@undefined_i$ and the morphism 
\[\RHom(\mathrm{C}_i,\mathrm{C}_j) \longrightarrow \RHom(\@undefined_i,\@undefined_j)\]  
induced by $\mathrm{F}$ is an equivalence for any $i,j\in \I$. Then $\mathrm{F}$ is an equivalence.
<!-- end lemma-32 -->
<!-- proof-51: body_md -->
The objects $\mathrm{C}\in \mathcal{C}$ such that $\RHom(\mathrm{C}_i,\mathrm{C}) \longrightarrow \RHom(\@undefined_i,\mathrm{F}(\mathrm{C}))$ is an equivalence form a thick subcategory containing the $\mathrm{C}_i$, hence all of $\mathcal{C}$. Similarly we can run this argument in the other variable, deducing $\mathrm{F}$ is fully faithful. Showing essential surjectivity is then straightforward, as the essential image is a thick subcategory containing the $\@undefined_i$ hence all of $\mathcal{D}$. Here we have used idempotent completeness of $\mathcal{C}$ to ensure the essential image is closed under retracts.
<!-- end proof-51 -->
<!-- lemma-33: body_md -->
\label{lem:ket_thick_gens}
Let $(\Spf \R,\mathcal{M})$ be a framed log affine. The category $\@undefined^{(b),\mathrm{pKum}}_{\cons,\@undefined}((\Spf \R,\mathcal{M})_\eta,\Z_p)$ is thickly generated by $j_{\Lambda,!}\mathbb{L}$ for $\mathbb{L}$ a $p$-Kummer sheaf in $\@undefined^{(b)}_{\mathrm{lisse}}((\Spf \R,\mathcal{M})_{\Lambda,\eta},\Z_p)$, where
\[j_{\Lambda}: (\Spf \R,\mathcal{M})_{\Lambda,\eta} \hookrightarrow (\X,\mathcal{M})_\eta\]
is the inclusion of the stratum for $\Lambda \subseteq \{1,\ldots,r\}$.
<!-- end lemma-33 -->
<!-- proof-52: body_md -->
Inductively apply the localization triangle
\[j_! j^* \mathscr{F} \longrightarrow \mathscr{F} \longrightarrow i_* i^* \mathscr{F}\]
for an open/closed stratification ($j$ being the open inclusion, $i$ the closed inclusion). Repeating this produces $\mathscr{F}$ in terms of the thick generators. It is worth pointing out that in this procedure $p$-Kummer sheaves are closed under extensions, since invariants for $\I_{\bar{x}}^{\log,(p)'}$ are exact (due to this being the prime-to-$p$ part).
<!-- end proof-52 -->
<!-- lemma-34: body_md -->
\label{lem:kashiwara}
Let $(\Spf \R,\mathcal{M})$ be a framed log affine, and as usual put $\mathrm{A}=\R_0^{\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\square$}}}}\mathopen{(\mkern-3mu(}q-1\mathclose{)\mkern-3mu)}^{\wedge}_p$ and fix $\Lambda \subset \{1,\ldots,r\}$. We put $\mathrm{J}_{\Lambda} = (\T_i)_{i\in \Lambda}$.

Then there is an equivalence
\[i^!:=\left((\mathrm{A}/\mathrm{J}_{\Lambda})\otimes^{\mathrm{L}}_{\mathrm{A}}-\right)[-|\Lambda|]: \@undefined_{\fgu}(\mathrm{A})^{h\Gamma}_{\mathrm{J}_{\Lambda}}\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\@undefined_{\fgu}(\mathrm{A}/\mathrm{J}_{\Lambda})^{h\Gamma}\]
<!-- end lemma-34 -->
<!-- proof-53: body_md -->
Put $\overline{\mathrm{A}}=\mathrm{A}/p$ and $\overline{\mathrm{J}}_{\Lambda}=\mathrm{J}_{\Lambda}\overline{\mathrm{A}}$. The categories and functor above satisfy the hypotheses of Lemma \ref{lem:categorical_nakayama}; the support condition is detected modulo $p$ by derived Nakayama. It is therefore enough to prove that
\[i^!:=\left((\overline{\mathrm{A}}/\overline{\mathrm{J}}_{\Lambda})\otimes^{\mathrm{L},\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\blacksquare$}}}}_{\overline{\mathrm{A}}}-\right)[-|\Lambda|]:\@undefined_{\fgu}(\overline{\mathrm{A}})_{\overline{\mathrm{J}}_{\Lambda}}^{h\Gamma}\longrightarrow\@undefined_{\fgu}(\overline{\mathrm{A}}/\overline{\mathrm{J}}_{\Lambda})^{h\Gamma}\]
is an equivalence. The functor is well-defined: one can use Lemma \ref{lem:derived_stratum_fgu}, and in particular $i^!$ is $\Gamma$-equivariant.

In this case, the functor $i^!$ is an equivalence \textit{before} we apply $(-)^{h\Gamma}$. One may use the proof of \cite[Corollary 5.11.3]{EmertonKisin2} to the present regular $\mathrm{F}$-finite situation (noting we have access to important ingredients like roots by \cite{BlickleGamma}). Thus one obtains an adjoint equivalence
\[i_+:\@undefined_{\fgu}(\overline{\mathrm{A}}/\overline{\mathrm{J}}_{\Lambda}) \rightleftarrows \@undefined_{\fgu}(\overline{\mathrm{A}})_{\overline{\mathrm{J}}_{\Lambda}}: i^!.\]
This survives after applying a cobar construction $(-)^{h\Gamma}$ to both sides, because evaluation on the degree zero term is conservative. Thus one may test $i^! i_+ \simeq \id$ and $i_+ i^! \simeq \id$ after evaluation on the degree zero term, at which point it reduces to the ordinary Kashiwara lemma for finitely generated unit modules.
<!-- end proof-53 -->
<!-- corollary-6: body_md -->
\label{cor:thick_gen_embedding}
The following diagram commutes:
\begin{display}
\Perf(\mathrm{A}_{\Lambda})^{h\Gamma,\varphi=1,\op} \ar{d}{\T_\ensuremath{\mathrm{\acute{e}t}}} \ar{r}{j_{\Lambda,!}} & \@undefined_{\fgu}(\mathrm{A})^{h\Gamma,\op} \ar{d}{\T_\ensuremath{\mathrm{\acute{e}t}}} \\
\@undefined^{(b),\mathrm{pKum}}_{\mathrm{lisse}}((\Spf \R,\mathcal{M})_{\Lambda,\eta},\Z_p) \ar{r}{j_{\Lambda,!}[-|\Lambda|]} & \@undefined^{(b),\mathrm{pKum}}_{\cons,\@undefined}((\Spf \R,\mathcal{M})_\eta,\Z_p)
\end{display}
On the right $\T_\ensuremath{\mathrm{\acute{e}t}}$ is passed through the equivalence of Theorem \ref{thm:qdR_crys_Gamma_mod}, which may then be explicitly computed via Lemma \ref{lem:factorization}.
<!-- end corollary-6 -->
<!-- proof-54: body_md -->
This is more or less clear by construction from Lemma \ref{lem:factorization}, by expanding what the square means:
\begin{display}
\Perf(\mathrm{A}_{\Lambda})^{h\Gamma,\varphi=1,\op} \ar[out=180,in=180,looseness=2,start anchor=west,end anchor=west,swap]{dd}{\T_\ensuremath{\mathrm{\acute{e}t}}} \ar{d}{\T_\ensuremath{\mathrm{\acute{e}t}}^{\perf}} \ar{r}{j_{\Lambda,!}} & \@undefined_{\fgu}(\mathrm{A})^{h\Gamma,\op} \ar{d}{\T_\ensuremath{\mathrm{\acute{e}t}}^{\perf}} \ar[out=0,in=0,looseness=2,start anchor=east,end anchor=east]{dd}{\T_\ensuremath{\mathrm{\acute{e}t}}} \\ 
\@undefined^{(b)}_{\mathrm{lisse}}(\Spec (\R_0^{\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\square$}}}})_{\infty,\Lambda,\eta}^{\flat},\Z_p)^{h\Gamma} \ar{d}{\mathrm{an}_\Gamma^*} \ar{r}{j_{\Lambda,!}[-|\Lambda|]} & \@undefined^b_{\mathrm{cons}, \@undefined_\infty}(\Spec (\R_0^{\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\square$}}}})_{\infty,\eta}^{\flat},\Z_p)^{h\Gamma} \ar{d}{\mathrm{an}_\Gamma^*} \\
\@undefined^{(b),\mathrm{pKum}}_{\mathrm{lisse}}((\Spf \R,\mathcal{M})_{\Lambda,\eta},\Z_p) \ar{r}{j_{\Lambda,!}[-|\Lambda|]} & \@undefined^{(b),\mathrm{pKum}}_{\cons,\@undefined}((\Spf \R,\mathcal{M})_\eta,\Z_p).
\end{display}
Here $\Spec (\R_0^{\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\square$}}}})_{\infty,\Lambda,\eta}^{\flat}$ similarly means that we take the reduced ring where $\T_i^{\flat} = 0$ for $i\in \Lambda$, and invert them for $i\not \in \Lambda$ (note this is not a perfectoid ring). By abuse of notation we base change to the perfection first and then apply $\T_\ensuremath{\mathrm{\acute{e}t}}^\perf$ -- more precisely, in Lemma \ref{lem:factorization} we have denoted the composite of the first two arrows by simply $\T_\ensuremath{\mathrm{\acute{e}t}}^{\perf}$.

The bottom square is commutative, so we reduce to checking commutativity of the top square. This is clear for the first component of
\[j_{\Lambda,!}: \Perf(\mathrm{A}_{\Lambda})^{h\Gamma,\varphi=1,\op} \hookrightarrow \@undefined_{\fgu}(\mathrm{A}/\mathrm{J}_{\Lambda})^{h\Gamma,\op} \xrightarrow{i_+} \@undefined_{\fgu}(\mathrm{A})^{h\Gamma,\op}\]
so we reduce to studying compatibility for $i_+$.

One can further reduce to checking this modulo $p$ by derived Nakayama, as there is already a morphism we can test is an equivalence to witness commutativity. Indeed for the closed part $i_+$ of our construction of $j_{\Lambda,!}$ there is a map
\[\T^{\perf}_\ensuremath{\mathrm{\acute{e}t}}(i_+ \M) \longrightarrow i_* i^* \T^{\perf}_\ensuremath{\mathrm{\acute{e}t}}(i_+ \M) \longrightarrow i_* \T^{\perf}_\ensuremath{\mathrm{\acute{e}t}}(\mathrm{A}/\mathrm{J}_{\Lambda} \otimes^{\mathrm{L}}_{\mathrm{A}} i_+ \M) = i_* \T^{\perf}_\ensuremath{\mathrm{\acute{e}t}}(\M)[-|\Lambda|].\]
This is then not too difficult, because one can see that for the deperfected Emerton-Kisin solution functor of \cite{EmertonKisin2} one has for $\M \in \Perf(\overline{\mathrm{A}}_{\Lambda})^{h\Gamma,\varphi=1}$ that
\[\mathrm{RSol}(i_+ \M) = i_* \mathrm{RSol}(\M)[-|\Lambda|],\]
compatibly with the $\Gamma$-action. On the left we use the solution functor for $\@undefined_{\fgu}(\overline{\mathrm{A}})$ and on the right for $\@undefined_{\fgu}(\overline{\mathrm{A}}/\mathrm{J}_{\Lambda})^{h\Gamma}$. By adjunction one can reduce the check to one for $i^!$ (revealing the source of the shift).

For the comparison we actually needed to work with $\T_\ensuremath{\mathrm{\acute{e}t}}^{\perf}$, but base changing to $\Spec (\R_0^{\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\square$}}}})_{\infty,\eta}^{\flat}$ preserves this identity.
<!-- end proof-54 -->
<!-- proposition-9: body_md -->
\label{prop:thick_gen_equiv}
The functor
\[\T_\ensuremath{\mathrm{\acute{e}t}}: \Perf(\mathrm{A}_{\Lambda})^{h\Gamma,\varphi=1,\op} \longrightarrow \@undefined^{(b),\mathrm{pKum}}_{\mathrm{lisse}}((\Spf \R,\mathcal{M})_{\Lambda,\eta},\Z_p)\]
is an equivalence.
<!-- end proposition-9 -->
<!-- proof-55: body_md -->
We first check the case $|\Lambda|=r$, which we will explain in full detail. Here this is because the corresponding stratum on the log adic generic fiber is an ordinary framed affine $\mathrm{Z}=\bigcap_{i=1}^r \@undefined_i$ over a rank $n-r$ torus with a rank $r$ hollow log structure. Equipping the target torus with the hollow chart $\N^r\to0$, we get an induced strict \'{e}tale framing
\[\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\square$}}}:(\mathrm{Z},\mathcal{M}|_{\mathrm{Z}})\longrightarrow\left(\Spf \W(k)[\zeta_p]\langle \T_{r+1}^\pm,\ldots,\T_n^\pm\rangle,(\N^r\to0)^a\right).\]
The torus has a natural perfectoid cover $\Spf \W(k)^{\mathrm{cyc}} \langle \T_{r+1}^{\pm 1/p^\infty}, \ldots, \T_n^{\pm 1/p^\infty} \rangle$ with hollow log structure $\N[1/p]^r\to 0$, so using $\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\square$}}}$ we obtain an associated perfectoid cover $(\R_0^{\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\square$}}}})_{\infty,\mathrm{Z}}[1/p]$ again with the chart $\N[1/p]^r\to 0$; we let $(\mathrm{A}/\mathrm{J}_{\Lambda})_\perf$ denote $\mathbb{A}_{\inf}((\R_0^{\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\square$}}}})_{\infty,\mathrm{Z}}[1/p])$. Katz's theorem, tilting, and pro-Kummer-\'{e}tale descent for the same full group $\Gamma$ give
\[\left(\Perf((\mathrm{A}/\mathrm{J}_{\Lambda})_\perf)^{\varphi=1,h\Gamma}\right)^\op\xrightarrow{\sim}\@undefined^{(b),\mathrm{pKum}}_{\mathrm{lisse}}\left(\left(\mathrm{Z},\N^r\right)_\eta,\Z_p\right) \xhookrightarrow{i_*} \@undefined^{(b)}_{\cons,\@undefined}((\Spf \R,\mathcal{M})_\eta, \Z_p).\]
In this case the finitely generated unit condition is equivalent to being perfect with unit Frobenius by the proof of Proposition \ref{prop:perfectoid_constructibility}. Moreover,
\[\@undefined_{\fgu}(\mathrm{A}/\mathrm{J}_{\Lambda})^{h\Gamma}\simeq\Perf((\mathrm{A}/\mathrm{J}_{\Lambda})_\perf)^{\varphi=1,h\Gamma}\]
by \cite[Proposition 3.6]{BhattScholzePrismaticFCrystals} and Lemma \ref{lem:categorical_nakayama}; thus the desired claim follows. We note Lemma \ref{lem:factorization} identifies this construction with $\T_\ensuremath{\mathrm{\acute{e}t}}$.

In the remaining cases where $|\Lambda|$ is smaller we must involve part of the open stratum theorem, but fortunately the hard work has already been done. The result we need is that
\[\Perf(\mathrm{A}_{\Lambda})^{h\Gamma,\varphi=1,\op} \xlongrightarrow{\sim} \@undefined^{(b),\mathrm{pKum}}_{\mathrm{lisse}}((\Spf \R,\mathcal{M})_{\Lambda,\eta},\Z_p),\]
where the target has its natural hollow pullback log structure. The equivalence on the open stratum tells us that there is an equivalence
\[\Perf(\mathrm{A}_{\Lambda})^{h\Gamma',\varphi=1,\op} \xlongrightarrow{\sim} \@undefined_{\mathrm{lisse}}^{(b)}((\Spf \R)_{\Lambda,\eta},\Z_p)\]
where on the right we use the trivial log structure and $\Gamma'$ is the quotient $(1+p\Z_p) \ltimes \Z_p(1)^{n-|\Lambda|}$. We can check the equivalence modulo $p$ by Lemma \ref{lem:categorical_nakayama}. Full faithfulness can be done through exactly the same argument as Theorem \ref{thm:open_stratum}. The only nontrivial point is to note that adding hollow directions to Proposition \ref{prop:open_decompletion_hom} does not affect the reduction argument. Moreover in the helper lemmas, since we work modulo $p$ by increasing the parameter $m$ we can make the hollow part act trivially after shrinking it. This follows because the action of $\Z_p(1)^{|\Lambda|}$ factors through a finite $p$-group modulo $p$. This follows on $\Vect(\overline{\mathrm{A}}_{\Lambda})^{h\Gamma,\varphi=1,\op}$ by using Katz's correspondence from \cite[Proposition 3.4]{BhattScholzePrismaticFCrystals}, so it amounts to the result that an $\F_p$ local system on a regular affine $\F_p$-scheme has a finite dimensional vector space of endomorphisms (and $\Z_p(1)^{|\Lambda|}$ acts by such endomorphisms). The hollow directions will then not affect the remainder of the argument, which can be carried out in the same way.

With full faithfulness in hand, essential surjectivity is easier. Objects in $\@undefined_{\mathrm{lisse}}^{(b)}((\Spf \R)_{\Lambda,\eta},\F_p)$ can be regarded as ones in $\@undefined^{(b),\mathrm{pKum}}_{\mathrm{lisse}}((\Spf \R,\mathcal{M})_{\Lambda,\eta},\F_p)$ where hollow log inertia acts trivially. We will roughly argue that these thickly generate to deduce essential surjectivity.

The key point is again that $\Z_p(1)^{|\Lambda|}$ acts on a finite dimensional $\F_p$-vector space $\V$ through a finite $p$-group $\mathrm{H}$, giving a finite filtration where the action on graded pieces is trivial. To construct this filtration we repeatedly use that fact that because $\mathrm{H}$ is a finite $p$-group we always have $\V^\mathrm{H} \neq 0$ for nonzero $\V$; this can be seen by applying the orbit-stabilizer theorem. We can filter an $\mathrm{H}$-representation $\V$ as follows: start with $0\subset \Fil^1 \V=\V^\mathrm{H}$, and then use the exact sequence
\[0 \longrightarrow \V^\mathrm{H} \longrightarrow \Fil^2 \V \longrightarrow (\V/\V^\mathrm{H})^\mathrm{H} \longrightarrow 0\]
of $\mathrm{H}$-representations, where $\Fil^2 \V \subseteq \V$ is the preimage of $(\V/\V^\mathrm{H})^\mathrm{H}$ under $\pi: \V \to \V/\V^\mathrm{H}$. Using the same fact, $(\V/\V^\mathrm{H})^\mathrm{H}\neq 0$. Continuing in this manner, since $\dim_{\F_p} \V$ is finite we get a finite $\mathrm{H}$-equivariant filtration $\Fil^\bullet \V$ where graded pieces have a trivial action by $\mathrm{H}$. In our situation $\V$ is actually a representation of the larger group in $\pi_1^{\ensuremath{\mathrm{k\acute{e}t}}}((\Spf \R,\mathcal{M})_{\Lambda,\eta},\bar{x})$, but since $\Z_p(1)^{|\Lambda|}$ is normal in $\pi_1^{\ensuremath{\mathrm{k\acute{e}t}}}((\Spf \R,\mathcal{M})_{\Lambda,\eta},x)$ via
\[1 \longrightarrow \widehat{\Z}(1)^{|\Lambda|} \longrightarrow \pi_1^{\ensuremath{\mathrm{k\acute{e}t}}}((\Spf \R,\mathcal{M})_{\Lambda,\eta},\bar{x}) \longrightarrow \pi_1^{\ensuremath{\mathrm{\acute{e}t}}}((\Spf \R)_{\Lambda,\eta},\bar{x}) \longrightarrow 1\]
