this argument yields a finite filtration $\Fil^\bullet \V$ for $p$-Kummer $\V \in \Rep_{\F_p}^{\mathrm{fin}}(\pi_1^{\ensuremath{\mathrm{k\acute{e}t}}}((\Spf \R,\mathcal{M})_{\Lambda,\eta},\bar{x}))$ with associated graded pieces in $\Rep_{\F_p}^{\mathrm{fin}}(\pi_1^{\ensuremath{\mathrm{\acute{e}t}}}((\Spf \R)_{\Lambda,\eta},\bar{x}))$.\footnote{Recall $p$-Kummer means that the prime-to-$p$ part $\widehat{\Z}^{(p)'}(1)^{|\Lambda|}$ already acts trivially.} Using derived full faithfulness, this filtration suffices to show all such $p$-Kummer $\V$ are in the essential image. By a Postnikov d\'{e}vissage we reduce to essential surjectivity in the heart, so the claim follows.
<!-- end proof-55 -->
<!-- remark-14: body_md -->
We can also argue essential surjectivity just as in the proof of Theorem \ref{thm:open_stratum} using $\mu_{\mathrm{N}}^{r-|\Lambda|}$ descent after taking a prime-to-$p$ Kummer cover. To make this fully rigorous requires dealing with more technical details than above, however, which is why we have not used this argument.
<!-- end remark-14 -->
<!-- lemma-35: body_md -->
\label{lem:crys_thick_gens}
Let $(\Spf \R,\mathcal{M})$ be a framed log affine. The category $\@undefined_{\fgu}(\mathrm{A})^{h\Gamma}$ is thickly generated by $j_{\Lambda,!}\M_\Lambda$ for $\M_\Lambda\in \Perf(\mathrm{A}_{\Lambda})^{h\Gamma,\varphi=1}$.
<!-- end lemma-35 -->
<!-- proof-56: body_md -->
Similar to Lemma \ref{lem:ket_thick_gens}, we need to produce analogous triangles extracting open and closed parts. Let $\M \in \@undefined_{\fgu}(\mathrm{A})^{h\Gamma}$.

For an irreducible component $\@undefined_i$ in $\@undefined$, there is an exact triangle
\[\mathrm{R}\Gamma_{\@undefined_i}(\M) \longrightarrow \M \longrightarrow \M(\ast \@undefined_i),\]
extracting $\M(\ast \@undefined_i)$ supported away from $\@undefined_i$ and $\mathrm{R}\Gamma_{\@undefined_i}(\M)$ supported on $\@undefined_i$ (we implicitly use Lemma \ref{lem:kashiwara} here to see that this part comes from $\@undefined_{\fgu}(\mathrm{A}/\T_i)^{h\Gamma}$). Repeating this for collections $\{\@undefined_i\}_{i\in \Lambda}$ we can eventually show that $\M$ is in the thick subcategory generated by $j_{\Lambda,!}\M_\Lambda$ for $\M_\Lambda\in \Perf(\mathrm{A}_{\Lambda})^{h\Gamma,\varphi=1}$.

Once we reach an individual stratum, a priori we only have $\M_\Lambda\in \@undefined_{\fgu}(\mathrm{A}_{\Lambda})^{h\Gamma}$. Fortunately the Fitting ideal argument in Proposition \ref{prop:perfectoid_constructibility} shows that these are necessarily perfect. Then we run the same argument: the $\Gamma$-invariant ideals are either zero or the unit ideal on connected components of the scheme. For an object $\M \in \Mod_{\fgu}(\overline{\mathrm{A}}_{\Lambda})^{h\Gamma}$ admits a $\Gamma$-equivariant minimal root $\beta: \M_0 \to \varphi^* \M_0$. Taking Fitting ideals, we see the source and target are vector bundles of the same rank and $\coker \beta$ is a vector bundle. Using ranks the root map is an equivalence, so all of the objects in the heart are vector bundles modulo $p$. By a Postnikov d\'{e}vissage, this proves perfectness modulo $p$. We can then test perfectness modulo $p$ since $\mathrm{A}_{\Lambda}$ is still derived $p$-complete (as well as $\M_{\Lambda}$), so the desired result follows.
<!-- end proof-56 -->
<!-- lemma-36: body_md -->
\label{lem: othog_red_ket}
Consider a framed log affine $(\Spf \R,\mathcal{M})$, and choose (possibly empty) subsets $\Lambda \subseteq \Lambda'\subseteq \{1,\ldots,r\}$. Letting $\mathbb{L}'\in \@undefined^{(b)}_{\mathrm{lisse}}((\Spf \R,\mathcal{M})_{\Lambda',\eta})$ and $\mathbb{L}$ be derived lisse on $\mathrm{Z}_{\Lambda,\eta} \subset (\Spf \R,\mathcal{M})_\eta$, we have
\[\RHom(j_{\Lambda',!} \mathbb{L}', j_{\Lambda,!} j_{\Lambda}^* \mathbb{L}) \simeq \RHom(j_{\Lambda',!}\mathbb{L}', i_{\mathrm{Z}_{\Lambda',\eta}}^* \mathbb{L})[-|\Lambda'\setminus \Lambda|].\]
Here $j_{\Lambda},j_{\Lambda'}$ are the inclusions of the strata $(\Spf \R,\mathcal{M})_{\Lambda,\eta}$ and $(\Spf \R,\mathcal{M})_{\Lambda',\eta}$ with their pullback log structures.
<!-- end lemma-36 -->
<!-- proof-57: body_md -->
We can reframe this by working in $\mathrm{Z}_{\Lambda,\eta} \setminus \bigcup_{j\not \in \Lambda'} \@undefined_{j,\eta}$. The point of doing this is so that $(\Spf \R,\mathcal{M})_{\Lambda',\eta}$ has its inclusion $i_{\Lambda'}$ become a strict closed immersion, and $(\Spf \R,\mathcal{M})_{\Lambda,\eta}$ has its inclusion $j_{\Lambda}$ become a strict open immersion. This makes their roles more transparent in what follows.

One checks
\[j_{\Lambda,!} j_\Lambda^* \mathbb{L} \simeq \left[ \mathbb{L} \longrightarrow \bigoplus_{i} \mathbb{L}|_{\@undefined_{i,\eta}} \longrightarrow \bigoplus_{i < j} \mathbb{L}|_{\@undefined_{i,\eta} \cap \@undefined_{j,\eta}} \longrightarrow \ldots \longrightarrow i_{\Lambda',*} i_{\Lambda'}^* \mathbb{L}\right].\]
Here the direct sums are indexed over members of $\Lambda' \setminus \Lambda$. This can be seen for example by checking stalks on both sides. A similar resolution appears in \cite[\S 2]{yamashita}.

If one substitutes this resolution in $\RHom(i_{\Lambda',*} \mathbb{L}', j_{\Lambda,!} j_{\Lambda}^* \mathbb{L})$, everything except the last term vanishes (which gives the shift). Vanishing can be checked modulo $p$ and after a Postnikov d\'{e}vissage to the heart, where we use logarithmic purity as in \cite[Corollary 4.6.7]{DiaoLanLiuZhuLogAdic}. The present hollow case can again be deduced from this by keeping track of hollow log inertia. For example to deduce the claim for $\mathrm{Z}_{\Lambda,\eta}^{\circ} \xhookrightarrow{j_{\Lambda}} \mathrm{Z}_{\Lambda,\eta}$ we instead equip them both with the log structure induced by $\bigcup_{i \not \in \Lambda} \@undefined_{i,\eta}$ (which has no hollow component), so the log structure on $\mathrm{Z}_{\Lambda,\eta}^{\circ}$ becomes trivial. Then \cite[Corollary 4.6.7]{DiaoLanLiuZhuLogAdic} applies, and on categories of derived lisse pro-Kummer-\'{e}tale sheaves we take $\Mod_{\Z_p\llbracket \widehat{\Z}(1)^{|\Lambda|} \rrbracket}(-)$; this proves the purity isomorphism $\mathbb{L} \simeq \R j_{\Lambda, \ast} j_{\Lambda}^\ast \mathbb{L}$ we want. When we intersect $k$ additional $\@undefined_{i,\eta}$ we take $\widehat{\Z}(1)^{|\Lambda|+k}$.
<!-- end proof-57 -->
<!-- lemma-37: body_md -->
\label{lem:orthog_red}
Consider a framed log affine $(\Spf \R,\mathcal{M})$, and choose (possibly empty) subsets $\Lambda \subseteq \Lambda'\subseteq \{1,\ldots,r\}$. Let $\M_{\Lambda} \in \Perf(\mathrm{A}/(\T_i)_{i\in \Lambda})^{h\Gamma,\varphi=1}$, and let $\M_{\Lambda'} \in \Perf(\mathrm{A}_{\Lambda'})^{h\Gamma,\varphi=1}$, and regard both as objects in $\@undefined_{\fgu}(\mathrm{A}/(\T_i)_{i\in \Lambda})^{h\Gamma}$ using Kashiwara's lemma (Lemma \ref{lem:kashiwara}). Then 
\[\RHom(\M_{\Lambda}(\ast \@undefined_{\Lambda}), \M_{\Lambda'}) \simeq \RHom(\mathrm{R}\Gamma_{\bigcap_{j \in \Lambda'\setminus \Lambda} \@undefined_j} \M_{\Lambda}, \M_{\Lambda'})[-|\Lambda'\setminus \Lambda|].\]
<!-- end lemma-37 -->
<!-- proof-58: body_md -->
The argument is more or less identical, but translated to the finitely generated unit side. We no longer have access to logarithmic purity so we will need to prove the required vanishing in a different way. 

For convenience of notation put $|\Lambda'\setminus \Lambda|=c$. Without affecting any of the results, we may instead work over $\mathrm{A}_{\Lambda,\Lambda'} := \mathrm{A}/(\T_i)_{i\in \Lambda}[1/\T_j]_{p,j\not \in \Lambda'}^{\wedge}$, since $\M_{\Lambda'}$ is already localized at these variables. This is the analogue in the previous proof of passing to $\mathrm{Z}_{\Lambda,\eta} \setminus \bigcup_{j\not \in \Lambda'} \@undefined_{j,\eta}$.

By tensoring with the ($\Gamma$-equivariant) localization triangles
\[\mathrm{R}\Gamma_{\@undefined_i}(\mathrm{A}_{\Lambda,\Lambda'}) \longrightarrow \mathrm{A}_{\Lambda,\Lambda'} \longrightarrow \mathrm{A}_{\Lambda,\Lambda'}(\ast \@undefined_i)\]
for $i\in \Lambda'\setminus \Lambda$ we see that
\[\M_{\Lambda}(\ast \bigcup_{i\in \Lambda'\setminus \Lambda} \@undefined_i) \simeq \left[ \mathrm{R}\Gamma_{\bigcap_{i\in \Lambda'\setminus \Lambda} \@undefined_i} \M_{\Lambda} \longrightarrow \bigoplus_{|\I| = c-1} \mathrm{R}\Gamma_{\bigcap_{i\in \I} \@undefined_i} \M_{\Lambda} \longrightarrow \ldots \longrightarrow \bigoplus_i \mathrm{R}\Gamma_{\@undefined_i} \M_{\Lambda} \longrightarrow \M_{\Lambda}\right] \]
where we always index over $\I \subseteq \Lambda' \setminus \Lambda$, and the resolution is in degrees $-c$ to zero. For the purposes of mapping out to $\M_{\Lambda'}$, this can be used in place of $\M_{\Lambda}(\ast \@undefined_{\Lambda})$.

What remains is an orthogonality result: the desired result follows if we show only the first term has nonzero $\RHom(-,\M_{\Lambda'})$.

Abstractly, for $\mathrm{R}\Gamma_{\bigcap_{i\in \I} \@undefined_i} \M_{\Lambda}$ one sees by Kashiwara that
\[\RHom(\mathrm{R}\Gamma_{\bigcap_{i\in \I} \@undefined_i} \M_{\Lambda},\M_{\Lambda'})\]
can be computed as an $\RHom$ in $\mathrm{A}_{\Lambda,\Lambda'}/(\T_i)_{i\in \I}$ where the first argument is perfect and the second argument is supported on $\@undefined_{j}$ for $j \not \in \I$ (here we assume $\I$ is proper). This follows from Lemma \ref{lem:unlocalized_closed_orthogonality}, after reducing to working modulo $p$.
<!-- end proof-58 -->
<!-- lemma-38: body_md -->
\label{lem:unlocalized_closed_orthogonality}
Let $\overline{\mathrm{A}}$ be a regular $\mathrm{F}$-finite $k\mathopen{(\mkern-3mu(}q-1\mathclose{)\mkern-3mu)}$ algebra, with a continuous action of $\Gamma = (1+p\Z_p) \ltimes \Z_p(1)^n$. Let $\T\in \overline{\mathrm{A}}$ be a nonzerodivisor such that all generators of $\Gamma$ act trivially, except for $\gamma_i$ generating the $i$th copy of $\Z_p(1)_i$ which acts by
\[\gamma_i \cdot \T = q^{p} \T\]
and fixes $\overline{\mathrm{A}}/\T$. Let $\M\in\Perf(\overline{\mathrm{A}})^{\varphi=1,h\Gamma}$ and $\M_i\in\@undefined_{\fgu}(\overline{\mathrm{A}}/\T)^{h\Gamma}$. Then
\[\RHom(\M,i_+\M_i)=0.\]
<!-- end lemma-38 -->
<!-- proof-59: body_md -->
Using Lemma \ref{lem:solid_Frob_perf_comparison} and the Emerton-Kisin correspondence in the regular case, established in \cite[Theorem 6.20]{MathewModpRH}, before taking $\Gamma$-invariants we identify the mapping complex $\RHom(\M,i_+\M_i)$ of finitely generated unit Frobenius modules over $\overline{\mathrm{A}}$ with $\RHom(i_*\mathscr{F},\mathrm{L})$ on $X=\Spec\overline{\mathrm{A}}$. Here $\mathscr{F}$ is a bounded constructible complex of \'{e}tale $\F_p$-sheaves on $\mathrm{Z}=\Spec(\overline{\mathrm{A}}/(\T))$ and $\mathrm{L}$ is a bounded complex with lisse cohomology on $\X=\Spec \overline{\mathrm{A}}$; we absorb the shift in Kashiwara's lemma into $\mathscr{F}$.

There is a subtlety in translating continuity to the \'{e}tale side, but we can avoid it here: it is enough to show that $\gamma_i-1$ acts invertibly on $\RHom(i_*\mathscr{F},\mathrm{L})$, where $\gamma_i$ is the chosen topological generator of $\Z_p(1)_i$. Naturality transfers this operator through the Emerton-Kisin correspondence. The Koszul resolution \eqref{eq:solid_group_resolution} for the toric subgroup $\Z_p(1)^n$, followed by Hochschild-Serre, then gives the desired vanishing.

By adjunction and the fact that $\mathrm{L}$ is derived lisse, we have
\[\underline{\mathrm{RHom}}_\X(i_*\mathscr{F},\mathrm{L})\simeq i_*\underline{\mathrm{RHom}}_{\mathrm{Z}}(\mathscr{F},i^!\mathrm{L})\simeq i_*\underline{\mathrm{RHom}}_{\mathrm{Z}}(\mathscr{F},i^*\mathrm{L}\otimes_{\F_p}^{\mathrm{L}}i^!\F_p).\]
A Postnikov d\'{e}vissage in $\mathscr{F}$ and $\mathrm{L}$ reduces the claim to $\mathscr{F}$ constructible and $\mathrm{L}$ lisse, both concentrated in degree zero. The group $\Z_p(1)_i$ fixes $\mathrm{Z}$, so its actions on $\mathscr{F}$ and $i^*\mathrm{L}$ factor through finite automorphism groups: a constructible $\F_p$-sheaf on a Noetherian scheme has finite dimensional $\F_p$-vector space of endomorphisms. Thus some $\mathrm{H}=p^\ell\Z_p(1)_i$ acts trivially on both. Put $\gamma=\gamma_i^{p^\ell}$. It remains to show that $\gamma-1$ acts invertibly on $i^!\F_p$.

For a geometric point $\bar{z}$ of $\mathrm{Z}$, put $\B=\ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}^{\mathrm{sh}}_{X,\bar{z}}$ and $\mathrm{K}=(\B[1/\T]/\B)[-1]$. Using the triangle
\[i_* i^! \F_p \longrightarrow \F_p \longrightarrow \R j_* \F_p\]
upon taking the stalk at $\bar{z}$ and using Artin-Schreier to compute $(\F_p)_{\bar{z}}$ and $(\R j_* \F_p)_{\bar{z}}$ as mapping fibers $\fib(\varphi-1:\B\longrightarrow\B)$ and $\fib(\varphi-1:\B[1/\T]\longrightarrow\B[1/\T])$ respectively, the fact that fibers commute with fibers yields
\[(i^!\F_p)_{\bar{z}} \simeq \fib(\varphi-1:\mathrm{K} \longrightarrow \mathrm{K}).\]
Since $\gamma$ fixes $\B/(\T)$ and sends $\T$ to $q^{p^{\ell+1}}\T$, the operator $\gamma-1$ acts by the units $q^{-mp^{\ell+1}}-1$ on the graded pieces of the filtration $\T^{-m}\B/\B$ on $\B[1/\T]/\B$. It is therefore invertible on $\mathrm{K}$ and, as it commutes with Frobenius, on $(i^!\F_p)_{\bar z}$. This proves the claim on stalks.

Thus $\gamma-1$ acts invertibly on $\underline{\mathrm{RHom}}_\X(i_*\mathscr{F},\mathrm{L})$. Finally, $\gamma-1=(\gamma_i-1)^{p^\ell}$ in characteristic $p$, so $\gamma_i-1$ is also invertible as desired.
<!-- end proof-59 -->
<!-- theorem-8: body_md -->
\label{thm:RHom_comparisons}
Choose (possibly empty) subsets $\Lambda, \Lambda'\subseteq \{1,\ldots,r\}$. Let $\M_{\Lambda} \in \Perf(\mathrm{A}_{\Lambda})^{h\Gamma,\varphi=1}$, and let $\M_{\Lambda'} \in \Perf(\mathrm{A}_{\Lambda'})^{h\Gamma,\varphi=1}$. Then $\T_\ensuremath{\mathrm{\acute{e}t}}$ induces an equivalence
\[\RHom_{\@undefined_{\fgu}(\mathrm{A})^{h\Gamma}}(j_{\Lambda,!}\M_{\Lambda},j_{\Lambda',!}\M_{\Lambda'}) \simeq \RHom(\T_\ensuremath{\mathrm{\acute{e}t}}(j_{\Lambda',!}\M_{\Lambda'}),\T_\ensuremath{\mathrm{\acute{e}t}}(j_{\Lambda,!}\M_{\Lambda})).\]
<!-- end theorem-8 -->
<!-- proof-60: body_md -->
The comparisons we need fit into three cases: where $\Lambda=\Lambda'$, where $\Lambda \subseteq \Lambda'$, and where neither holds or $\Lambda \not \subseteq \Lambda'$. In the third case, on both sides it is easy to see that the $\RHom$ is zero. In the first case we have already proven this by combining Corollary \ref{cor:thick_gen_embedding} and Proposition \ref{prop:thick_gen_equiv}.

Thus, all of the remaining work is the case $\Lambda \subseteq \Lambda'$. Geometrically, on the Kummer-\'{e}tale side both $\T_\ensuremath{\mathrm{\acute{e}t}}(j_{\Lambda',!}\M_{\Lambda'})$ and $\T_\ensuremath{\mathrm{\acute{e}t}}(j_{\Lambda,!}\M_{\Lambda})$ are supported on the closed locus
\[\mathrm{Z}_{\Lambda,\eta} = \bigcap_{\lambda \in \Lambda} \@undefined_{\lambda,\eta} \subset (\Spf \R,\mathcal{M})_{\eta}\]
equipped with the pullback log structure. Inside of this closed locus on the Kummer-\'{e}tale side of the correspondence, the $\RHom$ we are computing involves maps from $j_{\Lambda',!} \mathbb{L}' \to j_{!,\Lambda} \mathbb{L}$ (up to some shifts). In other words, maps from an arbitrary deeper stratum to $\mathbb{L}$ supported on the open stratum $(\X,\mathcal{M})_{\Lambda,\eta} = \mathrm{Z}_{\Lambda,\eta}^{\circ} \subset \mathrm{Z}_{\Lambda,\eta}$. Via Kashiwara's lemma, we may therefore drop $j_{\Lambda',!}$ and $j_{!,\Lambda}$ and simply consider objects $\M_{\Lambda'}, \M_{\Lambda}$ in $\@undefined_{\fgu}(\mathrm{A}/(\T_i)_{i\in \Lambda})^{h\Gamma}$ supported on the deeper stratum $(\X,\mathcal{M})_{\Lambda',\eta} \subset \mathrm{Z}_{\Lambda,\eta}$ and the open stratum respectively.

We first argue in a special case where $\M_{\Lambda}$ admits an extension to 
\[\M_{\Lambda}^{\mathrm{ext}} \in \Perf(\mathrm{A}/(\T_i)_{i\in \Lambda})^{\varphi=1,h\Gamma}.\]
This means $\M_{\Lambda}$ is recovered as $\M_{\Lambda}^{\mathrm{ext}} \otimes \mathrm{A}_{\Lambda} = \M_{\Lambda}^{\mathrm{ext}}(\ast \@undefined_{\Lambda})$, i.e. we $p$-completely invert the remaining coordinates. Geometrically, this asks on the Kummer-\'{e}tale side that it extends to a derived lisse sheaf on $\mathrm{Z}_{\Lambda,\eta}$ with its pullback log structure. 

In this situation, in $\@undefined_{\fgu}(\mathrm{A}/(\T_i)_{i\in \Lambda})^{h\Gamma}$ we have the equivalence
\[\RHom(\M_{\Lambda}^{\mathrm{ext}}(\ast \@undefined_{\Lambda}), \M_{\Lambda'}) \simeq \RHom(\mathrm{R}\Gamma_{\bigcap_{j \in \Lambda'\setminus \Lambda} \@undefined_j} \M_{\Lambda}^{\mathrm{ext}}, \M_{\Lambda'})[-|\Lambda'\setminus \Lambda|].\]
provided by Lemma \ref{lem:orthog_red}. On the right, using Kashiwara again gives an $\RHom$ in $\@undefined_{\fgu}(\mathrm{A}/(\T_i)_{i\in \Lambda'})^{h\Gamma}$, corresponding to a smaller closed locus. But then the target is in 
\[\Perf(\mathrm{A}_{\Lambda'})^{\varphi=1,h\Gamma} \subset \@undefined_{\fgu}(\mathrm{A}/(\T_i)_{i\in \Lambda'})^{h\Gamma},\] 
and in particular using the localization adjunction we obtain the $\RHom$
\[\RHom(\mathrm{R}\Gamma_{\bigcap_{j \in \Lambda'\setminus \Lambda} \@undefined_j} \M_{\Lambda}^{\mathrm{ext}}(\ast \@undefined_{\Lambda'}), \M_{\Lambda'})[-|\Lambda'\setminus \Lambda|],\]
now taken in $\Perf(\mathrm{A}_{\Lambda'})^{\varphi=1,h\Gamma}$ (so both arguments are being implicitly passed through Lemma \ref{lem:kashiwara}).

For this final $\RHom$ we know $\T_\ensuremath{\mathrm{\acute{e}t}}$ is fully faithful. The reduction will also work on the Kummer-\'{e}tale side as well, which follows from Lemma \ref{lem: othog_red_ket}. In particular, we obtain the analogous statement
\[\RHom(j_{\Lambda',!} \mathbb{L}', j_{\Lambda,!} j_{\Lambda}^* \mathbb{L}^{\mathrm{ext}}) \simeq \RHom(j_{\Lambda',!}\mathbb{L}', i_{\mathrm{Z}_{\Lambda',\eta}}^* \mathbb{L}^{\mathrm{ext}})[-|\Lambda'\setminus \Lambda|],\]
where the target $\RHom$ occurs on the closed locus $\mathrm{Z}_{\Lambda',\eta}$, and the source on $\mathrm{Z}_{\Lambda,\eta}$. Further restricting to the open locus $(\X,\mathcal{M})_{\Lambda',\eta} \subset \mathrm{Z}_{\Lambda',\eta}$, due to the supports this simplifies to a shifted $\RHom$ of derived lisse sheaves on $(\X,\mathcal{M})_{\Lambda',\eta}$. These two final $\RHom$s we obtained, on either side, have their reduction steps exchanged by $\T_\ensuremath{\mathrm{\acute{e}t}}$. Once the reduction is made they now involve derived lisse sheaves or objects in $\Perf(\mathrm{A}_{\Lambda'})^{\varphi=1,h\Gamma}$, and using Proposition \ref{prop:thick_gen_equiv} they can be seen to be identified by $\T_\ensuremath{\mathrm{\acute{e}t}}$.

The general case then follows from Lemma \ref{lem:primetop_Kum_red}, which reduces the claim to the situation where $\M_{\Lambda}^{\mathrm{ext}}$ exists. Indeed on the Kummer-\'{e}tale side the same formula for $\mu^{r}_{\mathrm{N}}$ invariants holds, precisely because
\[(\Spf \R_{\mathrm{N}},\mathcal{M}_{\mathrm{N}})_\eta \longrightarrow (\Spf \R,\mathcal{M})_\eta\]
is a torsor in the pro-Kummer-\'{e}tale topology for this group.
<!-- end proof-60 -->
<!-- lemma-39: body_md -->
\label{lem:primetop_Kum_red}
Choose subsets $\Lambda \subseteq \Lambda'\subseteq \{1,\ldots,r\}$, and suppose we are given objects $\M_{\Lambda'}$ and $\M_{\Lambda}$ in $\@undefined_{\fgu}(\mathrm{A}/(\T_i)_{i\in \Lambda})^{h\Gamma}$ supported on the strata for $\Lambda'$ and $\Lambda$ respectively. There is a prime-to-$p$ Kummer cover $f: (\Spf \R_{\mathrm{N}},\mathcal{M}_{\mathrm{N}}) \to (\Spf \R,\mathcal{M})$ such that 
\[f^* \M_{\Lambda} = \M_{\Lambda,\mathrm{N}}^{\mathrm{ext}}(\ast \@undefined_{\Lambda,\mathrm{N}})\]
where $\M_{\Lambda,\mathrm{N}}^{\mathrm{ext}}\in \Perf((\mathrm{A}_{\mathrm{N}}/(\T^{1/\mathrm{N}}_i)_{i\in \Lambda}))^{h\Gamma,\varphi=1}$. Moreover,
\[\RHom(f^* \M_{\Lambda}, f^* \M_{\Lambda'})^{h\mu^r_{\mathrm{N}}} = \RHom(\M_{\Lambda}, \M_{\Lambda'}).\]
<!-- end lemma-39 -->
<!-- proof-61: body_md -->
The first assertion is straightforward. Write
\[\mathrm{Z}_{\Lambda,\eta} = \bigcap_{\lambda \in \Lambda} \@undefined_{\lambda,\eta}\]
equipped with its pullback log structure as before.

Using Corollary \ref{cor:thick_gen_embedding}, since in the diagram
\begin{display}
\Perf((\mathrm{A}/(\T_i)_{i\in \Lambda}))^{h\Gamma,\varphi=1,\op} \ar{d} \ar{r}{\T_\ensuremath{\mathrm{\acute{e}t}}} & \@undefined^{(b),\mathrm{pKum}}_{\mathrm{lisse}}(\mathrm{Z}_{\Lambda,\eta},\Z_p) \ar{d}{j_{\Lambda}^\ast} \\
\Perf(\mathrm{A}_{\Lambda})^{h\Gamma,\varphi=1,\op} \ar{r}{\T_\ensuremath{\mathrm{\acute{e}t}}} & \@undefined^{(b),\mathrm{pKum}}_{\mathrm{lisse}}((\Spf \R,\mathcal{M})_{\Lambda,\eta},\Z_p)
\end{display}
both horizontal arrows are equivalences we must check that $\mathbb{L}\in \@undefined^{(b),\mathrm{pKum}}_{\mathrm{lisse}}((\Spf \R,\mathcal{M})_{\Lambda,\eta},\Z_p)$ admits an extension $\mathbb{L}^{\mathrm{ext}}$ which is again $p$-Kummer. Strictly speaking we did not show the top arrow is an equivalence, but because we have not inverted any $\T_i$ the proof is the same argument as the $|\Lambda|=r$ case of Proposition \ref{prop:thick_gen_equiv}, but with the log perfectoid cover of $\mathrm{Z}_{\Lambda,\eta}$ being the zero locus of $\T_i^{1/p^\infty}$ for $i\in \Lambda$ in $(\X,\mathcal{M})_{\infty,\eta}$ with its pullback log structure.

As we did in Propositon \ref{prop:thick_gen_equiv}, keeping track of log inertia we reduce to the general assertion that for a framed log affine $(\Spf \R,\mathcal{M})$ and $\mathbb{L}\in \@undefined^{(b)}_{\mathrm{lisse}}(\X_\eta \setminus \@undefined_\eta, \Z_p)$ there is a prime-to-$p$ Kummer cover $f: (\Spf \R_{\mathrm{N}},\mathcal{M}_{\mathrm{N}}) \to (\Spf \R,\mathcal{M})$ so $f_\eta^* \mathbb{L}$ admits a $p$-Kummer extension to $(\Spf \R_{\mathrm{N}},\mathcal{M}_{\mathrm{N}})_\eta$. By \cite[Corollary 6.3.4]{DiaoLanLiuZhuLogAdic}, the cohomology sheaves of $\mathbb{L}$ extend across the boundary as Kummer-\'{e}tale local systems. The vanishing in \cite[Theorem 4.6.1]{DiaoLanLiuZhuLogAdic}, applied modulo $p^n$ and passed to the inverse limit, makes the spectral sequence
\[\E_2^{a,b}=\R^a j_*\mathrm{H}^b(\mathbb{L}) \longrightarrow \mathrm{H}^{a+b}(\R j_*\mathbb{L})\]
degenerate. Thus $\R j_*\mathbb{L}$ is derived lisse, and, as in the essential surjectivity component of Theorem \ref{thm:open_stratum}, for every log geometric point $\bar{x}$ and $b\in\Z$,
\[\mathrm{im}\left(\I_{\bar{x}}^{\log,(p)'} \longrightarrow \mathrm{Aut}_{\Z_p}\left(\mathrm{H}^b(\R j_*\mathbb{L})_{\bar{x}}\right)\right)\]
is finite. It follows that for each cohomology sheaf there is some prime-to-$p$ Kummer cover making it $p$-Kummer by \cite[Proposition 5]{KoshikawaYaoCorrigendum}. Appealing to a Postnikov d\'{e}vissage as in \cite[Lemma 5.4.3]{HauckStacky} and boundedness, a single prime-to-$p$ Kummer cover $\Spf \R_{\mathrm{N}}$ makes $\R j_*\mathbb{L}$ $p$-Kummer. Thus, the first claim follows.

Similarly to Proposition \ref{prop:open_strat_Kum_desc}, we have 
\[\mathrm{A}_{\mathrm{N}} = \bigoplus_{\alpha \in (\Z/\mathrm{N}\Z)^r} \mathrm{A} \cdot \mathrm{S}^{\alpha},\] 
with a natural $\mu_{\mathrm{N}}^r$ action associated to the grading, which gives $\RHom(f^* \M_{\Lambda}, f^* \M_{\Lambda'})$ a $\mu_{\mathrm{N}}^r$-action. In our specific case, the components for $i\in \Lambda$ act trivially -- in what follows we will simply prove a more general assertion, regarding $\M_{\Lambda}$ and $\M_{\Lambda'}$ as arbitrary finitely generated unit modules in $\@undefined_{\fgu}(\mathrm{A})^{h\Gamma}$ (using Kashiwara's lemma).

Since $\mathrm{N}$ is invertible in $\Z_p$, for any $\M \in \@undefined_{\fgu}(\mathrm{A})^{h\Gamma}$ the homotopy fixed points of its pullback are computed by taking the degree zero summand in the decomposition $\mathrm{A}_{\mathrm{N}} = \bigoplus_{\alpha \in (\Z/\mathrm{N}\Z)^r} \mathrm{A} \cdot \mathrm{S}^{\alpha}$. The projection onto this summand is $\Gamma$-equivariant. It is also Frobenius equivariant, since Frobenius permutes the summands by $\alpha \mapsto p\alpha$ and $(p,\mathrm{N})=1$. The extension/restriction adjunction (in Frobenius modules) and preservation of limits by $\RHom(\M_{\Lambda},-)$ (to move $h\mu_{\mathrm{N}}^r$ inside) therefore give
\begin{align*}
\RHom(f^*\M_{\Lambda},f^*\M_{\Lambda'})^{h\mu_{\mathrm{N}}^r}
&\simeq \RHom\left(\M_{\Lambda},(\mathrm{A}_{\mathrm{N}}\widehat{\otimes}_{\mathrm{A}}^{\mathrm{L}}\M_{\Lambda'})^{h\mu_{\mathrm{N}}^r}\right) \\
&\simeq \RHom(\M_{\Lambda},\M_{\Lambda'}).
\end{align*}
This proves the second claim.
<!-- end proof-61 -->
<!-- theorem-9: body_md -->
Let $(\X,\mathcal{M})$ satisfy Assumption \ref{ass:snc_log_structure} over $\W(k)[\zeta_p]$. Let $\@undefined^{(b),\mathrm{pKum}}_{\cons,\@undefined}((\X,\mathcal{M})_\eta, \Z_p)$ denote the full subcategory of $p$-Kummer constructible sheaves in $\@undefined^{(b)}_{\cons,\@undefined}((\X,\mathcal{M})_\eta, \Z_p)$. Then
\begin{display}
\T_\ensuremath{\mathrm{\acute{e}t}}: \@undefined_{\fgu}((\X,\mathcal{M})_{\mathbbl{\Delta}},\ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}[1/\I_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}]_p^{\wedge})^\op \ar{r}{\sim} & \@undefined^{(b),\mathrm{pKum}}_{\cons,\@undefined}((\X,\mathcal{M})_\eta, \Z_p)
\end{display}
is a symmetric monoidal equivalence.
\label{thm:RH_main}
<!-- end theorem-9 -->
<!-- proof-62: body_md -->
By Lemma \ref{lem:strict_etale_local_framing} and strict \'{e}tale descent (for the source Theorem \ref{thm:fgu_etale_desc} and for the target Lemma \ref{lem:constructible_strict_etale_descent}), we may first work on a framed log affine $(\Spf\R,\mathcal{M})$.

In this case, we apply Lemma \ref{lem:thick_equiv_criterion}. We use the generators from Lemma \ref{lem:ket_thick_gens} and Lemma \ref{lem:crys_thick_gens}, which correspond (up to dimension shifts, which do not matter for the argument) by combining Corollary \ref{cor:thick_gen_embedding} and Proposition \ref{prop:thick_gen_equiv}. 

We have now checked all the hypotheses:
\begin{itemize}
  \item Both source and target are idempotent complete, and $\T_\ensuremath{\mathrm{\acute{e}t}}$ is exact. This is explained already immediately after Lemma \ref{lem:thick_equiv_criterion}.
  \item The generators of the source and target correspond under $\T_\ensuremath{\mathrm{\acute{e}t}}$, as explained above.
  \item The comparisons on $\RHom$s are done by Theorem \ref{thm:RHom_comparisons}.
\end{itemize}
Thus $\T_\ensuremath{\mathrm{\acute{e}t}}$ is an equivalence.

We further claimed that it is a symmetric monoidal equivalence. The fact that the equivalence is symmetric monoidal can also be tested locally, where via Lemma \ref{lem:factorization} it reduces to symmetric monoidality in Theorem \ref{thm:EK_perfect}.
<!-- end proof-62 -->
<!-- definition-11: body_md -->
For each logarithmic stratum $j_\Lambda:(\X,\mathcal{M})_{\Lambda,\eta} \hookrightarrow (\X,\mathcal{M})_\eta$, put $d_\Lambda=\dim((\X,\mathcal{M})_{\Lambda,\eta})$. The perverse $t$-structure of \cite{GabberTStructures} on the full subcategory of $p$-Kummer sheaves in $\@undefined^{(b)}_{\cons,\@undefined}((\X,\mathcal{M})_\eta,\Z_p)$ is defined by
\[{}^p\@undefined^{\leq0}=\{\mathscr{F}\mid j_\Lambda^*\mathscr{F}\in\@undefined^{\leq-d_\Lambda}((\X,\mathcal{M})_{\Lambda,\eta},\Z_p)\text{ for every }\Lambda\},\]
\[{}^p\@undefined^{\geq0}=\{\mathscr{F}\mid j_\Lambda^!\mathscr{F}\in\@undefined^{\geq-d_\Lambda}((\X,\mathcal{M})_{\Lambda,\eta},\Z_p)\text{ for every }\Lambda\}.\]
We write ${}^p\mathrm{H}^i$ for its cohomology functors. The $p^+$-perverse $t$-structure is
\[{}^{p^+}\@undefined^{\leq0}=\{\mathscr{F}\in{}^p\@undefined^{\leq1}\mid{}^p\mathrm{H}^1(\mathscr{F})\text{ is locally bounded }p\text{-power torsion}\},\]
with the $\ge 0$ part simply given by
\[{}^{p^+}\@undefined^{\geq0}=\{\mathscr{F}\mid \mathscr{F}\mathord{/\mkern-6mu/} p\in{}^p\@undefined^{\geq0}((\X,\mathcal{M})_\eta,\F_p)\}.\]

One may check these $t$-structures restrict to the $p$-Kummer subcategory (i.e. that perverse truncations of $p$-Kummer sheaves are $p$-Kummer). The argument of \cite[Construction 4.3 and Proposition 4.6]{BhattHansenCons}, applied to the defining bounds after $j_\Lambda^*$ and $j_\Lambda^!$, gives the following reduction criteria: for every $n\geq1$, derived reduction modulo $p^n$ is left $t$-exact for $p^+$-perversity. Moreover, $\mathscr{F} \in{}^{p^+}\@undefined^{\geq0}$ if and only if $\mathscr{F}\mathord{/\mkern-6mu/} p \in{}^p\@undefined^{\geq0}((\X,\mathcal{M})_\eta,\F_p)$.
\label{def:perverse_pKum}
<!-- end definition-11 -->
<!-- proposition-10: body_md -->
Assume that $(\X,\mathcal{M})_\eta$ is pure of dimension $d$. The equivalence of Theorem \ref{thm:RH_main} with its essential image, shifted by $[d]$, is $t$-exact for the standard $t$-structure on the source and the $p^+$-perverse $t$-structure of Definition \ref{def:perverse_pKum} on the target.
\label{prop:Tet_perverse_exact}
<!-- end proposition-10 -->
<!-- proof-63: body_md -->
The source $t$-structure is strict \'{e}tale local by Corollary \ref{cor:laur_t_struct}, and the same holds for the bounds in Definition \ref{def:perverse_pKum}. We may therefore work on a framed log affine. 

We first prove the claim modulo $p$ and therefore use the base $\overline{\mathrm{A}}=\overline{\R}^{\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\square$}}}}\mathopen{(\mkern-3mu(}q-1\mathclose{)\mkern-3mu)}$. We may consider $\M\in\@undefined_{\fgu}(\overline{\mathrm{A}})^{h\Gamma}$, using Theorem \ref{thm:qdR_crys_Gamma_mod}.

For $\Lambda\subseteq\{1,\ldots,r\}$, as before put
\[\overline{\mathrm{A}}_\Lambda=\left(\overline{\mathrm{A}}/(\T_i)_{i\in \Lambda}\right)[1/\T_j]_{j\notin\Lambda,\ j\leq r}\]
and write $\M_{\Lambda}$ for the derived base change $\M \otimes_{\overline{\mathrm{A}}}^{\mathrm{L}} \overline{\mathrm{A}}_\Lambda$.

Let $j_\Lambda:\X_{\eta,\Lambda}\hookrightarrow(\X,\mathcal{M})_\eta$ be the corresponding stratum, of dimension $d-|\Lambda|$. Lemma \ref{lem:derived_stratum_fgu} and the proof of Proposition \ref{prop:perfectoid_constructibility} show that each $\mathrm{H}^i(\M_\Lambda)$ is finite projective over $\overline{\mathrm{A}}_\Lambda$. Compatibility with restriction, Lemma \ref{lem:factorization}, and the contravariant Katz correspondence therefore yield
\[j_\Lambda^*\T_{\ensuremath{\mathrm{\acute{e}t}},\F_p}(\M)[d]\in\@undefined^{\leq-(d-|\Lambda|)} \Longleftrightarrow \M_\Lambda\in\@undefined^{\geq-|\Lambda|}.\]
We claim that $\M\in\@undefined^{\geq0}$ if and only if $\M_\Lambda\in\@undefined^{\geq-|\Lambda|}$ for every $\Lambda$, where we use the ordinary $t$-structure on $\@undefined_{\fgu}(\overline{\mathrm{A}})^{h\Gamma}$. Applying the coconnectivity criterion of \cite[Lemma 3.1]{AlonsoJeremiasSaorinTStructures} along the coordinate stratification, using $i_\Lambda^!\M\simeq\M_\Lambda[-|\Lambda|]$, gives the claim.

Definition \ref{def:perverse_pKum} now gives
\[\T_{\ensuremath{\mathrm{\acute{e}t}},\F_p}(\M)[d]\in{}^p\@undefined^{\leq0} \Longleftrightarrow \M\in\@undefined^{\geq0}.\]
Thus the contravariant equivalence exchanges coconnectivity on the source with perverse connectivity on the target. By orthogonality, it also exchanges connectivity with perverse coconnectivity, proving mod $p$ perverse $t$-exactness.

To deduce the general claim, we see $\M \in \@undefined^{\le 0}$ if and only if $\M \mathord{/\mkern-6mu/} p \in \@undefined^{\le 0}$ by derived Nakayama. On the Kummer-\'{e}tale side we have analogous reduction criteria explained in Definition \ref{def:perverse_pKum}, so for the $\le 0$ part we may reduce to the mod $p$ assertion. Orthogonality then proves the general claim.
<!-- end proof-63 -->
<!-- remark-15: body_md -->
Following \cite[Theorem 7.5.6]{KedlayaLiu2016}, call $\mathcal{E}\in\@undefined_{\mathrm{fgu}}((\X,\mathcal{M})_{\mathbbl{\Delta}},\ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}[1/\I_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}]_p^{\wedge})$ corresponding to an object in the ordinary heart of constructible sheaves \textit{effective} if, on every framed strict \'{e}tale chart, its associated $(\varphi,\Gamma)$-module $\M$ satisfies the following condition for every boundary coordinate $\T_i$: the $i$th $\Z_p(1)$-factor acts trivially on
\[(\mathrm{A}/(\T_i))\otimes^{\mathrm{L}}_{\mathrm{A}}\M\]
in the derived category. This condition is strict \'{e}tale local and independent of the framing. Theorem \ref{thm:RH_main} gives an equivalence
\begin{display}
\T_\ensuremath{\mathrm{\acute{e}t}}: \@undefined_{\mathrm{fgu}}((\X,\mathcal{M})_{\mathbbl{\Delta}},\ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}[1/\I_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}]_p^{\wedge})^{\mathrm{eff},\op} \ar{r}{\sim} & \@undefined^{\ensuremath\heartsuit}_{\mathrm{cons},\@undefined}(\X_{\eta,\ensuremath{\mathrm{pro\acute{e}t}}},\Z_p).
\end{display}
where on the target the ordinary $t$-structure is used.

In the derived setting, it seems plausible that one could take the ``effective part'' of an $\R\Hom$ to obtain the derived category of constructible sheaves along $\@undefined$.
\label{rem:eff}
<!-- end remark-15 -->
<!-- corollary-7: body_md -->
Theorem \ref{thm:RH_main} and all preceding results stated over $\W(k)[\zeta_p]$ admit corresponding variants over $\W(k)[\zeta_{p^\ell}]$ for every $\ell\geq0$. 
\label{cor:other_bases}
<!-- end corollary-7 -->
<!-- proof-64: body_md -->
Corollary \ref{cor:coh_laur_other_bases} is the only nontrivial change needed in the argument, which covers these cases. With this, one can deduce Theorem \ref{thm:fgu_etale_desc} verbatim (as it uses nothing about $\Gamma$). The following arguments are insensitive to the change in prismatic ideal or $\Gamma$, except for Proposition \ref{prop:open_decompletion_hom}; however there the reduction is to vanishing of a cohomology group, so changing $\Gamma$ from $(1+p\Z_p) \ltimes \Z_p(1)^n$ to $(\mu_{p-1} \times (1+p\Z_p)) \ltimes \Z_p(1)^n$ does not change the result by using Hochschild-Serre.
<!-- end proof-64 -->
<!-- remark-16: body_md -->
The entire local theory using $(\varphi,\Gamma)$-modules seems to have no obstruction to working over $\A_K$, but unfortunately the globalization step does not appear to work. One would want to have a prism $(\A_K^+, \varphi^n([p]_q))$ which satisfies 
\[\A_K^+[1/\varphi^{n}([p]_q)]_p^{\wedge} \simeq \A_K.\]
However it seems such a prism cannot exist in general without dropping some desirable properties. See \cite[Appendix 2, Proposition 23]{Watanabe} for more details. The argument there showing nonexistence uses that the mod $p$ reduction should be $\E_K^+$, the ring of integers of the field of norms. It is still possible that $\A_K^+$ exists by dropping this condition, but this seems unnatural to do.
<!-- end remark-16 -->
<!-- example-1: body_md -->
Let $(\X,\mathcal{M})=(\Spf \Z_p\langle \T\rangle,\N)$ with log structure induced by $\@undefined=\{\T=0\}$, and let $j:\U_\eta=\X_\eta\setminus\@undefined_\eta\hookrightarrow(\X_\eta,\N)$. Put $\overline{\R}=\F_p\langle\T\rangle$ and $\mathrm{A}=\overline{\R}^{\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\square$}}}}\mathopen{(\mkern-3mu(}q-1\mathclose{)\mkern-3mu)}$, using the framing given by $\T$.

Following \cite{Brinon}, let $f:\mathcal{E}\to\mathbb{D}=\X_\eta$ be the projectivization of the Tate family with parameter $\tilde{q}=p^p\T$, given by
\[v^2+uv=u^3-b_2(\tilde{q})-b_3(\tilde{q}),\]
where $b_2$ and $b_3$ are the standard coefficients for the Tate curve in $\tilde{q}\Z_p\llbracket \tilde{q} \rrbracket$.

It is smooth away from $\T=0$, where it becomes a nodal cubic. The ordinary Zariski constructible sheaf
\[\mathscr{F} = \R^1 f_* \F_p\]
therefore has rank two on $\U_\eta$ and rank one at the origin. On $\U_\eta$ the restriction of $\mathscr{F}$ is described by $\underline{\Hom}_{\F_p}(\mathcal{E}[p],\F_p)$. As explained in \cite[\S 3.1]{Brinon} one may describe $\mathcal{E}[p]$ on $\U_\eta$ as an extension of $\F_p$ by $\mu_p$ via the Kummer class $[\tilde{q}]$, and since $\tilde{q}=p^p\T$ this is also the nonzero Kummer class of $\T$. That is, $[\tilde{q}]=[\T]$ in $\mathrm{H}^1_\ensuremath{\mathrm{\acute{e}t}}(\U_\eta,\mu_p)$ as classes obtained via the Kummer map $\ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}(\U_\eta)^\times \to \mathrm{H}^1_\ensuremath{\mathrm{\acute{e}t}}(\U_\eta,\mu_p)$ since the kernel consists of $p$th powers. Brinon also explains the explicit formula for the Galois action, using this Kummer class $[\tilde{q}]$ for the Tate parameter.

Globally, the sheaf $\mathscr{F}$ is a nonsplit extension
\[0\longrightarrow \F_p \longrightarrow \mathscr{F} \longrightarrow j_!\F_p(-1) \longrightarrow 0.\]
Here we deduce it is nonsplit by dualizing the previous description of $\mathcal{E}[p]$ as a nonsplit extension corresponding to $[\tilde{q}] \neq 0$ on the open stratum.

The corresponding $(\varphi,\Gamma)$-module has underlying module
\[\M=\mathrm{A}[1/\T] e_1 \oplus \mathrm{A} e_2.\]
The submodule $\mathrm{A}[1/\T]e_1$ and quotient $\mathrm{A} e_2$ correspond respectively to $j_!\F_p(-1)$ and $\F_p$, in accordance with the contravariance of $\T_\ensuremath{\mathrm{\acute{e}t}}$. Frobenius fixes both basis vectors. For $\gamma=(a_\gamma,b_\gamma)\in\Gamma=\Z_p^\times \ltimes \Z_p(1)$, we use the matrix
\[\R_{\gamma} = \begin{pmatrix} \overline{a}_\gamma & \overline{b}_\gamma \\ 0 & 1 \end{pmatrix}\]
where the bars denote reduction modulo $p$ to give the action of $\Gamma$. This means for $a_\gamma$, in the decomposition $\Z_p^\times = \F_p^\times \times (1+p\Z_p)$ we extract only the $\F_p^\times$ component as $\overline{a}_\gamma$. Note $\R_{\gamma} \cdot \R_{\delta} = \R_{\gamma \delta}$ as needed.

This realizes $\mathscr{F}$ (applying $\T_{\ensuremath{\mathrm{\acute{e}t}},\F_p}$).
\label{ex:nontrivial_cons}
<!-- end example-1 -->
<!-- definition-12: body_md -->
For a formal prestack $\mathcal{Y}$ over $\Z_p^{\mathbbl{\Delta}}$, let $\mathrm{sh}_{\mathrm{\acute{e}id}}\mathcal{Y}$ denote the \'{e}id sheafification of the associated presheaf on $\mathrm{fSch}^{\mathrm{aff}}_{/\Z_p^{\mathbbl{\Delta}}}$ from \cite[Construction 2.2.7]{Kipp2}. We define
\[\mathcal{Y}^{\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\blacksquare$}}}}:=(-)^{\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\blacksquare$}}}}_{\mathrm{Kipp}}\bigl(\mathrm{sh}_{\mathrm{\acute{e}id}}\mathcal{Y}\bigr),\]
which we call informally the \emph{analytic realization} where
\[(-)^{\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\blacksquare$}}}}_{\mathrm{Kipp}}:(\Z_p^{\mathbbl{\Delta}})_{\mathrm{\acute{e}id}}\longrightarrow\mathrm{AnStack}_{/\Z_p^{{\mathbbl{\Delta}},\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\blacksquare$}}}}}\]
is the colimit-preserving left exact functor of \cite[Theorem 2.3.3(A) and \S3.6.1]{Kipp2}. We note $(-)^{\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\blacksquare$}}}}$ preserves finite limits, and $(\Spf\B)^{\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\blacksquare$}}}}=\Spa(\B,\B)$ for a bounded prism $\B$.
\label{def:box_analytic_realization}
<!-- end definition-12 -->
<!-- lemma-40: body_md -->
\label{lem:formal_f!}
Let $f: \X \to \Y$ be a morphism of analytic stacks, and suppose it is cohomologically smooth and weakly cohomologically proper. Then given a square
\begin{display}
\X \times_{\Y} \mathrm{Z} \ar{r}{\iota_{\X}} \ar{d}{f_{\mathrm{Z}}} & \X \ar{d}{f} \\
\mathrm{Z} \ar{r}{\iota_\Y} & \Y
\end{display}
the map $f_{\mathrm{Z}}: \X \times_\Y \mathrm{Z} \to \mathrm{Z}$ is cohomologically smooth and weakly cohomologically proper. Moreover, $f_{\mathrm{Z}}^! \ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}_{\mathrm{Z}}\simeq \iota_\X^* f^! \ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}_{\Y}$.
<!-- end lemma-40 -->
<!-- proof-65: body_md -->
Weak cohomological properness and cohomological smoothness are stable under arbitrary base change by \cite[Remark 1.1.8]{Kipp2}, so $f_{\mathrm{Z}}$ is again cohomologically smooth and weakly cohomologically proper. Put $\omega_f=f^!\ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}_\Y$. For a cohomologically smooth map, $\omega_f$ is invertible, the natural map $\omega_f\otimes f^*(-)\to f^!(-)$ is an equivalence, and $\omega_f$ commutes with arbitrary base change (see \cite[Definition 1.2.1.1]{Kipp}). Hence the square in the Lemma statement gives $\omega_{f_{\mathrm{Z}}}\simeq\iota_\X^*\omega_f$. Applying this to the unit object gives $f_{\mathrm{Z}}^!\ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}_{\mathrm{Z}}\simeq\omega_{f_{\mathrm{Z}}}\simeq\iota_\X^*f^!\ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}_\Y$.
<!-- end proof-65 -->
<!-- lemma-41: body_md -->
\label{lem:formal_pushforward_duality}
Let $f:\X\to\Y$ be a cohomologically smooth and weakly cohomologically proper morphism of analytic stacks, and put $\omega_f=f^!\ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}_\Y$. Suppose further that
\[\R f_! \simeq \R f_*\]
via the canonical map.

Then $\R f_*$ preserves dualizable objects, and for every dualizable object $\mathcal{E} \in \@undefined_{\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\blacksquare$}}}}(\X)$ there is a natural equivalence
\[(\R f_*\mathcal{E})^\vee \simeq \R f_*(\mathcal{E}^\vee\otimes\omega_f).\]
<!-- end lemma-41 -->
<!-- proof-66: body_md -->
For every $\mathcal{E}'\in\@undefined_{\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\blacksquare$}}}}(\Y)$, one has
\[\underline{\mathrm{RHom}}_\Y(\R f_*\mathcal{E},\mathcal{E}') \simeq \R f_*\underline{\mathrm{RHom}}_\X(\mathcal{E},f^!\mathcal{E}') \simeq \R f_*(\mathcal{E}^\vee\otimes\omega_f) \otimes \mathcal{E}'.\]
The first isomorphism follows from $\underline{\mathrm{RHom}}_\Y(\R f_!\mathcal{E},\mathcal{E}') \simeq \R f_*\underline{\mathrm{RHom}}_\X(\mathcal{E},f^!\mathcal{E}')$ (which one can check by showing maps into each are the same, and using the tensor/Hom adjunction and the projection formula) and $\R f_! \simeq \R f_*$, while the second is just using the formula $f^!(-)\simeq \omega_f \otimes \mathrm{L} f^*(-)$.

Thus $\R f_*\mathcal{E}$ is dualizable with dual $\R f_*(\mathcal{E}^\vee\otimes\omega_f)$.
<!-- end proof-66 -->
<!-- lemma-42: body_md -->
Let $f:(\X,\mathcal{M}_\X)\to(\Y,\mathcal{M}_\Y)$ be a strict log smooth proper morphism of log $p$-adic formal schemes satisfying Assumption \ref{ass:snc_log_structure} over $\ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}_K$ of pure relative dimension $d$. Then the induced maps on $(\X,\mathcal{M}_\X)^{{\mathbbl{\Delta}},\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\blacksquare$}}}}$ and $(\X,\mathcal{M}_\X)^{\mathcal{L},\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\blacksquare$}}}}$ are cohomologically smooth and weakly cohomologically proper, and on both stacks one has
\[f^!\ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}\simeq\ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}\{d\}[2d].\]
Moreover $\R f_! \simeq \R f_*$ via the canonical map.
\label{lem:prismatic_stack_cohom_smooth_proper}
<!-- end lemma-42 -->
<!-- proof-67: body_md -->
We first will argue this without log structures, and deduce the actual statement of the lemma as a formal consequence.

The underlying map of formal schemes is smooth and proper by strictness. Theorem 4.1.3(C) (using Example 4.3.2 of \cite{Kipp2} to deduce analogous claims for the prismatization) therefore show that the induced map
\[\X^{{\mathbbl{\Delta}},\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\blacksquare$}}}} \longrightarrow \Y^{{\mathbbl{\Delta}},\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\blacksquare$}}}}\]
is cohomologically smooth and weakly cohomologically proper. Using Theorem 4.1.3(F) we also get $f^!\ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}\simeq\ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}\{d\}[2d]$. However, weak cohomological properness is insufficient to deduce the last claim that $\R f_! \simeq \R f_*$ via the canonical map: it only gives a noncanonical isomorphism between these. The main content of this lemma will be to fix this issue, using results from \cite{MikamiDuality}. 

In what follows we use $\@undefined_{\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\blacksquare$}}}}$ to denote the six functor formalism on analytic stacks. Let $\pi_2$ denote the second projection from $\X^{{\mathbbl{\Delta}},\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\blacksquare$}}}}\times_{\Y^{{\mathbbl{\Delta}},\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\blacksquare$}}}}}\X^{{\mathbbl{\Delta}},\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\blacksquare$}}}}$. Weak cohomological properness implies that $f$ is $\@undefined_{\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\blacksquare$}}}}$-prim, so \cite[Corollary 1.28]{MikamiDuality} gives a codualizing object
\[\delta_f\simeq\R\pi_{2,*}\R\Delta_{f,!}\ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}\]
and a natural equivalence $\R f_!(\delta_f\otimes-)\xrightarrow{\sim}\R f_*$.

Thus it remains to trivialize $\delta_f$ canonically. Since $\pi_2\circ\Delta_f=\id$, it is enough to construct a canonical equivalence $\R\Delta_{f,!}\simeq\R\Delta_{f,*}$. Since $f: \X \to \Y$ is smooth and separated, the diagonal $\X \to \X \times_\Y \X$ on the formal schemes is a regular closed immersion and hence locally of finite presentation. The induced map $\Delta_f$ on $(-)^{{\mathbbl{\Delta}},\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\blacksquare$}}}}$ is therefore $!$-able by \cite[Theorem 4.1.3(A)]{Kipp2}. The argument will be to apply \cite[Lemma 1.50]{MikamiDuality}\footnote{See \cite[Definition 1.10]{MikamiDuality} for why it applies to analytic stacks.}, upon which the desired equivalence holds provided that $\Delta_f$ is, universally $\@undefined_{\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\blacksquare$}}}}(-)^*$-locally on its target represented by affine proper morphisms (compare \cite[\S2.1.10]{Kipp2} and the class in \cite[Definition 1.5(2)]{MikamiDuality}).

We now check this is true. Since the functor $\X\mapsto\X^{{\mathbbl{\Delta}},\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\blacksquare$}}}}$ preserves finite limits by \cite[Construction 3.7.1]{Kipp2}, the target of $\Delta_f$ is $(\X\times_\Y\X)^{{\mathbbl{\Delta}},\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\blacksquare$}}}}$. Work on the semiperfectoid cover $\Spa({\mathbbl{\Delta}}_{\R_0},{\mathbbl{\Delta}}_{\R_0})$ of this target from \cite[Construction 3.7.1]{Kipp2}. After taking a Zariski refinement, we can assume $f$ is smooth of pure relative dimension $d$ (as a map of formal schemes), so the diagonal is a regular immersion of codimension $d$. Thus, after this localization, the pullback of $\Delta_f$ on analytic stacks is induced by a derived quotient $\mathrm{S}_0=\R_0\mathord{/\mkern-6mu/}(g_1,\ldots,g_d)$. Choose a perfectoid ring $\R$ surjecting onto $\R_0$, lift the $g_i$ to $f_i\in\R$, and put $\mathrm{S}=\R\mathord{/\mkern-6mu/}(f_1,\ldots,f_d)$, again as a derived quotient. The setup is summarized by the following Cartesian squares:
\begin{display}
\X^{{\mathbbl{\Delta}},\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\blacksquare$}}}} \ar{r}{\Delta_f} & \X^{{\mathbbl{\Delta}},\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\blacksquare$}}}}\times_{\Y^{{\mathbbl{\Delta}},\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\blacksquare$}}}}}\X^{{\mathbbl{\Delta}},\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\blacksquare$}}}} \\
\Spa({\mathbbl{\Delta}}_{\mathrm{S}_0},{\mathbbl{\Delta}}_{\mathrm{S}_0}) \ar{u} \ar{r}{\Delta_{f,\R_0}} \ar{d} & \Spa({\mathbbl{\Delta}}_{\R_0},{\mathbbl{\Delta}}_{\R_0}) \ar{u} \ar{d} \\
\Spa({\mathbbl{\Delta}}_{\mathrm{S}},{\mathbbl{\Delta}}_{\mathrm{S}}) \ar{r} & \Spa({\mathbbl{\Delta}}_{\R},{\mathbbl{\Delta}}_{\R}).
\end{display}
It is therefore enough to show that $\Spa({\mathbbl{\Delta}}_{\mathrm{S}},{\mathbbl{\Delta}}_{\mathrm{S}})\longrightarrow\Spa({\mathbbl{\Delta}}_{\R},{\mathbbl{\Delta}}_{\R})$ is affine proper. Indeed, by construction $\Spa({\mathbbl{\Delta}}_{\R_0},{\mathbbl{\Delta}}_{\R_0})$ is an effective epimorphism of analytic stacks, hence a universal $\@undefined_{\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\blacksquare$}}}}^{*}$-cover. After a further Zariski refinement, the prismatic ideal is $\I=(\widetilde d)$ and we may choose lifts $\widetilde f_i\in{\mathbbl{\Delta}}_\R$ of $f_i\in\R\simeq{\mathbbl{\Delta}}_\R/\I$. One then has
\[{\mathbbl{\Delta}}_{\mathrm{S}}\simeq {\mathbbl{\Delta}}_\R\left\{\frac{\widetilde f_1}{\widetilde d},\ldots,\frac{\widetilde f_d}{\widetilde d}\right\}_{\delta,(p,\widetilde d)}^{\wedge}.\]
Lemma \ref{lem:prismatic_envelope_integral} and \cite[Example 2.1.13]{Kipp2} then show that $\Spa({\mathbbl{\Delta}}_{\mathrm{S}},{\mathbbl{\Delta}}_{\mathrm{S}})\longrightarrow\Spa({\mathbbl{\Delta}}_{\R},{\mathbbl{\Delta}}_{\R})$ is affine proper.

Thus we have verified necessary hypotheses for $\Delta_f$, and hence obtain a natural equivalence $\R\Delta_{f,!}\simeq\R\Delta_{f,*}$. As explained at the start, this shows the claim without log structures.

Deducing the claim with log structures added is immediate using base change. Indeed using strictness,
\[(\X,\mathcal{M}_\X)^{{\mathbbl{\Delta}},\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\blacksquare$}}}}\simeq\X^{{\mathbbl{\Delta}},\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\blacksquare$}}}}\times_{\Y^{{\mathbbl{\Delta}},\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\blacksquare$}}}}}(\Y,\mathcal{M}_\Y)^{{\mathbbl{\Delta}},\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\blacksquare$}}}}.\]
The claimed result for $(\X,\mathcal{M}_\X)^{{\mathbbl{\Delta}},\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\blacksquare$}}}}$ then follows from Lemma \ref{lem:formal_f!} and compatibility of $\R f_!\simeq\R f_*$ with arbitrary base change. For the Laurent stack $(\X,\mathcal{M}_\X)^{\mathcal{L},\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\blacksquare$}}}}$, the claim again follows by base change.
<!-- end proof-67 -->
<!-- proposition-11: body_md -->
For every log formal scheme $(\X,\mathcal{M})$ satisfying Assumption \ref{ass:snc_log_structure}, there is a natural equivalence
\[\mathrm{an}_{(\X,\mathcal{M})}: \@undefined_{\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\blacksquare$}}}}((\X,\mathcal{M})^{\mathcal{L},\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\blacksquare$}}}}) \xrightarrow{\sim} \@undefined_{\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\blacksquare$}}}}((\X,\mathcal{M})_{\mathbbl{\Delta}},\ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}[1/\I_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}]_p^{\wedge}).\]
\label{prop:stack_site_compare}
<!-- end proposition-11 -->
<!-- proof-68: body_md -->
First, the equivalence is local because both sides satisfy strict \'{e}tale descent. For the target this is shown in the appendix in Corollary \ref{cor:laur_strict_etale}. For the source, by construction the stack itself satisfies strict \'{e}tale descent, because $\X^{{\mathbbl{\Delta}},\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\blacksquare$}}}}$ satisfies \'{e}tale descent by using \cite[Theorem 4.1.3(D)]{Kipp2} (again using Example 4.3.2 of \cite{Kipp2} to deduce analogous claims for the prismatization).

Thus we may work on a framed log affine. In this case, there exists a choice of log Breuil-Kisin prism atlas $(\mathrm{A}^+,\I,\mathcal{N})^a$ for this framed log affine such that we obtain the presentation
\[(\X,\mathcal{M})^{{\mathbbl{\Delta}},\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\blacksquare$}}}} = \colim_n \Spa(\mathrm{A}^{+,(n)},\mathrm{A}^{+,(n)})\]
proved in Proposition \ref{prop:log_BK_analytic_presentation}. Base changing to $(\X,\mathcal{M})^{\mathcal{L},\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\blacksquare$}}}}$ we obtain an analogous presentation, but replace the terms $\Spa(\mathrm{A}^{+,(n)},\mathrm{A}^{+,(n)})$ with $\colim_m \Spa(\mathrm{A}^{+,(n)}/p^m[1/\I],\mathrm{A}^{+,(n)}/p^m)$.

In Definition \ref{def:laur_category}, the category $\@undefined_{\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\blacksquare$}}}}(\colim_m \Spa(\mathrm{A}^{+,(n)}/p^m[1/\I],\mathrm{A}^{+,(n)}/p^m))$ is precisely what we assign to the log prisms $\mathrm{A}^{+,(n)}$ appearing in the \v{C}ech nerve of $(\mathrm{A}^+,\I,\mathcal{N})^a$. Combining with Theorem \ref{thm:laur_cech}, we obtain
\[\@undefined_{\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\blacksquare$}}}}((\X,\mathcal{M})_{\mathbbl{\Delta}},\ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}[1/\I_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}]_p^{\wedge}) \simeq \lim_n \@undefined_{\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\blacksquare$}}}}(\colim_m \Spa(\mathrm{A}^{+,(n)}/p^m[1/\I],\mathrm{A}^{+,(n)}/p^m))\simeq \@undefined_{\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\blacksquare$}}}}((\X,\mathcal{M})^{\mathcal{L},\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\blacksquare$}}}}).\]
Thus we get an identification for each log Breuil-Kisin prism. This identification is also independent of choices. One can see this by either assembling together the identifications for every log Breuil-Kisin prism into a canonical one, or noting that a canonical functor exists already. Indeed, for some $(\mathrm{A},(d),\mathcal{N})^a$ in the strict log prismatic site, applying the functor $(-)^{\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\blacksquare$}}}}$ (Definition \ref{def:box_analytic_realization}) to the map of Lemma \ref{lem:log_prism_stack_map} gives
\[\Spa(\mathrm{A},\mathrm{A}) \longrightarrow (\X,\mathcal{M})^{{\mathbbl{\Delta}},\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\blacksquare$}}}},\]
so passing to Laurent stacks yields a canonical functor
\[\@undefined_{\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\blacksquare$}}}}((\X,\mathcal{M})^{\mathcal{L},\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\blacksquare$}}}}) \longrightarrow \@undefined_{\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\blacksquare$}}}}((\X,\mathcal{M})_{\mathbbl{\Delta}},\ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}[1/\I_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}]_p^{\wedge})\]
This we call $\mathrm{an}_{(\X,\mathcal{M})}$.
<!-- end proof-68 -->
<!-- lemma-43: body_md -->
For every $(\X,\mathcal{M})$ satisfying Assumption \ref{ass:snc_log_structure}, there is a functorial symmetric monoidal equivalence
\[\mathrm{an}_{(\X,\mathcal{M})}:  \Perf((\X,\mathcal{M})^{\mathcal{L},\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\blacksquare$}}}}) \xrightarrow{\sim} \Perf((\X,\mathcal{M})_{\mathbbl{\Delta}},\ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}[1/\I_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}]_p^{\wedge}).\]
If $(\Y,\mathcal{N})$ satisfies the same hypothesis and $f:(\X,\mathcal{M})\to(\Y,\mathcal{N})$ is strict log smooth and proper, denote by $f_{\mathcal{L}}$ is the induced map of Laurent analytic stacks. Then the site pushforward $\R f_{{\mathbbl{\Delta}},*}$ preserves $\Perf$ and
\[\mathrm{an}_{(\Y,\mathcal{N})} \R f_{\mathcal{L},*}\simeq \R f_{{\mathbbl{\Delta}},*}\mathrm{an}_{(\X,\mathcal{M})}.\]
\label{lem:kipp_perf_compare}
<!-- end lemma-43 -->
<!-- proof-69: body_md -->
This is formal from the previous results. For the first point, we constructed the functor through pullbacks of stacks so it will be symmetric monoidal. For the second point, this follows by taking right adjoints and observing $\mathrm{an}$ has pullback compatibility.

Once we know this, preservation of $\Perf$ is true on the stack side by applying Lemma \ref{lem:prismatic_stack_cohom_smooth_proper} and Lemma \ref{lem:formal_pushforward_duality}.
<!-- end proof-69 -->
<!-- corollary-8: body_md -->
Let $f:(\X,\mathcal{M})\to(\Y,\mathcal{N})$ be as in Lemma \ref{lem:prismatic_stack_cohom_smooth_proper}, and suppose both source and target satisfy Assumption \ref{ass:snc_log_structure}. Then $f^!\mathcal{F}\simeq f^*\mathcal{F}\{d\}[2d]$ for $\mathcal{F}\in\Perf((\Y,\mathcal{N})_{\mathbbl{\Delta}},\ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}[1/\I_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}]_p^{\wedge})$, and
\[\R f_{{\mathbbl{\Delta}},*}\mathcal{E} \simeq \underline{\mathrm{RHom}}_{\ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}[1/\I_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}]_p^{\wedge}}\bigl(\R f_*(\mathcal{E}^{\vee}\{d\}),\ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}[1/\I_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}]_p^{\wedge}[-2d]\bigr)\]
for every $\mathcal{E}\in\Perf((\X,\mathcal{M})_{\mathbbl{\Delta}},\ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}[1/\I_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}]_p^{\wedge})$.
\label{cor:laurent_prismatic_pd}
<!-- end corollary-8 -->
<!-- proof-70: body_md -->
Transporting Lemma \ref{lem:prismatic_stack_cohom_smooth_proper} through Lemma \ref{lem:kipp_perf_compare} gives $f^!\mathcal{F}\simeq f^*\mathcal{F}\{d\}[2d]$. Lemma \ref{lem:formal_pushforward_duality}, together with the pushforward comparison in Lemma \ref{lem:kipp_perf_compare}, gives
\[(\R f_{{\mathbbl{\Delta}},*}\mathcal{E})^\vee\simeq\R f_{{\mathbbl{\Delta}},*}(\mathcal{E}^\vee\{d\})[2d].\]
Dualizing, this equivalence gives the claim.
<!-- end proof-70 -->
<!-- lemma-44: body_md -->
\label{lem:laurent_cartier_descent}
In the above setting, relative Frobenius induces a fully faithful functor
\[\mathrm{Fr}^*:\Perf(((\X,\mathcal{M}_\X)/\mathrm{A})^{\mathcal{L},\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\blacksquare$}}},(\varphi)}) \longrightarrow \Perf(((\X,\mathcal{M}_\X)/\mathrm{A})^{\mathcal{L},\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\blacksquare$}}}}).\]
<!-- end lemma-44 -->
<!-- proof-71: body_md -->
The projection formula immediately reduces the claim to proving that the unit $\ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}\to\R\mathrm{Fr}_*\ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}$ is an equivalence. Since we have restricted to perfect complexes, we don't need to check $\mathrm{Fr}$ is proper first to use this.

We may also work strict \'{e}tale locally by descent of the source and target (this is again automatic from the claim for $(\X,\mathcal{M}_\X)^{{\mathbbl{\Delta}},\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\blacksquare$}}}}$ by base change): thus we assume that $\X$ is a framed log affine relative to $(\Y,\mathcal{M}_\Y)$ with relative coordinates $\T_1,\ldots,\T_d$. More precisely, we have 
\[(\X,\mathcal{M}_\X) \longrightarrow (\Y,\mathcal{M}_\Y) \times_{\Spf \W(k)[\zeta_{p^\ell}]} \widehat{\mathbf{G}}_m^d \longrightarrow \mathbb{T}^{n+d}_r\]
where $\widehat{\mathbf{G}}_m^d$ has a trivial log structure. Thus $(\X,\mathcal{M}_\X)$ inherits a framing, and has a corresponding log $q$-de Rham prism with ring $\B^+$ and $\B=\B^+[1/(q-1)]_p^{\wedge}$. A straightforward variant of Proposition \ref{prop:Gamma_mod_ff} gives a proper morphism $\rho:[\AnSpf\B/\Z_p^d]\to((\X,\mathcal{M}_\X)/\mathrm{A})^{\mathcal{L},\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\blacksquare$}}}}$ with a fully faithful pullback where $\Z_p^d$ fixes $\mathrm{A}$ and $\gamma_i \cdot \T_j =q^{p^\ell \delta_{ij}}\T_j$ for the generators $\gamma_i$ of $\Z_p^d$. For $\ell=0$, we use the same chart with $\I=([p]_q)$, which still gives a cover over $\W(k)$. In this case $\gamma_i\cdot \T_j =q^{p\delta_{ij}}\T_j$ and $\varphi(\I)=([p]_{q^p})$; the proof is similar for this case so we focus on $\ell \ge 1$.

We first observe that there is a commutative diagram
\begin{display}
{[\AnSpf \B/\Z_p^d]} \ar{d}{\mathrm{F}} \ar{r}{\rho} & ((\X,\mathcal{M}_\X)/\mathrm{A})^{\mathcal{L},\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\blacksquare$}}}} \ar{d}{\mathrm{Fr}} \\
{[\AnSpf \B^{(\varphi)}/\Z_p^d]} \ar{r}{\rho^{(\varphi)}} & ((\X,\mathcal{M}_\X)/\mathrm{A})^{\mathcal{L},\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\blacksquare$}}},(\varphi)}.
\end{display}
Here $\rho^{(\varphi)}$ is the pullback along $\varphi_{\mathrm{A}}$ and $\mathrm{F}$ is induced by the relative Frobenius
\[\B^{(\varphi)} := \B \widehat{\otimes}_{\mathrm{A},\varphi_\mathrm{A}} \mathrm{A} \longrightarrow \mathrm{B}.\]
Moreover, from the argument of Proposition \ref{prop:Gamma_mod_ff} we have seen $\R\rho_* \ensuremath{\mathcal{O}} = \ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}$ and that $\rho$ is proper. We also get $\R \rho_*^{(\varphi)} \ensuremath{\mathcal{O}} \simeq \ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}$ by proper base change.

Now the diagram is useful: from $\R\rho_* \ensuremath{\mathcal{O}} = \ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}$, equivalently we can compute the pushforward along the other path, first computing $\mathrm{F}_* \B$ and then applying $\R \rho_*^{(\varphi)}$. The first part is immediate, as we see
\[\mathrm{F}_* \B \simeq \bigoplus_{\beta\in\{0,\ldots,p-1\}^d} \B^{(\varphi)} \prod_i \T_i^{\beta_i}.\]
where the $\Z_p^d$ action acts on $\T_i$ in the usual way by $\gamma_i \cdot \T_j = q^{p^\ell \delta_{ij}} \T_j$. Now we must compute the pushforward for each summand. For $\beta=0$, we have already seen $\R \rho_*^{(\varphi)} \ensuremath{\mathcal{O}} \simeq \ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}$. Thus our task is to show the remaining summands $\B^{(\varphi)} \prod_i \T_i^{\beta_i} \in \@undefined_{\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\blacksquare$}}}}([\AnSpf \B^{\varphi}/\Z_p^d])$ are killed by $\R \rho^{(\varphi)}_{*}$.

To actually compute this we will need to apply proper base change again. We let $\B^{(1),\varphi}$ be the Frobenius pullback along $\varphi_{\mathrm{A}}$ of the first (Laurentized) term in the \v{C}ech nerve of $\AnSpf \B \to ((\X,\mathcal{M}_\X)/\mathrm{A})^{\mathcal{L},\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\blacksquare$}}}}$  We will instead use the square
\begin{display}
{[\AnSpf \B^{(1),(\varphi)}/\Z_p^d]} \ar{d} \ar{r} & \AnSpf \B^{(\varphi)} \ar{d} \\
{[\AnSpf \B^{(\varphi)}/\Z_p^d]} \ar{r}{\rho^{(\varphi)}} & ((\X,\mathcal{M}_\X)/\mathrm{A})^{\mathcal{L},\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\blacksquare$}}},(\varphi)}.
\end{display}
We know already that the right vertical map is a proper effective epimorphism. We can deduce this using Proposition \ref{prop:log_BK_analytic_presentation}. Thus proper base change reduces us to showing that 
\[\mathrm{R}\Gamma_{\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\blacksquare$}}}}(\Z_p^d, \B^{(1),(\varphi)} \otimes_{\B^{(\varphi)},p_1} \B^{(\varphi)} \prod_i \T_i^{\beta_i}) = 0\]
for $\beta \neq 0$. This is now a self-coproduct in the relative site\footnote{Later in Lemma \ref{lem:mixed_BK_fiber_product}, we compute this first \v{C}ech term in the absolute case (which extends to the Laurent stacks by finite limit compatibility of $(-)^{\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\blacksquare$}}}}$ from Definition \ref{def:box_analytic_realization}). The relative computation follows formally from the absolute case, since for example $\Spf \B \times_{(\X/\mathrm{A})^{{\mathbbl{\Delta}}}} \Spf \B = (\Spf \B^{(1)}) \times_{\Spf \mathrm{A}^{(1)}} \Spf \mathrm{A}$, where $\mathrm{A}^{(1)}$ and $\B^{(1)}$ are the self-coproducts for the absolute sites.}, so we may compute
\[\B^{+,(1),(\varphi)} = \B^{+,(\varphi)}[u_1^{\pm1},\ldots,u_d^{\pm1}]\left\{\frac{u_1-1}{[p]_{q^{p^\ell}}},\ldots,\frac{u_d-1}{[p]_{q^{p^\ell}}}\right\}_{\delta,(p,q-1)}^\wedge.\]
Here $\delta(u_i)=0$ and $u_i=\T_{i,1}/\T_{i,0}$. In particular, the formula is nearly identical to Lemma \ref{lem:qdr_actual_cech_envelope}, so one may run the same argument to embed
\[\B^{+,(1),(\varphi)} \subset \mathrm{C}(\Z_p^d, \B^{+,(\varphi)})\]
such that the mod $p$ reduction, as in Lemma \ref{lem:Cq_criterion}, identifies with the functions
\[\left(\bigoplus_{\alpha \in \N^d}\overline{\B}^{+,(\varphi)} (q^{p^\ell}-1)^{|\alpha|}\binom{x}{\alpha}\right)^{\wedge}_{(q-1)} \subset \mathrm{C}(\Z_p^d, \overline{\B}^{+,(\varphi)}).\]
When we consider $\B^{(1),(\varphi)} \otimes_{\B^{(\varphi)},p_1} \B^{(\varphi)} \prod_i \T_i^{\beta_i}$ this simply twists the $\Z_p^d$ action, instead making
\[\gamma_i \cdot f(x) = q^{p^\ell \beta_i} f(x+e_i)\]
where $e_i$ is the $i$th basis vector in $\Z_p^d$ (and we use $x$ for the full coordinate). Taking any $\beta_i\neq 0$, this shows directly $\fib(\gamma_i-1)$ is zero because $\frac{\gamma_i-1}{q^{p^\ell}-1} = [\beta_i]_{q^{p^\ell}} + q^{p^\ell \beta_i} \frac{\Delta_i}{q^{p^\ell}-1}$ is invertible, where $\Delta_i$ is the finite difference operator. This shows the vanishing modulo $p$ which suffices by derived Nakayama.
<!-- end proof-71 -->
<!-- proposition-12: body_md -->
Let $f:(\X,\mathcal{M}_\X)\to(\Y,\mathcal{M}_\Y)$ be a strict log smooth proper morphism between log formal schemes satisfying Assumption \ref{ass:snc_log_structure} over $\W(k)[\zeta_{p^\ell}]$ with $\ell\geq0$. For every $\mathcal{E}\in\Perf((\X,\mathcal{M}_\X)_{\mathbbl{\Delta}},\ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}[1/\I_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}]_p^{\wedge})$, the canonical map
\[\varphi^*\R f_*\mathcal{E} \longrightarrow \R f_*\varphi^*\mathcal{E}\]
is an isomorphism.
\label{prop:frob_bc}
<!-- end proposition-12 -->
<!-- proof-72: body_md -->
By Proposition \ref{prop:stack_site_compare} and proper base change from Lemma \ref{lem:prismatic_stack_cohom_smooth_proper} we may reduce to the case where $(\Y,\mathcal{M}_\Y)$ is a framed log affine; note here we also use strict \'{e}tale descent from Corollary \ref{cor:laur_strict_etale}. In the $\ell=0$ case the log $q$-de Rham is not a Breuil-Kisin prism; in this case it is still a cover so the argument is similar.

We may evaluate the canonical comparison morphism on a logarithmic $q$-de Rham chart $(\mathrm{A},\I,\M_{\Spf \mathrm{A}})$ of $(\Y,\mathcal{M}_\Y)=(\Spf \mathrm{A}/\I, \M_{\Spf \mathrm{A}/\I})$. Pullback along this chart is conservative (since it gives an effective epimorphism of the log prismatic stack, as in Proposition \ref{prop:log_BK_analytic_presentation}), so we need only check the claim on the relative stack. Also, by strictness $\X$ is smooth over $\Spf \mathrm{A}/\I$. Writing $f_{\mathrm{A}}$ for the structure map $(\X/\mathrm{A})^{\mathcal{L},\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\blacksquare$}}}} \to \AnSpf \mathrm{A}[1/\I]_p^{\wedge} = (\Spf \mathrm{A}/\I / \mathrm{A})^{\mathcal{L},\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\blacksquare$}}}}$, we have a commutative diagram
\begin{display}
((\X,\mathcal{M}_\X)/\mathrm{A})^{\mathcal{L},\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\blacksquare$}}}} \ar{r}{\mathrm{Fr}} \ar{dr}[swap]{f_{\mathrm{A}}} & ((\X,\mathcal{M}_\X)/\mathrm{A})^{\mathcal{L},\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\blacksquare$}}},(\varphi)} \ar{r}{\widetilde{\varphi}_{\mathrm{A}}} \ar{d}{f_{\mathrm{A}}^{(\varphi)}} & ((\X,\mathcal{M}_\X)/\mathrm{A})^{\mathcal{L},\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\blacksquare$}}}} \ar{d}{f_{\mathrm{A}}} \\
& \AnSpf \mathrm{A}[1/\I]_p^{\wedge} \ar{r}{\varphi_{\mathrm{A}}} & \AnSpf \mathrm{A}[1/\I]_p^{\wedge}
\end{display}
whose right square is Cartesian, so $\widetilde{\varphi}_{\mathrm{A}}$ is the base change of $\varphi_{\mathrm{A}}$ along $f_{\mathrm{A}}$, and $\widetilde{\varphi}_{\mathrm{A}}\circ\mathrm{Fr}=\varphi$. Put $\mathcal{E}^{(\varphi)}=\widetilde{\varphi}_{\mathrm{A}}^*\mathcal{E}$. Proper base change and Lemma \ref{lem:laurent_cartier_descent} give
\[\begin{aligned}
\varphi_{\mathrm{A}}^*\R f_{\mathrm{A},*}\mathcal{E}
&\simeq\R f_{\mathrm{A},*}^{(\varphi)}\mathcal{E}^{(\varphi)}\\
&\xrightarrow{\sim}\R f_{\mathrm{A},*}^{(\varphi)}\R\mathrm{Fr}_*\mathrm{Fr}^*\mathcal{E}^{(\varphi)}
\simeq\R f_{\mathrm{A},*}\varphi^*\mathcal{E}.
\end{aligned}\]
Thus the claim follows.
<!-- end proof-72 -->
<!-- theorem-10: body_md -->
Let $f: (\X,\mathcal{M}_\X) \to (\Y,\mathcal{M}_\Y)$ be strict log smooth proper, where the source and target satisfy Assumption \ref{ass:snc_log_structure} over $\Spf \W(k)[\zeta_{p^\ell}]$. Then $\R f_+$ induces a functor
\[\R f_+: \@undefined_{\fgu}((\X,\mathcal{M}_\X)_{\mathbbl{\Delta}},\ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}[1/\I_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}]_p^{\wedge}) \longrightarrow \@undefined_{\fgu}((\Y,\mathcal{M}_\Y)_{\mathbbl{\Delta}},\ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}[1/\I_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}]_p^{\wedge}).\]
\label{thm:fgu_pushforward}
<!-- end theorem-10 -->
<!-- proof-73: body_md -->
Since the finitely generated unit category is stable under shifts and twists we may test the assertion for $\R f_*$. We may also test the assertion modulo $p$ by derived Nakayama, and further reduce to the case where the $p$-torsion input $\mathcal{E}$ lies in the heart. Then by Corollary \ref{cor:global_root_fgu_condition}, there is a coherent root $\mathcal{E}_0$ of $\mathcal{E}$. But then since $\R f_* \simeq \R f_!$ canonically in this situation on the Laurent stacks and Proposition \ref{prop:stack_site_compare}, the pushforward commutes with colimits. In particular,
\[\R f_* (\colim_n \varphi^{*n} \mathcal{E}_0) \simeq \colim_n \R f_* \varphi^{*n} \mathcal{E}_0.\]
By Proposition \ref{prop:frob_bc} we see this is $\colim_n \varphi^{*n} \R f_* \mathcal{E}_0$. Using Lemma \ref{lem:kipp_perf_compare}, we see $\R f_* \mathcal{E}_0$ is perfect, which proves the result is finitely generated unit.
<!-- end proof-73 -->
<!-- theorem-11: body_md -->
\label{thm:fgu_pushforward_compat}
Let $f:(\X,\mathcal{M}_\X)\to(\Y,\mathcal{M}_\Y)$ be a strict log smooth proper morphism of pure relative dimension $d$ where both satisfy Assumption \ref{ass:snc_log_structure} over $\Spf \W(k)[\zeta_{p^\ell}]$ whose log adic generic fibers are pure of dimensions $d_\X$ and $d_\Y$ respectively. Let $\@undefined_\X$ and $\@undefined_\Y$ be horizontal normal crossings divisors inducing $\M_\X$ and $\M_\Y$. There is a commutative diagram
\begin{display}
\@undefined_{\fgu}((\X,\mathcal{M}_\X)_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}, \ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}[1/\I_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}]_p^{\wedge})^\op \ar{r}{\T_{\ensuremath{\mathrm{\acute{e}t}},\X}[d_\X]} \ar{d}{\R f_* \{d\} [d]} & \@undefined^{(b)}_{\cons,\@undefined_\X}((\X,\mathcal{M}_\X)_\eta,\Z_p) \ar{d}{\R f_{\eta,*}} \\
\@undefined_{\fgu}((\Y,\mathcal{M}_\Y)_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}, \ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}[1/\I_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}]_p^{\wedge})^\op \ar{r}{\T_{\ensuremath{\mathrm{\acute{e}t}},\Y}[d_\Y]} & \@undefined^{(b)}_{\cons,\@undefined_\Y}((\Y,\mathcal{M}_\Y)_\eta,\Z_p).
\end{display}
<!-- end theorem-11 -->
<!-- proof-74: body_md -->
Theorem \ref{thm:fgu_pushforward} and Corollary \ref{cor:pullback} allow us to restrict the pushforward and pullback functors to the finitely generated unit categories. For $\mathcal{E}$ on $\X$ and $\mathcal{F}$ on $\Y$, transporting Lemma \ref{lem:prismatic_stack_cohom_smooth_proper} through Proposition \ref{prop:stack_site_compare} and using the projection formula give
\[
\begin{aligned}
\RHom(\R f_+\mathcal{E}[d],\mathcal{F})
&\simeq\RHom(\R f_*(\mathcal{E}\{d\}[2d]),\mathcal{F})\\
&\simeq\RHom(\mathcal{E}\{d\}[2d],f^!\mathcal{F})
\simeq\RHom(\mathcal{E},\mathrm{L} f^*\mathcal{F}).
\end{aligned}
\]
Thus $\R f_+[d]$ is left adjoint to $\mathrm{L} f^*$. The units and counits in this calculation are Frobenius compatible (see the remark after Corollary \ref{cor:laurent_prismatic_pd}), so the adjunction persists after applying $(-)^{\varphi=1}$ to all categories in sight. 

The functor $\R f_{\eta,*}$ also preserves $p$-Kummer constructible complexes, so the adjunction $\mathrm{L} f_\eta^*\leftrightarrows\R f_{\eta,*}$ restricts to these categories.
