To see this, first observe proper smooth pushforward preserves lissity on each logarithmic stratum. It is easy to check the $p$-Kummer condition is preserved as well: one may use a spectral sequence to understand the prime-to-$p$ log inertia on the pushforward at a geometric stalk.\footnote{If one uses a spectral sequence to argue this, it is important to note invariants for the prime-to-$p$ log inertia are exact. In particular it will again act trivially on extensions, which is why on the abutment of the spectral sequence it will still act trivially if it does on the $\E_2$ page.}

We already saw that $\R f_+[d]$ is left adjoint to $\mathrm{L} f^*$. Pullback compatibility of $\T_\ensuremath{\mathrm{\acute{e}t}}$ yields
\[\T_{\ensuremath{\mathrm{\acute{e}t}},\X}^{-1} \circ \mathrm{L} f_\eta^* \rightleftarrows \T_{\ensuremath{\mathrm{\acute{e}t}},\Y}\circ(\R f_+[d]).\]
Note here to transport the adjunction we are using the equivalence in \ref{thm:RH_main} and that $\R f_+[d]$ preserves the crystal side and that $\mathrm{L} f_\eta^*$ preserves $p$-Kummer sheaves.

Uniqueness of right adjoints therefore gives
\[\T_{\ensuremath{\mathrm{\acute{e}t}},\Y}(\R f_+\mathcal{E}[d])\simeq\R f_{\eta,*}\T_{\ensuremath{\mathrm{\acute{e}t}},\X}(\mathcal{E}).\]
Here we have used the previous observation that $\R f_{\eta,*}$ preserves $p$-Kummer constructible sheaves. Since $d_\X=d_\Y+d$ this yields the asserted commutative diagram.
<!-- end proof-74 -->
<!-- remark-17: body_md -->
\label{rem:perfectoid_base}
Let $K$ be a characteristic zero perfectoid field containing a compatible system of $p$-power roots of unity. We introduce a new prism $\A_{\inf,\R}^{\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\square$}}}}$, similar to the construction in \cite{MinWangRelativePhiGamma}. For $\R=\ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}_{K} \langle \T_1,\ldots,\T_r, \T_{r+1}^\pm,\ldots,\T_n^\pm\rangle$ we use the log prism
\[(\A_{\inf}(\ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}_{K}) \langle \T_1,\ldots,\T_r, \T_{r+1}^\pm,\ldots,\T_n^\pm \rangle_{(p,\I)}, \I,\mathcal{M}_{\V(\T_1\cdots\T_r)} )^a\]
where $\I = \ker(\theta: \A_{\inf}(\ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}_{K}) \to \ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}_{K})$. For a general framed log affine over $\ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}_{K}$, it has a strict \'{e}tale framing $\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\square$}}}$ to $\Spf \ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}_{K} \langle \T_1,\ldots,\T_r, \T_{r+1}^\pm,\ldots,\T_n^\pm\rangle$ with the log structure $\mathcal{M}_{\V(\T_1\cdots\T_r)}$. Similar to the construction of the log $q$-de Rham prism we may lift along the framing to obtain the desired log prism with ring $\A_{\inf,\R}^{\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\square$}}}}$. We note the mod $p$ reduction of $\A_{\inf,\R}^{\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\square$}}}}[1/\I]_p^{\wedge}$ is regular $F$-finite (it will be an affinoid algebra over $K^\flat$ \'{e}tale over $K^\flat \langle \T_1,\ldots,\T_r, \T_{r+1}^\pm,\ldots,\T_n^\pm\rangle$). 

This prism is equipped with a $\Z_p(1)^n$ action, and all arguments in the appendix for Breuil-Kisin atlases (indeed as this \text{is} a Breuil-Kisin atlas) readily adapt to this prism. In particular, all results thus far admit a simpler variant where we simply ignore the $\Z_p^\times$ component of $\Gamma$ in the argument. Indeed the arguments which deal with something beyond the toric part of the action (so they do not adapt word for word) are Proposition \ref{prop:open_decompletion_hom} and Lemma \ref{lem:Cech_cohomology}. In the first we may make the same reduction to mod $p$ vector bundle coefficients, and then in calculating the cohomology we can skip $\mathrm{A}_{\perf}^{\circ,\mathrm{cyc}}$. The method is identical, with the helper lemma for the cyclotomic part not being needed. In Lemma \ref{lem:Cech_cohomology} the argument is identical, just omitting the $\eta_{0,m}$ from the basis. For the toric component, put $q=[(1,\zeta_p,\zeta_{p^2},\ldots)^{1/p}]$, so $\I=([p]_q)$ and $\gamma_i(\T_j)=q^{p\delta_{ij}}\T_j$. One may also argue as in Lemma \ref{lem:laurent_cartier_descent} that the toric part of $\Gamma$ action acts by $(\gamma_i-1)\eta_\alpha=(q-1)u_i \eta_{\alpha'}$ where $\alpha'$ is the same multi-index but with the $i$th position lowered by one, and negative indices mean zero. In particular the same argument also shows the desired cohomology calculation. Elsewhere, arguments adapt verbatim.
<!-- end remark-17 -->
<!-- definition-13: body_md -->
\label{def:Olsson_stack}
Let $(\X,\mathcal{M})$ be a bounded fs log formal scheme. Then there is a map $\X \to \mathrm{Log}$ induced by the log structure. We define $(\X,\mathcal{M})^{{\mathbbl{\Delta}}}$ to be the fiber product
\begin{display}
(\X,\mathcal{M})^{{\mathbbl{\Delta}}} \ar{d} \ar{r} & \X^{{\mathbbl{\Delta}}} \ar{d} \\
\mathrm{Log} \times \Z_p^{\mathbbl{\Delta}} \ar{r}{\pi_{\mathrm{Log}}} & \mathrm{Log}^{{\mathbbl{\Delta}}}.
\end{display}
This is the log prismatic stack introduced by Olsson in
\cite{OlssonLogPrismaticStack}.\footnote{We note that the definition of this stack was also considered by Koshikawa.}
<!-- end definition-13 -->
<!-- definition-14: body_md -->
Let $(\X,\mathcal{M})$ satisfy Assumption \ref{ass:snc_log_structure} over $\ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}_K$. A logarithmic Breuil-Kisin prism for $(\X,\mathcal{M})$ is a log prism $(\mathrm{A},\I,\M_{\Spf \mathrm{A}})^a$ such that
\[(\Spf \mathrm{A}/\I, \M_{\Spf \mathrm{A}/\I}) \longrightarrow (\X,\mathcal{M})\]
is a strict open immersion of log $p$-adic formal schemes.
<!-- end definition-14 -->
<!-- lemma-45: body_md -->
\label{lem:standard_log_BK_prism}
Let $(\X,\mathcal{M})=(\Spf\R,\mathcal{M})$ be a framed log affine over $\ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}_K$. Then there is a logarithmic Breuil-Kisin prism $(\mathrm{A},\I,\M_{\Spf\mathrm{A}})^a$ which is an atlas for $(\X,\mathcal{M})$.
<!-- end lemma-45 -->
<!-- proof-75: body_md -->
This construction is also explained in \cite[Construction 5.10]{Inoue}, but we explain it again here for convenience of the reader.

First suppose $K/\W(k)[1/p]$ is finite with residue field $k$. Write $\R\simeq\R_0\widehat\otimes_{\W(k)}\ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}_K$ by the remark after Definition \ref{def:fr_log_aff}. 

We first review what happens for a point. Choose a uniformizer $\pi$ of $\ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}_K$ with Eisenstein polynomial $\E(u)$, and give $\mathfrak{S}=\W(k)\llbracket u \rrbracket$ the $\delta$ structure with Frobenius $u\mapsto u^p$ (with the Witt vector Frobenius on $\W(k)$). This makes $(\mathfrak{S},(\E(u)))$ a Breuil-Kisin prism for $\ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}_K$. When $\ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}_K=\W(k)[\zeta_{p^\ell}]$ as in our applications, we may use the $q$-de Rham prism $(\W(k)\llbracket q-1 \rrbracket,(\varphi^{\ell-1}([p]_q)))$ with $q\mapsto q^p$ (for $\ell \ge 1$); this is also a Breuil-Kisin prism under our definition. We discuss a general construction compatible with the first case, but a similar construction works in the second case.

For a framed log affine, give
\[\mathbb{T}_r^n = \Spf \W(k)\langle \T_1,\ldots,\T_r,\T_{r+1}^{\pm 1},\ldots,\T_n^{\pm 1}\rangle\]
the Frobenius lift induced by $\T_i \mapsto \T_i^p$. Since $\R_0$ is $p$-completely \'{e}tale over its ring of functions, we may lift Frobenius uniquely to $\R_0$. We then set
\[\mathrm{A}=(\R_0\otimes_{\W(k)}\mathfrak{S})^{\wedge}_{(p,\E(u))}\]
with prismatic ideal $\E(u)$ and the chart $\N^r\to\mathrm{A}$ sending the $i$th generator to $\T_i$ and $\delta_{\log}(e_i)=0$, giving a bounded fine log prism. One may check
\[(\Spf\mathrm{A}/\I,\M_{\Spf\mathrm{A}/\I}) \simeq (\X,\mathcal{M}).\]
<!-- end proof-75 -->
<!-- lemma-46: body_md -->
\label{lem:log_prism_stack_map}
Let $(\X,\mathcal{M})$ satisfy Assumption \ref{ass:snc_log_structure} over $\ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}_K$, and let $(\mathrm{A},\I,\mathcal{N})^a$ be a bounded log prism with fine log structure and a strict map $(\Spf\mathrm{A}/\I,\mathcal{N}|_{\Spf\mathrm{A}/\I})\longrightarrow(\X,\mathcal{M})$. Then there is a natural map 
\[\rho_{\X,\mathrm{A}}:\Spf\mathrm{A} \longrightarrow (\X,\mathcal{M})^{\mathbbl{\Delta}}.\]

If $(\X,\mathcal{M})$ is a framed log affine and $(\mathrm{A},\I,\mathcal{N})^a$ is the logarithmic Breuil-Kisin prism associated with its framing, then $\rho_{\X,\mathrm{A}}$ is an fpqc epimorphism.
<!-- end lemma-46 -->
<!-- proof-76: body_md -->
Construction 8.14 of \cite{APC2} gives a map $\Spf\mathrm{A} \to \X^{\mathbbl{\Delta}}$, using the prism structure. Using the definition of $(\X,\mathcal{M})^{{\mathbbl{\Delta}}}$ as a relative prismatic stack with respect to $\mathrm{Log}$, it remains to complete the diagram
\begin{display}
\Spf \mathrm{A} \ar{r} \ar[dashed]{d} & \X^{{\mathbbl{\Delta}}} \ar{d} \\
\Z_p^{\mathbbl{\Delta}} \times \mathrm{Log} \ar{r}{\pi_{\mathrm{Log}}} & \mathrm{Log}^{{\mathbbl{\Delta}}}.
\end{display}
Currently we are missing the dashed arrow as we have not used the log structure, but this is supplied because $\mathcal{M}_{\Spf \mathrm{A}}$ gives a map to $\mathrm{Log}$, with the other component being the classifying map to $\Z_p^{{\mathbbl{\Delta}}}$; unwinding definitions and using that we have a log prism one may check the composites to $\mathrm{Log}^{\mathbbl{\Delta}}$ agree, so we get the desired map.

Now suppose $(\X,\mathcal{M})$ is a framed log affine. In this situation, Lemma \ref{lem:chart_log_prism} supplies an fpqc epimorphism 
\[\rho_{\X,\B_{\mathrm{P}}}:\Spf \B_{\mathrm{P}} \longrightarrow (\X,\mathcal{M})^{{\mathbbl{\Delta}}}.\]
We may check whether $\rho_{\X,\mathrm{A}}: \Spf \mathrm{A} \to (\X,\mathcal{M})^{{\mathbbl{\Delta}}}$ is an fpqc epimorphism after base change along one, and indeed we obtain
\begin{display}
\Spf (\mathrm{A} \coprod_* \B_{\mathrm{P}}) \ar{r} \ar{d} & \Spf \B_{\mathrm{P}} \ar{d} \\
\Spf \mathrm{A} \ar{r}{\rho_{\X,\mathrm{A}}} & (\X,\mathcal{M})^{{\mathbbl{\Delta}}}
\end{display}
using Lemma \ref{lem:mixed_BK_fiber_product} (which only uses the first part of this lemma). Here $(\mathrm{A} \coprod_* \B_{\mathrm{P}})$ is the coproduct in the category of log prisms $(\X,\mathcal{M})_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}^{\mathrm{op}}$ which exists by Lemma \ref{lem:prism_coproduct}. But one can directly check that 
\[\Spf (\mathrm{A} \coprod_* \B_{\mathrm{P}}) \longrightarrow \Spf \B_{\mathrm{P}}\] 
is fpqc as it is a prismatic envelope of a $(p,\I)$-completely regular sequence, using \cite[Proposition 3.13]{BhattScholzePrisms} (as constructed in Lemma \ref{lem:prism_coproduct}). This proves the claim.
<!-- end proof-76 -->
<!-- lemma-47: body_md -->
\label{lem:prism_coproduct}
Let $(\X,\mathcal{M})$ be a framed log affine over $\ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}_K$ with $\X=\Spf\R$, let $(\mathrm{A},\I,\M_{\Spf\mathrm{A}})^a$ be the logarithmic Breuil-Kisin prism associated with its framing, and let $(\B,(d),\mathcal{N})^a$ be an orientable bounded strict object of $(\X,\mathcal{M})_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}$. The coproduct $\mathrm{A}\coprod_*\B$ in $(\X,\mathcal{M})_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}^\op$ exists.
<!-- end lemma-47 -->
<!-- proof-77: body_md -->
We recall that the construction in Lemma \ref{lem:standard_log_BK_prism} has several variants: the first uses the usual Breuil-Kisin prism with prismatic ideal $\E(u)$ generated by an Eisenstein polynomial of a uniformizer $\pi$, or we may use a log $q$-de Rham prism. The argument in each case is very similar, so we will focus on the first case (the answer in the $q$-de Rham case, at least for a self-coproduct, is already recorded in Lemma \ref{lem:qdr_actual_cech_envelope}). The general argument is analogous to \cite[Proposition 4.13]{KoshikawaLogPrismaticI}.

Write $\R=\R_0\widehat\otimes_{\W(k)}\ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}_K$, with the strict \'{e}tale framing
\[\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\square$}}}: (\Spf \R_0,\N^r) \longrightarrow \bigl(\Spf \W(k)\langle\T_1,\ldots,\T_r,\T_{r+1}^{\pm1},\ldots,\T_n^{\pm1}\rangle, \N^r\bigr).\]
We keep $\E(u)$ as a choice of Eisenstein polynomial for a choice of uniformizer $\pi$. From Lemma \ref{lem:standard_log_BK_prism}, we construct $\mathrm{A}=\R_0 \llbracket u \rrbracket$ and $\I=(\E(u))$, where $u, \T_i$ are sent to $0$ by $\delta$; it is equipped with a log structure with prelog chart $\N^r$ lifted along the framing.

We wish to construct the coproduct $\mathrm{A}\coprod_*\B$. For the other log prism $(\B,(d),\mathcal{N})^a$, put $\overline{\B}=\B/d$. By strictness and \cite[Lemma 3.8]{KoshikawaLogPrismaticI} we get a chart $\N^r \to \Gamma(\Spf\B,\mathcal{N})$ with $e_i\mapsto m_i \in \Gamma(\Spf\B,\mathcal{N})$ (using the lemma to lift the sections on $\Gamma(\Spf \B/d, \mathcal{N}|_{\B/d})$ which is pulled back from $\mathcal{M}$ by strictness). Write $\alpha:\Gamma(\Spf\B,\mathcal{N})\to \B$ for the log structure map on global sections. For $\mathrm{A}$, we denote by $e_i$ the analogous log sections $\N^r \to \mathrm{A}$ which are sent modulo $\E(u)$ to $\T_i$. 

The coproduct $\mathrm{C}=\mathrm{A}\coprod_*\B$ is characterized by its universal property, which we will match directly with an explicit construction. To do this we must construct a log prism $\mathrm{C}$ with maps from $\mathrm{A}$ and $\B$ such that, for every bounded test log prism $\mathrm{S}$ over $(\X,\mathcal{M})$,
\[\Hom_{(\X,\mathcal{M})_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}^{\mathrm{op}}}(\mathrm{C},\mathrm{S}) \simeq \Hom_{(\X,\mathcal{M})_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}^{\mathrm{op}}}(\mathrm{A},\mathrm{S}) \times \Hom_{(\X,\mathcal{M})_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}^{\mathrm{op}}}(\B,\mathrm{S}).\]
For a pair $f:\mathrm{A}\to\mathrm{S}$ and $g:\B\to\mathrm{S}$ on the right side, rigidity of prisms shows the prismatic ideal of $\mathrm{S}$ is $d\mathrm{S}$. We work with the strict site and $f$ and $g$ are morphisms of prisms over $(\X,\mathcal{M})$, so log sections $g(m_i)$ and $f(e_i)$ are forced to have the same reduction. Then Lemma 3.8 of \cite{KoshikawaLogPrismaticI} gives us a unique unit $\lambda_i\in 1+d\mathrm{S}$ such that $g(m_i)=\lambda_i f(e_i)$. 

Now we construct $\mathrm{C}$ with this property by matching with the universal property of a prismatic envelope. We adjoin variables $v_i$ representing these units $\lambda_i$. Form
\[\@undefined_0^{\mathrm{ex}}=\left((\R_0[u]\otimes_{\W(k)} \B)[v_1^{\pm1},\ldots,v_r^{\pm1}]/(\alpha(m_i)-v_i\T_i)_{i=1}^r\right)^{\wedge}_{(p,d)}.\]
Recall $\alpha:\Gamma(\Spf\B,\mathcal{N})\to \B$ is the log structure map. Give this ring the log structure pulled back from $\B$ and set the $\delta$ (or rather $\delta_{\log}$) structure as $\delta(v_i)=v_i^p\delta_{\log}(m_i)$.\footnote{This construction is realized as exactification of a $\delta_{\log}$-triple as in \cite[Construction 2.17]{KoshikawaLogPrismaticI}.}

Using the maps $\R_0[u]\to \R \to \overline{\B}$, $\B \to \overline{\B}$, and $v_i \mapsto 1$ we obtain
\[q_0: \@undefined_0^{\mathrm{ex}} \to \overline{\B}.\]
Using the framing $\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\square$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\square$}}}$ and noting $\T_i=\alpha(m_i)/v_i$ for $i\leq r$ to eliminate these variables we see $\@undefined_0^{\mathrm{ex}}$ is $(p,d)$-completely smooth over $\B$ of relative dimension $n+1$ (these come from $u$, the remaining $\T_i$ for $r<i\le n$, and the $v_i$). Locally $\ker(q_0)=(d,x_1,\ldots,x_{n+1})$, with the $x_j$ a $(p,d)$-completely regular sequence relative to $\B$ (in the sense of \cite[Definition 2.42]{BhattScholzePrisms}). We finally construct $\mathrm{C}$ as the prismatic envelope
\[\mathrm{C}=\left(\@undefined_0^{\mathrm{ex}}\{x_1/d,\ldots,x_{n+1}/d\}_\delta\right)^{\wedge}_{(p,d,\E)},\]
with the naturally induced log structure from $\@undefined_0^{\mathrm{ex}}$. The map $\B\to\mathrm{C}$ makes it so $\mathrm{C}$ is a strict log prism in $(\X,\mathcal{M})_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}^\op$. Since $\E(u)\in\ker(q_0)$ maps into $d\mathrm{C}$, the map $\R_0[u]\to\mathrm{C}$ extends to a log prism map $\mathrm{A}\to\mathrm{C}$.

Now we need to match the universal properties. Recall that the universal property of this prismatic envelope is that for each prism $(\mathrm{S},\I_{\mathrm{S}})$ and $\delta$-map
\[h: \@undefined_0^{\mathrm{ex}} \longrightarrow \mathrm{S}\]
carrying $\ker(q_0)$ into $\I_{\mathrm{S}}$ there is a unique compatible map $\mathrm{C} \to \mathrm{S}$. 

Now suppose we have for some test log prism $\mathrm{S}$, two log prism maps over $(\X,\mathcal{M})$: $\mathrm{A} \to \mathrm{S}$ and $\B \to \mathrm{S}$. Then the construction of $\@undefined_0^{\mathrm{ex}}$ makes it so that there is a unique $\delta_{\log}$-map
\[\@undefined_0^{\mathrm{ex}} \longrightarrow \mathrm{S}\]
that carries $v_i$ to $\lambda_i$. The maps agree over $(\X,\mathcal{M})$, forcing this map to also carry $\ker(q_0)$ into $\I_{\mathrm{S}}$. Now we use the universal property of the prismatic envelope: there is a unique compatible map $\mathrm{C} \to \mathrm{S}$, which is forced to be a map of log prisms. This gives an injection 
\[\Hom_{(\X,\mathcal{M})_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}^{\mathrm{op}}}(\mathrm{A},\mathrm{S}) \times \Hom_{(\X,\mathcal{M})_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}^{\mathrm{op}}}(\B,\mathrm{S}) \hookrightarrow \Hom_{(\X,\mathcal{M})_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}^{\mathrm{op}}}(\mathrm{C},\mathrm{S}).\]
It is surjective, since we can restrict a log prism map $h: \mathrm{C} \to \mathrm{S}$ along the log prism maps $\mathrm{A} \to \mathrm{C}$ and $\B \to \mathrm{C}$ to obtain $f$ and $g$. These must satisfy $g(m_i) = h(v_i) f(e_i)$ by construction, where $h(v_i)\in 1 + \I_{\mathrm{S}}$. But then by uniqueness we get $h(v_i)=\lambda_i \in 1 + \I_{\mathrm{S}}$, and it follows that the map 
\[\@undefined_0^{\mathrm{ex}} \longrightarrow \mathrm{S}\]
we then obtain is $h|_{\@undefined_0^{\mathrm{ex}}}$, so by the previous procedure we recover $h$ from $f$ and $g$.
<!-- end proof-77 -->
<!-- lemma-48: body_md -->
\label{lem:mixed_BK_fiber_product}
Let $(\X,\mathcal{M})$ be a framed log affine over $\ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}_K$ and let $(\mathrm{A},\I,\M_{\Spf\mathrm{A}})^a$ be the logarithmic Breuil-Kisin prism associated with its framing. Let $(\B,(d),\mathcal{N})^a$ be an bounded log prism in $(\X,\mathcal{M})_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}^\op$. Then
\[\Spf(\mathrm{A}\coprod_*\B)\simeq\Spf\mathrm{A}\times_{(\X,\mathcal{M})^{\mathbbl{\Delta}}}\Spf\B.\]
The analogous assertion also holds with trivial log structures.
<!-- end lemma-48 -->
<!-- proof-78: body_md -->
By Lemma \ref{lem:prism_coproduct}, the coproduct exists and therefore the statement makes sense. We will use the notation of Lemma \ref{lem:prism_coproduct}, with $\overline{\B}=\B/d$. 

In the situation of a framed log affine, the log structure factors as $\X \to \mathcal{A}_{\N^r} \to \mathrm{Log}$. Here $\mathcal{A}_{\N^r}\to\mathrm{Log}$ is an \'{e}tale chart for the log stack, given by $\mathcal{A}_{\mathrm{P}}:=[\Spf \Z_p\langle \mathrm{P}\rangle/\Spf \Z_p\langle \mathrm{P}^{\mathrm{gp}}\rangle]$. This fact is useful because in the definition of $(\X,\mathcal{M})^{{\mathbbl{\Delta}}}$ it allows us to replace all instances of $\mathrm{Log}$ with $\mathcal{A}_{\N^r}$. That is,
\[(\X,\mathcal{M})^{\mathbbl{\Delta}} \simeq (\X/\mathcal{A}_{\N^r})^{\mathbbl{\Delta}}.\]
In what follows, we will use the diagram
\begin{display}
\X \ar{r}{\mathrm{id}} \ar{d} & \X \ar{d} & \Spf \overline{\B} \ar{l} \ar{d} \\
\Spf\mathrm{A} \ar{r} & \mathcal{A}_{\N^r} & \Spf \B \ar{l}.
\end{display}
Taking relative prismatic stacks on the columns and noting $(\X/\Spf\mathrm{A})^{\mathbbl{\Delta}} \simeq \Spf\mathrm{A}$ and $(\Spf \overline{\B}/\Spf\B)^{\mathbbl{\Delta}} \simeq \Spf\B$, we get maps
\[\Spf \mathrm{A} \longrightarrow (\X,\mathcal{M})^{\mathbbl{\Delta}} \longleftarrow \Spf \B.\]
Revisiting the construction in Lemma \ref{lem:log_prism_stack_map}, these are precisely $\rho_{\X,\mathrm{A}}$ and $\rho_{\X,\B}$.

Even better, using finite limit compatibility of the relative prismatization in this diagram (for $\delta$-pairs by \cite[Lemma 4.20]{AKNRelativeDelta}) we obtain
\[\Spf\mathrm{A} \times_{(\X,\mathcal{M})^{\mathbbl{\Delta}}} \Spf\B \simeq \left(\Spf\bar{\B}/\bigl(\Spf\mathrm{A}\times^{\R}_{\mathcal{A}_{\N^r}}\Spf\B\bigr)\right)^{\mathbbl{\Delta}}.\]
We will compute the relative prismatic stack on the right, showing that it is discrete. Using the presentation $\mathcal{A}_{\N^r}=[\Spf\Z_p\langle \N^r\rangle/\mathbf{G}_m^r]$ we may compute the denominator $\Spf\mathrm{A}\times^{\R}_{\mathcal{A}_{\N^r}}\Spf\B$ explicitly as
\[\Spf\left((\mathrm{A}\otimes^{\mathrm{L}}_{\Z_p}\B)[v_1^{\pm1},\ldots,v_r^{\pm1}]\mathord{/\mkern-6mu/} (\alpha(m_i)-v_i\T_i)_{i=1}^r\right)^{\wedge}_{(p,\E,d)}.\]
Here $v_i$ are the coordinates on $\mathbf{G}_m^r$, and the map from $\Spf \overline{\B}$ is given by $v_i \mapsto 1$.

This is \textit{very} similar to the construction in Lemma \ref{lem:prism_coproduct}, but with one difference. Let us recall exactly what this construction did. From Lemma \ref{lem:prism_coproduct}, the $\E$-completion $\@undefined^{\mathrm{ex}}$ has the presentation
\[\@undefined^{\mathrm{ex}}=\left((\mathrm{A}\otimes^{\mathrm{L}}_{\W(k)}\B)[v_1^{\pm1},\ldots,v_r^{\pm1}]\mathord{/\mkern-6mu/} (\alpha(m_i)-v_i\T_i)_{i=1}^r\right)^{\wedge}_{(p,\E,d)}.\]
Note this completion is harmless as ultimately we will get the same prismatic envelope. The difference is then clear: we have changed from $\Z_p$ to $\W(k)$. The maps $\W(k)\longrightarrow \overline{\B}$ induced by $\mathrm{A}$ and $\B$ agree. Now since $\W(k)$ is $p$-completely formally \'{e}tale over $\Z_p$, the canonical map
\[\left( \overline{\B}/\@undefined^{\mathrm{ex}} \right)^{\mathbbl{\Delta}} \xrightarrow{\sim}
\left(\Spf \overline{\B}/\bigl(\Spf\mathrm{A}\times^{\R}_{\mathcal{A}_{\N^r}}\Spf\B\bigr)\right)^{\mathbbl{\Delta}}\]
is an equivalence (see \cite[Lemma 5.9]{AKNRelativeDelta}. The proof shows a comparison of stacks, even though it is stated for cohomology). Thus this distinction is irrelevant.

Now it remains to compute $\left(\overline{\B}/\@undefined^{\mathrm{ex}}\right)^{\mathbbl{\Delta}}$. By \cite[Theorem 7.17]{APC2} to do so, we then see
\[\Spf\mathrm{A}\times_{(\X,\mathcal{M})^{\mathbbl{\Delta}}}\Spf\B \simeq \Spf {\mathbbl{\Delta}}_{\bar{\B}/\@undefined^{\mathrm{ex}}}.\]
This may be computed directly as a prismatic envelope as $\bar{\B}$ is locally cut out by a Koszul regular sequence in $\@undefined^{\mathrm{ex}}/d$, and as previously observed this prismatic envelope is the same as the one computed using $\@undefined_0^{\mathrm{ex}}$. Thus in Lemma \ref{lem:prism_coproduct} we have shown this is $\Spf (\mathrm{A} \coprod_* \B)$ where the coproduct is in the category of prisms $(\X,\mathcal{M})_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}^\op$.

The ordinary assertion follows by a similar (far easier) argument.
<!-- end proof-78 -->
<!-- proposition-13: body_md -->
\label{prop:log_stack_presentation}
Let $(\X,\mathcal{M})=(\Spf\R,\mathcal{M})$ be a framed log affine over $\ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}_K$, and let
\[\rho_{\X,\mathrm{A}}: \Spf \mathrm{A} \longrightarrow (\X,\mathcal{M})^{{\mathbbl{\Delta}}}\]
be the fpqc epimorphism of Lemma \ref{lem:log_prism_stack_map} associated with the logarithmic Breuil-Kisin prism of its framing. Then the \v{C}ech nerve of $\Spf \mathrm{A}$ identifies with $\Spf \mathrm{A}^{(n)}$ where $\mathrm{A}^{(n)}$ are the iterated self-coproducts of $(\mathrm{A},\I,\M_{\Spf \mathrm{A}})^a$ in $(\X,\mathcal{M})_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}^\op$. In particular
\[(\X,\mathcal{M})^{\mathbbl{\Delta}} \simeq \left|\Spf\mathrm{A}^{(\bullet)}\right|\]
in formal stacks.
<!-- end proposition-13 -->
<!-- proof-79: body_md -->
Lemma \ref{lem:mixed_BK_fiber_product}, applied with $\B=\mathrm{A}$, identifies the first term of the \v{C}ech nerve of $\Spf \mathrm{A}$ over $(\X,\mathcal{M})^{{\mathbbl{\Delta}}}$ with $\Spf(\mathrm{A}\coprod_*\mathrm{A})$. The higher terms are the formal spectra of the iterated coproducts $(\mathrm{A}^{(1)})^{\widehat{\otimes}_{\mathrm{A}} n}$, for both the site-theoretic \v{C}ech nerve and the \v{C}ech nerve of $\rho_{\X,\mathrm{A}}: \Spf \mathrm{A} \to (\X,\mathcal{M})^{{\mathbbl{\Delta}}}$. Using Lemma \ref{lem:log_prism_stack_map}, this is an fpqc epimorphism so the claim follows.
<!-- end proof-79 -->
<!-- proposition-14: body_md -->
\label{prop:stacky_qcoh}
Let $(\X,\mathcal{M})$ satisfy Assumption \ref{ass:snc_log_structure} over $\ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}_K$. There is a natural symmetric monoidal equivalence
\[\iota_{(\X,\mathcal{M})}: \@undefined((\X,\mathcal{M})_{\mathbbl{\Delta}},\ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}) \xrightarrow{\sim} \@undefined_{\mathrm{qc}}((\X,\mathcal{M})^{\mathbbl{\Delta}}).\]
<!-- end proposition-14 -->
<!-- proof-80: body_md -->
We first note that the assertion can be checked strict \'{e}tale locally. On a framed log affine, using the logarithmic Breuil-Kisin prism $(\mathrm{A},\I,\M_{\Spf \mathrm{A}})^a$ associated with its framing yields
\[\lim_{[n]\in\Delta} \@undefined_{(p,\I^{(n)})}(\mathrm{A}^{(n)}) \simeq \@undefined((\X,\mathcal{M})_{\mathbbl{\Delta}},\ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}_{\mathbbl{\Delta}})\]
where $\mathrm{A}^{(n)}$ is the logarithmic \v{C}ech nerve. The (analogous) proof of Corollary \ref{cor:laur_strict_etale} for ordinary crystals gives strict \'{e}tale descent of the crystal side, which is well-known.

The same descent claim holds for the stack $(\X,\mathcal{M})^{{\mathbbl{\Delta}}}$ by \'{e}tale descent for $\X^{{\mathbbl{\Delta}}}$ in $\X$ from \cite{APC2}. We may therefore assume $(\X,\mathcal{M})=(\Spf\R,\mathcal{M})$ is a framed log affine. The logarithmic Breuil-Kisin prism $\mathrm{A}$ associated with its framing covers the log prismatic stack by Lemma \ref{lem:log_prism_stack_map}.

Now we can use Proposition \ref{prop:log_stack_presentation} to identify
\[\@undefined_{\mathrm{qc}}((\X,\mathcal{M})^{{\mathbbl{\Delta}}}) \simeq \lim_{[n]\in\Delta}\@undefined_{\mathrm{qc}}(\Spf \mathrm{A}^{(n)}) \simeq \@undefined((\X,\mathcal{M})_{\mathbbl{\Delta}},\ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}).\]
Indeed, $\rho_{\X,\mathrm{A}}: \Spf \mathrm{A} \to (\X,\mathcal{M})^{{\mathbbl{\Delta}}}$ is an fpqc epimorphism and we have identified its \v{C}ech nerve with $\Spf \mathrm{A}^{(n)}$, and thus $\@undefined_{\mathrm{qc}}$ satisfies descent for such maps. See the discussion after \cite[Definition 2.4]{syncrisloc} for more details.
<!-- end proof-80 -->
<!-- proposition-15: body_md -->
\label{prop:stacky_qcoh_pushforward}
Let $f:(\X,\mathcal{M})\to(\Y,\mathcal{N})$ be a strict morphism between pairs satisfying Assumption \ref{ass:snc_log_structure} over $\ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}_K$. For every $\mathcal{E} \in \@undefined((\X,\mathcal{M})_{\mathbbl{\Delta}},\ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}_{\mathbbl{\Delta}})$, there is a natural equivalence
\[\iota_{(\Y,\mathcal{N})} \R f_{{\mathbbl{\Delta}},*}\mathcal{E} \simeq \R f_*\iota_{(\X,\mathcal{M})}\mathcal{E}.\]
<!-- end proposition-15 -->
<!-- proof-81: body_md -->
Compatibility of Proposition \ref{prop:stacky_qcoh} with strict pullback gives a commutative diagram
\begin{display}
\@undefined((\Y,\mathcal{N})_{\mathbbl{\Delta}},\ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}) \ar{r}{\iota_{(\Y,\mathcal{N})}} \ar{d}{f^*} & \@undefined_{\mathrm{qc}}((\Y,\mathcal{N})^{\mathbbl{\Delta}}) \ar{d}{(f^{\mathbbl{\Delta}})^*} \\
\@undefined((\X,\mathcal{M})_{\mathbbl{\Delta}},\ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}) \ar{r}{\iota_{(\X,\mathcal{M})}} & \@undefined_{\mathrm{qc}}((\X,\mathcal{M})^{\mathbbl{\Delta}}).
\end{display}
Both vertical pullback functors preserve colimits, thus taking right adjoints of this square gives the asserted equivalence.
<!-- end proof-81 -->
<!-- remark-18: body_md -->
Laurent $\mathrm{F}$-crystals in \cite{KoshikawaYao2025,KoshikawaYaoCorrigendum} use the saturated log prismatic site. By \cite[Lemma 5.9]{Inoue}, the strict subsite is cofinal in the full log prismatic site. If $(\X,\mathcal{M})$ is fine and saturated, a strict object has the same characteristic monoid as the pullback of $\overline{\mathcal{M}}$, and is therefore saturated. The strictification in \cite[Lemma 5.9]{Inoue} has this same characteristic monoid, so the strict subsite is also cofinal in the saturated log prismatic site. Thus the limits defining the crystal categories on the full, saturated, and strict sites agree.

We suppress this distinction for $\@undefined((\X,\mathcal{M})_{\mathbbl{\Delta}},\ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}_{\mathbbl{\Delta}})$ and its perfect and Laurent variants for this reason.
\label{rem:crystal_indep}
<!-- end remark-18 -->
<!-- definition-15: body_md -->
\label{def:anspf}
Let $(\mathrm{A},(d))$ be an orientable prism. Then we write
\[\AnSpf(\mathrm{A}[1/d]_p^{\wedge}):=\colim_n \Spa((\mathrm{A}\mathord{/\mkern-6mu/} p^n)[1/d],\mathrm{A}\mathord{/\mkern-6mu/} p^n)\], where we use $\Spa$ to denote the analytic stack attached to a Huber pair as in \cite[Example 2.1.5]{Kipp2}.
<!-- end definition-15 -->
<!-- definition-16: body_md -->
\label{def:laur_category}
Let $(\mathrm{A},(d))$ be an orientable prism. Associated to the derived $(p,d)$-complete ring $\mathrm{A}$ is the analytic adic ring $(\mathrm{A},\mathrm{A})$ in the sense of \cite{AnschutzMannDescent}. We define
\[\@undefined_{\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\blacksquare$}}}}(\mathrm{A}[1/d]_p^{\wedge}) := \varprojlim_n \Mod_{(\mathrm{A}\mathord{/\mkern-6mu/} p^n)[1/d]} \@undefined_{\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\blacksquare$}}}}((\mathrm{A},\mathrm{A})),\]
where $(\mathrm{A}\mathord{/\mkern-6mu/} p^n)[1/d]$ is regarded as an algebra object of $\@undefined_{\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\blacksquare$}}}}((\mathrm{A},\mathrm{A}))$. Equivalently, this is $\@undefined_{\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\blacksquare$}}}}$ of $\AnSpf(\mathrm{A}[1/d]_p^{\wedge})$.

Then
\[\@undefined_{\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\blacksquare$}}}}((\X,\mathcal{M})_{\mathbbl{\Delta}},\ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}[1/\I_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}]_p^{\wedge}) := \lim_{(\mathrm{A},(d),\M_{\Spf \mathrm{A}})^a \in (\X,\mathcal{M})_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}^{\mathrm{op}}} \@undefined_{\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\blacksquare$}}}}(\mathrm{A}[1/d]_p^{\wedge}).\]
<!-- end definition-16 -->
<!-- lemma-49: body_md -->
Let $\mathrm{A}\to\B$ be a faithfully flat map of connective animated rings. If $\pi_0\B$ is countably presented as a $\pi_0\mathrm{A}$-module, then $\mathrm{A}\to\B$ is descendable of index at most $2$.
\label{lem:countable_flat_descendable}
<!-- end lemma-49 -->
<!-- proof-82: body_md -->
See \cite[Corollary 3.33 and the proof of Proposition 3.32]{MathewGaloisStableHomotopy}.
<!-- end proof-82 -->
<!-- lemma-50: body_md -->
\label{lem:prismatic_product_adic_descendable}
Let $(\X,\mathcal{M})$ be a framed log affine over $\ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}_K$, let $(\mathrm{A},\I,\M_{\Spf\mathrm{A}})^a$ be the logarithmic Breuil-Kisin prism associated with its framing, and let $(\B,(d),\mathcal{N})^a\in (\X,\mathcal{M})_{{\mathbbl{\Delta}}}^\op$. Put
\[\mathrm{C}=\mathrm{A}\coprod_*\B\]
for the coproduct in $(\X,\mathcal{M})_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}^\op$. Then
\[\B\longrightarrow\mathrm{C}\]
is completely descendable for the $(p,d)$-adic topologies in the sense of \cite[Definition 2.4.1.7]{Kipp}, and the induced algebra is descendable in $\@undefined_{\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\blacksquare$}}}}((\B,\B))$.

Moreover, $\Spa(\mathrm{C},\mathrm{C})\to\Spa(\B,\B)$ is a proper descendable cover.
<!-- end lemma-50 -->
<!-- proof-83: body_md -->
We prove the logarithmic assertion; the ordinary case is identical.

By the construction in Lemma \ref{lem:prism_coproduct}, Zariski locally we have
\begin{equation}
\mathrm{C} \simeq \left(\@undefined^{\mathrm{ex}}\{x_1/d,\ldots,x_m/d\}_\delta\right)^{\wedge}_{(p,d)},
\label{eq:prismatic_product_envelope}
\end{equation}
where $\ker(\@undefined^{\mathrm{ex}} \to \overline{\B})=(d,x_1,\ldots,x_m)$. Using \cite[Proposition 5.52, and Remark 5.54]{MaoDerivedCrystalline} we see that $\B \to \mathrm{C}$ is $(p,d)$-completely faithfully flat. Its derived reductions modulo $(p^k,d^k)$ are faithfully flat and countably presented on $\pi_0$ as modules, since we adjoin finitely many variables as a $\delta$ ring. By Lemma \ref{lem:countable_flat_descendable}, these reductions are then descendable of index $\le 2$.

However for our application, we need complete descendability, as in \cite[Definition 2.4.1.7]{Kipp}. Using rigidity of prisms, we see $\B\to\mathrm{C}$ is adic. Put $\mathrm{J}=\fib(\B\to\mathrm{C})$ in the derived $(p,d)$-complete category and write $\mathrm{J}_k=\mathrm{J}\mathord{/\mkern-6mu/}(p^k,d^k)$. Derived completeness then gives
\[\RHom_{\B}(\mathrm{J}\widehat\otimes_{\B}\mathrm{J},\B)\simeq\R\lim_k \RHom_{\B\mathord{/\mkern-6mu/}(p^k,d^k)}(\mathrm{J}_k^{\otimes2},\B\mathord{/\mkern-6mu/}(p^k,d^k)).\]
As we have seen already, the canonical map $\mathrm{J}\widehat\otimes_{\B}\mathrm{J}\to\B$ is nullhomotopic modulo $(p^k,d^k)$. One may then still apply the argument of \cite[Lemma 11.22]{BhattScholzeWittGrassmannian} (despite that it applies to $\N$-indexed colimits) to show that $(\mathrm{J}\widehat\otimes_{\B}\mathrm{J})^{\otimes 2} \to \B$ is nullhomotopic and therefore that $\mathrm{C}$ is descendable of index $\le 4$ in the derived $(p,d)$-complete category as desired.

Under $\@undefined(\Spf\B)\simeq\@undefined_{(p,d)\text{-comp}}(\B)$, the analytification functor used in the proof of \cite[Theorem 2.3.3(A)]{Kipp2} preserves descendable algebras. Hence the algebra induced by $\mathrm{C}$ in $\@undefined_{\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\blacksquare$}}}}((\B,\B))$ is descendable as desired.

It remains to prove properness. Example 2.1.13 of \cite{Kipp2} says that a map $\Spa(\mathrm{C},\mathrm{C})\to\Spa(\B,\B)$ is proper if and only if $\mathrm{C}$ is integral over the subring generated by $\B$ and topologically nilpotent elements of $\mathrm{C}$. In the present situation, it is therefore enough to prove that
\[\pi_0(\B\mathord{/\mkern-6mu/}(p,d)) \longrightarrow \pi_0(\mathrm{C}\mathord{/\mkern-6mu/}(p,d))\]
is integral. Indeed, if a monic polynomial $f$ over $\pi_0\B$ annihilates $c$ modulo $(p,d)$, then $f(t)-f(c)$ is a monic polynomial over $\pi_0\B+(p,d)\pi_0\mathrm{C}$ annihilating $c$.

Applying Lemma \ref{lem:prismatic_envelope_integral} to (\ref{eq:prismatic_product_envelope}), using $\@undefined^{\mathrm{ex}}/(d,x_1,\ldots,x_m)\simeq\B/d$, gives the needed integrality and hence properness (as for maps of Huber pairs regarded as analytic rings, the property of being affine proper is detected when the map on $+$ rings is integral up to topologically nilpotent elements). The same argument applies to the ordinary case.
<!-- end proof-83 -->
<!-- lemma-51: body_md -->
\label{lem:prismatic_envelope_integral}
Let $\mathrm{A}$ be an animated $\delta$-ring, let $d\in\pi_0\mathrm{A}$ be distinguished, and let $\{f_i\}$ be any (arbitrarily large) family of elements of $\pi_0\mathrm{A}$. Suppose $\mathrm{A}$ is further derived $(p,d)$ complete. Then the morphism
\[\Spf \left(\mathrm{A}\{f_i/d\}_\delta\right)^{\wedge}_{(p,d)} \longrightarrow \Spf \mathrm{A}\]
induced by the structure map is integral in the sense of \cite[2.2.5]{Kipp2}. In other words, on rings it is true in the ordinary sense modulo $(p,d)$.
<!-- end lemma-51 -->
<!-- proof-84: body_md -->
As we discuss integrality on formal schemes, we must show 
\[\pi_0(\mathrm{A}\mathord{/\mkern-6mu/}(p,d)) \longrightarrow \pi_0\left(\left(\mathrm{A}\{f_i/d\}_\delta\right)^{\wedge}_{(p,d)}\mathord{/\mkern-6mu/}(p,d)\right)\]
is integral. It suffices to check all of the iterates $\delta^n(f_i/d)$ satisfy monic polynomials in $\pi_0(\mathrm{A}\mathord{/\mkern-6mu/}(p,d))[\T]$ modulo $(p,d)$. We will show that $\delta^n(f_i/d)$ satisfies a monic polynomial in $\pi_0(\mathrm{A}\mathord{/\mkern-6mu/}(p,d))[(f_i/d), \delta(f_i/d), \ldots, \delta^{n-1}(f_i/d)]$. 

The key identity for us will be 
\[0 = \delta^n(d (f_i/d) - f_i) = \varphi^n(d) \delta^n(f_i/d) + \mathrm{F}_n((f_i/d), \delta(f_i/d), \ldots, \delta^{n-1}(f_i/d))\]
where $\mathrm{F}_n$ is a polynomial with coefficients in $\mathrm{A}$. Moreover, for $n\geq1$, modulo $(p,d)$, $\mathrm{F}_n$ has degree $p$ in $\delta^{n-1}(f_i/d)$, with leading coefficient $\delta(\varphi^{n-1}(d))$. We will drop the argument of $\mathrm{F}_n$ from here on.

The identity holds for $n=0$ with $\mathrm{F}_0=-f_i$. Applying $\delta$ to the relation, one sees that $\delta^{n+1}(d (f_i/d) - f_i)$ equals
\[\delta(\varphi^n(d) \delta^n(f_i/d)) + \delta(\mathrm{F}_n) - \sum_{j=1}^{p-1} \frac{1}{p}\binom{p}{j}(\varphi^n(d) \delta^n(f_i/d))^j \mathrm{F}_n^{p-j}.\]
One computes $\delta(\varphi^n(d) \delta^n(f_i/d)) = \varphi^{n+1}(d) \delta^{n+1}(f_i/d) + \delta(\varphi^n(d))(\delta^n(f_i/d))^p$ as well. Collecting the remaining terms to form $\mathrm{F}_{n+1}$ gives the first part of the claim. For the second part, if we work modulo $(p,d)$, the previous display becomes $\delta(\varphi^n(d) \delta^n(f_i/d)) + \delta(\mathrm{F}_n)$, as the factor we subtract has all terms divisible by $\varphi^n(d)\in (p,d)$. Since $\mathrm{F}_n$ involves only the preceding iterates, $\delta(\mathrm{F}_n)$ has degree at most one in $\delta^n(f_i/d)$ modulo $p$. Thus the degree $p$ term of $\mathrm{F}_{n+1}$ has the asserted coefficient.

To finally deduce the desired claim for $\delta^n(f_i/d)$, one then reduces this relation for the index $n+1$ modulo $(p,d)$: this kills the term $\varphi^{n+1}(d) \delta^{n+1}(f_i/d)$, leaving only the remaining terms $\mathrm{F}_{n+1}((f_i/d), \delta(f_i/d), \ldots, \delta^{n}(f_i/d))$. We know the leading coefficient in $\delta^{n}(f_i/d)$ for $\mathrm{F}_{n+1}$ modulo $(p,d)$ was $\delta(\varphi^{n}(d))$ attached to $(\delta^{n}(f_i/d))^p$, but $\varphi$ and $\delta$ commute so this is a unit (since $d$ is distinguished; i.e. $\delta(d)$ is a unit). Thus after we divide by this unit, we obtain a monic polynomial in $\pi_0(\mathrm{A}\mathord{/\mkern-6mu/}(p,d))[(f_i/d), \delta(f_i/d), \ldots, \delta^{n-1}(f_i/d)]$ that $\delta^n(f_i/d)$ satisfies modulo $(p,d)$. The claim follows.
<!-- end proof-84 -->
<!-- theorem-12: body_md -->
\label{thm:laur_cech}
Let $(\X,\mathcal{M})$ be a framed log affine over $\ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}_K$, and let $(\mathrm{A},\I,\M_{\Spf\mathrm{A}})^a$ be the logarithmic Breuil-Kisin prism associated with its framing. If $(\mathrm{A}^{(m)},\I,\M^{(m)})^a$ is the degree $m$ term of its \v{C}ech nerve in the strict log prismatic site, then
\[\@undefined_{\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\blacksquare$}}}}((\X,\mathcal{M})_{\mathbbl{\Delta}},\ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}[1/\I_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}]_p^{\wedge}) \simeq \lim_{[m]\in\Delta}\@undefined_{\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\blacksquare$}}}}(\mathrm{A}^{(m)}[1/\I]^{\wedge}_p).\]
<!-- end theorem-12 -->
<!-- proof-85: body_md -->
By definition, 
\[\@undefined_{\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\blacksquare$}}}}((\X,\mathcal{M})_{\mathbbl{\Delta}},\ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}[1/\I_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}]_p^{\wedge}) \simeq \lim_{(\B,(d),\M_{\Spf \B})^a \in (\X,\mathcal{M})_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}^\op} \@undefined_{\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\blacksquare$}}}}(\B[1/d]_p^{\wedge})\]
where $\@undefined_{\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\blacksquare$}}}}(\B[1/d]_p^{\wedge})$ is interpreted as in Definition \ref{def:laur_category}. Now Lemma \ref{lem:prismatic_product_adic_descendable} tells us
\[\@undefined_{\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\blacksquare$}}}}(\B[1/d]^{\wedge}_p) \simeq \lim_{[m]\in\Delta}\@undefined_{\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\blacksquare$}}}}((\mathrm{A}^{(m)}\coprod_*\B)[1/d]^{\wedge}_p).\]
Now upon commuting limits, we get
\[\@undefined_{\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\blacksquare$}}}}((\X,\mathcal{M})_{\mathbbl{\Delta}},\ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}[1/\I_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}]_p^{\wedge}) \simeq \lim_{[m]\in \Delta} \left( \lim_{(\B,(d),\M_{\Spf \B})^a \in (\X,\mathcal{M})_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}^\op} \@undefined_{\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\blacksquare$}}}}((\mathrm{A}^{(m)}\coprod_*\B)[1/d]^{\wedge}_p) \right).\]
We are now done, as formally we have
\[\lim_{(\B,(d),\M_{\Spf \B})^a \in (\X,\mathcal{M})_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}^\op} \@undefined_{\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\blacksquare$}}}}((\mathrm{A}^{(m)}\coprod_*\B)[1/d]^{\wedge}_p) \simeq \@undefined_{\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\blacksquare$}}}}(\mathrm{A}^{(m)}[1/\I]_p^{\wedge}),\]
proving the claim. One way to see this last point is that the coproduct functor
\[(\X,\mathcal{M})_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}^\op \longrightarrow (\X,\mathcal{M})_{{\mathbbl{\Delta}},/\mathrm{A}^{(m)}}^\op\]
sending $(\B,(d),\M_{\Spf \B})^a \mapsto (\mathrm{A}^{(m)}\coprod_*\B)$ regarded as a log prism is left adjoint to the forgetful functor, so by adjunction the limit is
\[\lim_{\mathrm{A}^{(m)} \to \B} \@undefined_{\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\blacksquare$}}}}(\B[1/d]_p^{\wedge}) \simeq \@undefined_{\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\blacksquare$}}}}(\mathrm{A}^{(m)}[1/\I]_p^{\wedge}).\]
Thus $\@undefined_{\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\blacksquare$}}}}((\X,\mathcal{M})_{\mathbbl{\Delta}},\ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}[1/\I_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}]_p^{\wedge}) \simeq \lim_{[m]\in\Delta}\@undefined_{\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\blacksquare$}}}}(\mathrm{A}^{(m)}[1/\I]^{\wedge}_p)$.
<!-- end proof-85 -->
<!-- lemma-52: body_md -->
\label{lem:perf_comparison}
Let $(\mathrm{A},(d))$ be an orientable transversal prism, i.e. $\mathrm{A}/d$ is $p$-torsionfree. Then we have
\[\@undefined_{\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\blacksquare$}}}}(\mathrm{A}[1/d]^{\wedge}_p)^{\mathrm{dual}} \simeq \varprojlim_n\Perf((\mathrm{A}/p^n)[1/d]) \simeq \Perf(\mathrm{A}[1/d]^{\wedge}_p).\]
In the setting of Theorem \ref{thm:laur_cech}, these give
\[\Perf((\X,\mathcal{M})_{\mathbbl{\Delta}},\ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}[1/\I_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}]_p^{\wedge}) \simeq \varprojlim_{[m]\in\Delta} \Perf(\mathrm{A}^{(m)}[1/\I]^{\wedge}_p).\]
<!-- end lemma-52 -->
<!-- proof-86: body_md -->
This follows by taking dualizable objects in Theorem \ref{thm:laur_cech} and applying \cite[Theorem 14.10]{ScholzeAnalyticGeometry}, noting dualizables can be detected termwise in a limit diagram.
<!-- end proof-86 -->
<!-- lemma-53: body_md -->
\label{lem:qdr_laur_cech}
Let $(\Spf\R,\mathcal{M})$ be a framed log affine over $\Spf\W(k)[\zeta_p]$. Let $((\mathrm{A}^+)^{(m)},[p]_q,\mathcal{M}^{(m)})^a$ be the degree $m$ term of the log $q$-de Rham \v{C}ech nerve in $(\Spf\R,\mathcal{M})_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}$, and put $\mathrm{A}^{(m)}=(\mathrm{A}^+)^{(m)}[1/[p]_q]^{\wedge}_p$. Then
\[\@undefined_{\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\blacksquare$}}}}((\Spf\R,\mathcal{M})_{\mathbbl{\Delta}},\ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}[1/\I_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}]_p^{\wedge})\simeq \varprojlim_{[m]\in\Delta}\@undefined_{\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\blacksquare$}}}}(\mathrm{A}^{(m)}).\]
<!-- end lemma-53 -->
<!-- proof-87: body_md -->
In Lemma \ref{lem:standard_log_BK_prism}, the log $q$-de Rham prism is a valid choice of a logarithmic Breuil-Kisin atlas. Theorem \ref{thm:laur_cech} therefore gives the needed \v{C}ech description.
<!-- end proof-87 -->
<!-- corollary-9: body_md -->
\label{cor:laur_strict_etale}
On log formal schemes satisfying Assumption \ref{ass:snc_log_structure} over $\ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}_K$, the assignment
\[(\X,\mathcal{M}) \longmapsto \@undefined_{\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\blacksquare$}}}}((\X,\mathcal{M})_{\mathbbl{\Delta}},\ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}[1/\I_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}]_p^{\wedge})\]
is a stack for the strict \'{e}tale topology. The same holds for $\Perf((\X,\mathcal{M})_{\mathbbl{\Delta}},\ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}[1/\I_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}]_p^{\wedge})$.
<!-- end corollary-9 -->
<!-- proof-88: body_md -->
Framed log affines form a basis for the strict \'{e}tale topology on log formal schemes satisfying Assumption \ref{ass:snc_log_structure} over $\ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}_K$ by Lemma \ref{lem:strict_etale_local_framing}, so it is enough to consider an affine strict \'{e}tale cover $\U\to\X$ by framed log affines with $\X$ framed. We give every term $\U^{(n)}$ of its \v{C}ech nerve the framing induced from $\X$, and let $\mathrm{A}_\X$ be the logarithmic Breuil-Kisin prism associated with the framing of $\X$. The \'{e}tale lifting property identifies its pullback to each $\U^{(n)}$ with the logarithmic Breuil-Kisin prism $\mathrm{A}_{\U^{(n)}}$ associated with the induced framing. Writing $\mathrm{A}_{\X}^{(m)}$ and $\mathrm{A}_{\U^{(n)}}^{(m)}$ for the Laurent rings in degree $m$ of their \v{C}ech nerves, they form an (augmented) bicosimplicial diagram as follows:
\begin{display}
\@undefined_{\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\blacksquare$}}}}((\X,\mathcal{M})_{\mathbbl{\Delta}},\ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}[1/\I_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}]_p^{\wedge})
  \ar[r]
  \ar[d]
& \@undefined_{\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\blacksquare$}}}}(\mathrm{A}_{\X}^{(0)})
  \ar[r,shift left=.6ex]
  \ar[r,shift right=.6ex]
  \ar[d]
& \@undefined_{\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\blacksquare$}}}}(\mathrm{A}_{\X}^{(1)})
  \ar[r,shift left=1ex]
  \ar[r]
  \ar[r,shift right=1ex]
  \ar[d]
& \cdots \\
\@undefined_{\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\blacksquare$}}}}((\U,\mathcal{M}|_{\U})_{\mathbbl{\Delta}},\ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}[1/\I_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}]_p^{\wedge})
  \ar[r]
  \ar[d,shift left=.6ex]
  \ar[d,shift right=.6ex]
& \@undefined_{\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\blacksquare$}}}}(\mathrm{A}_{\U}^{(0)})
  \ar[r,shift left=.6ex]
  \ar[r,shift right=.6ex]
  \ar[d,shift left=.6ex]
  \ar[d,shift right=.6ex]
& \@undefined_{\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\blacksquare$}}}}(\mathrm{A}_{\U}^{(1)})
  \ar[r,shift left=1ex]
  \ar[r]
  \ar[r,shift right=1ex]
  \ar[d,shift left=.6ex]
  \ar[d,shift right=.6ex]
& \cdots \\
\@undefined_{\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\blacksquare$}}}}((\U^{(1)},\mathcal{M}|_{\U^{(1)}})_{\mathbbl{\Delta}},\ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}[1/\I_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}]_p^{\wedge})
  \ar[r]
  \ar[d,shift left=1ex]
  \ar[d]
  \ar[d,shift right=1ex]
& \@undefined_{\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\blacksquare$}}}}(\mathrm{A}_{\U^{(1)}}^{(0)})
  \ar[r,shift left=.6ex]
  \ar[r,shift right=.6ex]
  \ar[d,shift left=1ex]
  \ar[d]
  \ar[d,shift right=1ex]
& \@undefined_{\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\blacksquare$}}}}(\mathrm{A}_{\U^{(1)}}^{(1)})
  \ar[r,shift left=1ex]
  \ar[r]
  \ar[r,shift right=1ex]
  \ar[d,shift left=1ex]
  \ar[d]
  \ar[d,shift right=1ex]
& \cdots \\
\vdots & \vdots & \vdots & {}
\end{display}
For fixed $n$, Theorem \ref{thm:laur_cech} identifies the limit of the $n$th row with the solid Laurent crystal category of $\U^{(n)}$. For fixed $m$, compatibility with strict \'{e}tale localization also identifies the $m$th column with the \v{C}ech nerve of an \'{e}tale cover. For such maps $\@undefined_{\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\blacksquare$}}}}(\Spa(\mathrm{A},\mathrm{A}))$ satisfies descent by \cite[Theorem 2.3.3(A),(B)]{Kipp2}, which suffices for our situation: since limits commute with limits, we obtain
\[
\begin{aligned}
\varprojlim_{[n]\in\Delta}
\@undefined_{\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\blacksquare$}}}}((\U^{(n)},\mathcal{M}|_{\U^{(n)}})_{\mathbbl{\Delta}},\ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}[1/\I_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}]_p^{\wedge})
&\simeq
\varprojlim_{[n]\in\Delta}\varprojlim_{[m]\in\Delta}
\@undefined_{\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\blacksquare$}}}}(\mathrm{A}_{\U^{(n)}}^{(m)})\\
&\simeq
\varprojlim_{[m]\in\Delta}\varprojlim_{[n]\in\Delta}
\@undefined_{\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\blacksquare$}}}}(\mathrm{A}_{\U^{(n)}}^{(m)})\\
&\simeq
\varprojlim_{[m]\in\Delta}
\@undefined_{\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\blacksquare$}}}}(\mathrm{A}_{\X}^{(m)})\\
&\simeq
\@undefined_{\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\blacksquare$}}}}((\X,\mathcal{M})_{\mathbbl{\Delta}},\ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}[1/\I_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}]_p^{\wedge}).
\end{aligned}
\]
The claim follows for $\Perf((\X,\mathcal{M})_{\mathbbl{\Delta}},\ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}[1/\I_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}]_p^{\wedge})$ since dualizability can be tested termwise in a limit of symmetric monoidal categories.
<!-- end proof-88 -->
<!-- corollary-10: body_md -->
\label{cor:laur_t_struct}
Let $(\X,\mathcal{M})$ satisfy Assumption \ref{ass:snc_log_structure} over $\ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}_K$. The canonical $t$-structure on $\@undefined_{\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\blacksquare$}}}}((\X,\mathcal{M})_{\mathbbl{\Delta}},\ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}[1/\I_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}]_p^{\wedge})$ restricts to $\Perf((\X,\mathcal{M})_{\mathbbl{\Delta}},\ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}[1/\I_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}]_p^{\wedge})$.
<!-- end corollary-10 -->
<!-- proof-89: body_md -->
Using a covering by framed log affines via Lemma \ref{lem:strict_etale_local_framing}, we may use their associated logarithmic Breuil-Kisin prisms $(\mathrm{A},\I,\M_{\Spf \mathrm{A}})^a$ from Lemma \ref{lem:standard_log_BK_prism} to produce a covering family (by Theorem \ref{thm:laur_cech}). The argument ends up being slightly technical since there is a subtlety that it is not clear the maps in the Breuil-Kisin \v{C}ech nerve are $t$-exact for $\@undefined_{\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\blacksquare$}}}}(-)$.

First we simply check that there exists a $t$-structure on $\Perf((\X,\mathcal{M})_{\mathbbl{\Delta}},\ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}[1/\I_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}]_p^{\wedge})$ regarded as ordinary Laurent crystals, defined via orthogonality from the Breuil-Kisin presentation of $\Perf^{\le 0}((\X,\mathcal{M})_{\mathbbl{\Delta}},\ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}[1/\I_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}]_p^{\wedge})$: we ask for the connective objects to be those which are connective on each \v{C}ech term $\mathrm{A}^{(n)}[1/\I]_p^{\wedge}$. This follows by the abstract argument of \cite[Footnote 70]{Fgauge}, noting that we actually only need the maps $\mathrm{A}[1/\I]^{\wedge}_p \to \mathrm{A}^{(n)}[1/\I]^{\wedge}_p$ to be flat (which they are in the ordinary sense since $\mathrm{A}[1/\I]^{\wedge}_p$ is Noetherian, using that $p$-complete flatness upgrades to ordinary flatness with a Noetherian source). By Lemma \ref{lem:perf_comparison} this also yields a $t$-structure on the dualizable objects in $\@undefined_{\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\blacksquare$}}}}((\X,\mathcal{M})_{\mathbbl{\Delta}},\ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}[1/\I_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}]_p^{\wedge})$ as dualizability is detected termwise in a limit.

One may check that any $\mathcal{E}$ in $\Perf^{\le 0}((\X,\mathcal{M})_{\mathbbl{\Delta}},\ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}[1/\I_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}]_p^{\wedge})$ is also in $\@undefined^{\le 0}_{\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\blacksquare$}}}}((\X,\mathcal{M})_{\mathbbl{\Delta}},\ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}[1/\I_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}]_p^{\wedge})$. We must check all evaluations on log prisms are connective, as we define the canonical $t$-structure on $\@undefined^{\le 0}_{\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\blacksquare$}}}}((\X,\mathcal{M})_{\mathbbl{\Delta}},\ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}[1/\I_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}]_p^{\wedge})$ this way by orthogonality. By construction of $\Perf^{\le 0}((\X,\mathcal{M})_{\mathbbl{\Delta}},\ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}[1/\I_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}]_p^{\wedge})$ we see the evaluation on $(\mathrm{A} \coprod_* \B)[1/\I]^{\wedge}$ is connective (as it is obtained by pullback from the value on $(\mathrm{A},\I,\M_{\Spf \mathrm{A}})^a$, which by definition is connective). In Lemma \ref{lem:prismatic_product_adic_descendable} we argued $(\mathrm{A} \coprod_* \B)[1/\I]^{\wedge}$ is a descendable algebra in $\@undefined_{\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\blacksquare$}}}}(\B[1/\mathrm{J}]_p^{\wedge})$. In particular, the base change functor $\B[1/\mathrm{J}]_p^{\wedge} \to (\mathrm{A} \coprod_* \B)[1/\I]^{\wedge}$ is conservative: in this situation base change detects connectivity on perfect complexes.

One may also check that $\mathcal{E}\in \Perf^{\ge 0}((\X,\mathcal{M})_{\mathbbl{\Delta}},\ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}[1/\I_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}]_p^{\wedge})$ is also in $\@undefined^{\ge 0}_{\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\blacksquare$}}}}((\X,\mathcal{M})_{\mathbbl{\Delta}},\ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}[1/\I_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}]_p^{\wedge})$ for its canonical $t$-structure. Indeed this is defined as the right orthogonal of 
\[\@undefined^{\le -1}_{\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\blacksquare$}}}}((\X,\mathcal{M})_{\mathbbl{\Delta}},\ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}[1/\I_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}]_p^{\wedge}).\]
For $\mathcal{E}' \in \@undefined^{\le -1}_{\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\blacksquare$}}}}((\X,\mathcal{M})_{\mathbbl{\Delta}},\ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}[1/\I_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}]_p^{\wedge})$, every evaluation on \v{C}ech terms $\mathrm{A}^{(n)}[1/\I]_p^{\wedge}$ lies in the $\le -1$ part of the solid $t$-structure. Writing $\mathcal{E}_n$ and $\mathcal{E}'_n$ for these evaluations, we get
\[\Map_{\@undefined_{\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\blacksquare$}}}}(\mathrm{A}^{(n)}[1/\I]_p^{\wedge})}(\mathcal{E}'_n, \mathcal{E}_n) = 0\]
using that $\mathcal{E}_n$ are in the $\ge 0$ part (using that it is perfect here to relate ordinary and solid $t$-structures). But mapping spaces are computed by the limit over the \v{C}ech nerve, so the claim of the corollary follows.
<!-- end proof-89 -->
<!-- proposition-16: body_md -->
\label{prop:ordinary_BK_analytic_presentation}
Let $\X$ be an affine smooth $p$-adic formal scheme over $\ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}_K$, and let $(\mathrm{A},\I)$ be an ordinary Breuil-Kisin atlas obtained from a smooth lift over $\W(k)\llbracket u\rrbracket$. The induced map
\[\Spa(\mathrm{A},\mathrm{A})\longrightarrow\X^{{\mathbbl{\Delta}},\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\blacksquare$}}}}\]
is a representable proper effective epimorphism. If $\mathrm{A}^{(n)}$ denotes the $n$th iterated self-coproduct in the category of prisms over $\X$, then
\[\X^{{\mathbbl{\Delta}},\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\blacksquare$}}}}\simeq\left|\Spa(\mathrm{A}^{(\bullet)},\mathrm{A}^{(\bullet)})\right|\]
in analytic stacks.
<!-- end proposition-16 -->
<!-- proof-90: body_md -->
Choose a classical regular semiperfectoid cover of $\X$ in the infinite-root/\'{e}tale topology. Construction 3.7.1 and Corollary 3.6.3 of \cite{Kipp2} show that
\[\coprod_i\Spa(\B_i,\B_i)\longrightarrow\X^{{\mathbbl{\Delta}},\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\blacksquare$}}}}\]
is an effective epimorphism. It therefore suffices to test the first assertion after pullback to each $\Spa(\B_i,\B_i)$. Lemma \ref{lem:mixed_BK_fiber_product} and finite limit preservation of $(-)^{\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\blacksquare$}}}}$ (Definition \ref{def:box_analytic_realization}) identify this pullback with
\[\Spa(\mathrm{A}\coprod_*\B_i,\mathrm{A}\coprod_*\B_i)\longrightarrow\Spa(\B_i,\B_i),\]
which is a proper descendable cover by Lemma \ref{lem:prismatic_product_adic_descendable}. Representability is local on the target, as is properness by \cite[Remark 2.3.1]{Kipp2}, so this proves the first assertion.

Upon using the non-logarithmic case \ref{lem:mixed_BK_fiber_product} and finite limit preservation of $(-)^{\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\blacksquare$}}}}$ (as in Definition \ref{def:box_analytic_realization}) we may identify the $n$th \v{C}ech term with $\Spa(\mathrm{A}^{(n)},\mathrm{A}^{(n)})$. Since the map from $\Spa(\mathrm{A},\mathrm{A})$ is an effective epimorphism, we deduce $\X^{{\mathbbl{\Delta}},\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\blacksquare$}}}}\simeq\left|\Spa(\mathrm{A}^{(\bullet)},\mathrm{A}^{(\bullet)})\right|$.
<!-- end proof-90 -->
<!-- lemma-54: body_md -->
\label{lem:chart_log_prism}
Let $(\X,\mathcal{M})$ be a framed log affine over $\ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}_K$, let $(\mathrm{A},\I,\M_{\Spf\mathrm{A}})^a$ be the logarithmic Breuil-Kisin prism associated with its framing, and let $\mathrm{P}=\N^r$ be its framing's chart. There is an orientable bounded fine log prism $(\B_\mathrm{P},\I,\mathcal{N}_\mathrm{P})^a$ with a strict map
\[(\Spf(\B_\mathrm{P}/\I),\mathcal{N}_\mathrm{P}|_{\Spf(\B_\mathrm{P}/\I)})\longrightarrow(\X,\mathcal{M})\]
yielding an effective epimorphism $\Spa(\B_\mathrm{P},\B_\mathrm{P}) \longrightarrow (\X,\mathcal{M})^{{\mathbbl{\Delta}},\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\blacksquare$}}}}$. In formal stacks the map
\[\Spf \B_{\mathrm{P}} \longrightarrow  (\X,\mathcal{M})^{{\mathbbl{\Delta}}}\]
is also an effective epimorphism.
<!-- end lemma-54 -->
<!-- proof-91: body_md -->
Since $\mathrm{P}=\N^r$ anyway, we will just write $\N^r$ directly in the proof. We will first construct the effective epimorphism 
\[\Spf \B_{\N^r} \longrightarrow  (\X,\mathcal{M})^{{\mathbbl{\Delta}}}\]
of fpqc stacks, and argue that after applying the functor $(-)^{\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\blacksquare$}}}}$ from Definition \ref{def:box_analytic_realization} we obtain an effective epimorphism of analytic stacks.

Since we work with a framed log affine, when constructing $(\X,\mathcal{M})^{{\mathbbl{\Delta}}}$ we can realize it as the relative stack $(\X/\mathcal{A}_{\N^r})^{{\mathbbl{\Delta}}}$. Writing the stack this way reveals that there is an fpqc epimorphism
\[\Spf\mathrm{A} \times_{\mathcal{A}_{\N^r}^{\mathbbl{\Delta}}}(\Z_p^{\mathbbl{\Delta}}\times\Spf\Z_p\langle \N^r\rangle) \longrightarrow (\X,\mathcal{M})^{{\mathbbl{\Delta}}}.\]
Indeed, termwise $\Spf \mathrm{A} \to \X^{{\mathbbl{\Delta}}}$ is an fpqc epimorphism, as is $\Z_p^{\mathbbl{\Delta}}\times\Spf\Z_p\langle \mathrm{P}\rangle \to \Z_p^{\mathbbl{\Delta}} \times \mathcal{A}_{\N^r}$. Thus we must construct an fpqc epimorphism 
\[\Spf \B_{\mathrm{P}} \to \Spf\mathrm{A} \times_{\mathcal{A}_{\N^r}^{\mathbbl{\Delta}}}(\Z_p^{\mathbbl{\Delta}}\times\Spf\Z_p\langle \N^r\rangle).\]
This follows from rewriting the target stack in a different way. The main issue is that $\mathcal{A}_{\N^r}$ is a stack -- if it was a smooth $p$-adic formal scheme, we could try to relate the target to $\Spf$ of some coproduct of prisms, which would give the desired claim.

What fixes this is that $\mathcal{A}_{\N^r}$ has affine diagonal. Let us rewrite the target using the Cartesian square

\begin{display}
\Spf\mathrm{A} \times_{\mathcal{A}_{\N^r}^{\mathbbl{\Delta}}}(\Z_p^{\mathbbl{\Delta}}\times\Spf\Z_p\langle \N^r\rangle) \ar{d} \ar{r} & \X^{{\mathbbl{\Delta}}} \times_{\X^{{\mathbbl{\Delta}}}} \Spf \mathrm{A} \ar{d} \\
\Z_p\langle \N^r \rangle^{{\mathbbl{\Delta}}} \times_{\Z_p\langle \N^r \rangle^{{\mathbbl{\Delta}}}} \Z_p^{\mathbbl{\Delta}}\times\Spf\Z_p\langle \N^r\rangle \ar{r} & \mathcal{A}_{\N^r}^{{\mathbbl{\Delta}}} \times_{\Z_p^{\mathbbl{\Delta}}} \Z_p^{{\mathbbl{\Delta}}}.
\end{display}
The idea is to trivially rewrite each term, so that upon commuting limits with limits we get
\[(\X \times \mathbf{G}_m^r)^{{\mathbbl{\Delta}}} \times_{(\X \times \Spf \Z_p\langle \N^r \rangle)^{{\mathbbl{\Delta}}}} \Spf(\mathrm{A} \widehat{\otimes} \Z_p\langle \N^r \rangle).\]
The key thing we have used here is that $(-)^{{\mathbbl{\Delta}}}$ is compatible with fiber products, and $\Spf \Z_p\langle \N^r \rangle \times_{\mathcal{A}_{\N^r}} \X$ becomes affine. For the proof, in the upper right corner we could have equally well chosen $\Z_p\langle \N^r \rangle$ again, and the entire argument still works. We only make this choice to reuse the Breuil-Kisin prism $\mathrm{A}$ in a moment.

This new presentation is substantially more useful, because there is a Breuil-Kisin prism $\mathrm{A}\langle u_1^{\pm1},\ldots,u_r^{\pm1}\rangle_{(p,\I)}$ with $\delta(u_i)=0$ giving an fpqc epimorphism
\[\Spf \mathrm{A}\langle u_1^{\pm1},\ldots,u_r^{\pm1}\rangle_{(p,\I)} \longrightarrow (\X \times \mathbf{G}_m^r)^{{\mathbbl{\Delta}}}.\]
Upon base change, we obtain an fpqc epimorphism
\[\Spf \mathrm{A}\langle u_1^{\pm1},\ldots,u_r^{\pm1}\rangle_{(p,\I)} \times_{(\X \times \Spf \Z_p\langle \N^r \rangle)^{{\mathbbl{\Delta}}}} \Spf \mathrm{A} (\widehat{\otimes} \Z_p\langle \N^r \rangle) \longrightarrow \Spf\mathrm{A}\times_{\mathcal{A}_{\N^r}^{\mathbbl{\Delta}}}(\Z_p^{\mathbbl{\Delta}}\times\Spf\Z_p\langle \N^r\rangle).\]
The source is now a fiber product of two prisms with their natural maps to $(\X \times \Spf \Z_p\langle \N^r \rangle)^{{\mathbbl{\Delta}}}$, exactly the (non-logarithmic) situation understood in Lemma \ref{lem:mixed_BK_fiber_product}. Letting the coproduct of these prisms be $\B_{\N^r}$ we obtain a composite fpqc epimorphism
\[\Spf \B_{\N^r} \longrightarrow \Spf\mathrm{A}\times_{\mathcal{A}_{\N^r}^{\mathbbl{\Delta}}}(\Z_p^{\mathbbl{\Delta}}\times\Spf\Z_p\langle \N^r\rangle) \longrightarrow (\X,\mathcal{M})^{{\mathbbl{\Delta}}}.\]
This gives the second claim. Note that $\B_{\N^r}$ is also a log prism as it naturally comes with a projection to $\Z_p^{\mathbbl{\Delta}} \times \mathcal{A}_{\mathrm{P}}$ compatible with the map to $\mathcal{A}_{\mathrm{P}}^{\mathbbl{\Delta}}$ using this map.

For the variant on analytic stacks, we apply $(-)^{\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\blacksquare$}}}}$ to both maps. The important property is that it is compatible with finite limits, so in all of the fiber products above we may simply apply it individually to each formal stack. For the first arrow, it is a proper effective epimorphism of analytic stacks by Proposition \ref{prop:ordinary_BK_analytic_presentation}.

For the second arrow, on the first factor we again apply Proposition \ref{prop:ordinary_BK_analytic_presentation}, and for the second factor we only use that
\[\Spf \Z_p\langle \N^r\rangle \longrightarrow \mathcal{A}_{\N^r}\]
is sent to an effective epimorphism of analytic stacks by $(-)^{\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\blacksquare$}}}}$ which is clear.
<!-- end proof-91 -->
<!-- proposition-17: body_md -->
\label{prop:log_BK_analytic_presentation}
Let $(\X,\mathcal{M})$ be a framed log affine over $\ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}_K$, and let $(\mathrm{A},\I,\M_{\Spf\mathrm{A}})^a$ be the logarithmic Breuil-Kisin prism associated with its framing. The induced map
\[\Spa(\mathrm{A},\mathrm{A})\longrightarrow(\X,\mathcal{M})^{{\mathbbl{\Delta}},\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\blacksquare$}}}}\]
is a representable proper effective epimorphism. If $\mathrm{A}^{(n)}$ denotes the $n$th iterated self-coproduct in $(\X,\mathcal{M})_{\mathbbl{\Delta}}^{\mathrm{op}}$, then
\[(\X,\mathcal{M})^{{\mathbbl{\Delta}},\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\blacksquare$}}}}\simeq\left|\Spa(\mathrm{A}^{(\bullet)},\mathrm{A}^{(\bullet)})\right|\]
in analytic stacks.
<!-- end proposition-17 -->
<!-- proof-92: body_md -->
The proof is similar to Proposition \ref{prop:ordinary_BK_analytic_presentation}. Let $\mathrm{P}=\N^r$ be the framing's chart. Using Lemma \ref{lem:chart_log_prism} we get an effective epimorphism
\[\Spa(\B_\mathrm{P},\B_\mathrm{P})\longrightarrow (\X,\mathcal{M})^{{\mathbbl{\Delta}},\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\blacksquare$}}}}\]
induced by the map $\rho_{\X,\B_{\mathrm{P}}}$ induced by the log prism structure on $\B_{\mathrm{P}}$.

Lemma \ref{lem:mixed_BK_fiber_product} identifies the pullback of $\Spa(\mathrm{A},\mathrm{A})$ along this map with
\[\Spa(\mathrm{A}\coprod_*\B_\mathrm{P},\mathrm{A}\coprod_*\B_\mathrm{P})\longrightarrow\Spa(\B_\mathrm{P},\B_\mathrm{P}).\]
This is a proper descendable cover by Lemma \ref{lem:prismatic_product_adic_descendable}. Representability is local on the target, as is properness by \cite[Remark 2.3.1]{Kipp2}, so this proves the first assertion. 

Finally, lemma \ref{lem:mixed_BK_fiber_product} and finite limit preservation of $(-)^{\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\blacksquare$}}}}$ (as in Definition \ref{def:box_analytic_realization}) identify the $n$th \v{C}ech term with $\Spa(\mathrm{A}^{(n)},\mathrm{A}^{(n)})$. Since the map from $\Spa(\mathrm{A},\mathrm{A})$ is an effective epimorphism, we deduce $(\X,\mathcal{M})^{{\mathbbl{\Delta}},\mathord{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.75}{$\displaystyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\textstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptstyle\blacksquare$}}{\scalebox{0.75}{$\scriptscriptstyle\blacksquare$}}}}\simeq\left|\Spa(\mathrm{A}^{(\bullet)},\mathrm{A}^{(\bullet)})\right|$.
<!-- end proof-92 -->
